product_title: Jean Patou Joy Eau de Parfum Spray, 1.6 Fl Oz
review_text:
This is a new formula, but made in France, not the UK.  To me it smells more like old Joy than the UK-reformulated version did.  I suspect it's not possible to get all the ingredients for old Joy anymore--perhaps there were animal ingredients not produced today, for example.  There is an ingredient list on the box now that includes several lab-created scent molecules that were certainly not available when Joy was first blended.

I've been wearing Joy since the 1970's when my mother gave me a sample.  The UK-made version a few years back was Sooooo disappointing we searched high and low for vintage Joy and found some, but then no more.  I decided to try this version before my old supply runs out, as several reviewers said it was at least made in France, which it is.

When I compare the versions, the initial scent of this version is heavier on the jasmine than the rose of old Joy, but as it dries off the rose asserts itself as well, of course with many other intriguing notes that still say "Joy" to me, where the spicier and muskier UK version did not.  So far, I think this one does not last as well as the old Joy, but it is at least close to my favorite scent of all time, so I am happy with it.

product_title: Michel Germain Sexual Pour Homme Eau de Toilette Spray, 4.2 fl. oz.
review_text:
This isn't so much a review of the product itself, as it isn't at all what I thought I was getting. I failed to do my homework and was looking for a different fragrance in the same line called Sexual Secret (a co-worker used it and I just had to know what it was!) Well what I didn't realize is that the item on this page is a different product entirely. Mostly my fault, but the pictures...

3 out of 4 of the product pictures clearly show Sexual Secret by Michael Germain, which as I now know, is not the same thing as this. I also didn't realize they were customer images, but trusted that Amazon would have it's stuff together and wouldn't allow pictures of different products. or that at least by now the images would have been flagged and removed if they were incorrect.

It's my fault for not researching more, but for how much Amazon is trying to make it easy for you to impulse buy everything ever, with one-click and pay phrases and an intelligent behavior tracking heuristic, they really don't try very hard to ensure accurate descriptions of their products. The long and the short of it is that I bought this product because I trusted that what I saw in the picture was what I was getting. I was wrong.

Amazon: Please vet customer images more carefully, or allow a flagging system to allow the community to do it for you (all I saw was a flag for abuse).

product_title: Jean Patou Joy Eau de Parfum Spray, 1.6 Fl Oz
review_text:
I've loved Joy since my teens (I'm in my mid 40s now). At that time, my mother was an employee of Higbees department store. She had an employee discount card for 25% off, and on one day a year employees could combine it with an additional 25% off. And that's when I discovered Joy. One day a year Mom would buy me a new bottle. Sadly, even the upscale department stores in town no longer carry Joy.

Its key scents are rose and jasmine - classic and never out of style. This scent is fresh, attractive, and not overpowering like my mother's signature scent, Youth Dew.  I love Youth Dew, but cannot wear it in warm weather or spray it liberally. Joy, on the other hand, is never clingy or overpowering on me. I love it so much that I purchased a Joy smell-alike massage oil from a business I see at a yearly festival I attend.

A word of warning about the purchase of expensive perfumes from online, though. I see Amazon is both the seller and shipper here. That's good news. Amazon is not going to sell counterfeits. They're a powerhouse seller with a reputation to uphold. Beware purchases on eBay or no name sites or companies. Scammers go to a great deal of trouble to create look alike packaging for their fake scents. I also assumed that buying used older bottles would be a way to save money, but it turns out they'll even partially fill real, used bottles with the fake stuff. I got burned on the second bottle of Joy I bought at one of those sites, but next bottle I buy will be from Amazon! Look it up online, and you'll be shocked at the sites showing the minute differences between a real bottle and a fake one.

review_title: EAU JOY! It's the real thing!
review_text: I was afraid that this would be another disappointment -- that it would be diluted or counterfeit. I should have had more faith in Amazon. Amazon.com has restored two of the fragrances I wore in my youth, both of which are sensational and evoke wonderful memories for me. Joy, with its inimitable bouquet of rose and precious jasmine, is one of those. Jean de Patou stopped making this incredible scent years ago, and I was thrilled to find it on Amazon. I had thought this was a hopeless cause -- that I would never be able to wear this fragrance again or find anything close to it. Fragrances today are so light they disappear within seconds of application -- a waste of money and time. The House of Jean Patou was the grand old master of the perfume world, creating fragrances that would last with a single spritz, would not be heavy or intrusive, and smell like . . . flowers. A good thing. Thanks to Amazon for carrying this endangered species.

product_title: Lacoste Booster Eau de Toilette for Men
review_text: I disregarded the bad reviews, figured for the price why not try it. Here's why, it's definitely a good air freshener. Sure it has a menthol + eucalyptus smell and has some qualities I guess some people might like so if that's your thing by all means, this might suite you well. This might make a good lotion, soap, air freshener, etc. Even if you're looking for a light breezy cool cologne for the Summer this doesn't work imo. There's definitely fresher & more pleasant scents available. I'll use my bottle as an air freshener in the bedroom and bathroom until it's gone. Needless to say, do yourself a favor and go check this one out before buying it or if it's a gift pick another fragrance.

review_text:
I purchased this as a birthday gift for my wife, who loves Red Door. I ordered the Eau de Parfum 1.7 oz. but got a bottle of Eau de Toilette instead.  I couldn't return it so I ordered the Parfum directly from Elizabeth Arden website at full price.  I don't think what I got from the Amazon retailer was the real stuff anyway. Since placing the original order with Amazon the name of the retailer has changed about 3 times! The receipt listed someone totally different from the Amazon retailer listed!  I always found my way back to this item by clicking on the Items Ordered link in my purchase history, so there should be no mistake that I found different retailers due to random searches.

Based on other bad reviews I've read for this item I'm just going to throw it away.  What a real waste of money!  I was lucky I ordered early enough to get the real thing from Elizabeth Arden in time for my wife's birthday!!!  This purchase was from a scammer, for sure.  I'm angry at Amazon for not policing their retailers better and not offering a way to compensate me.  I've ordered from Amazon plenty of times before successfully, but this has made me wary of purchasing items from their third-party retailers!

review_text: Perfumes never smell good on me, but I get compliments galore when I wear Lacoste Pour Femme. It doesn't have that "heavy", "overpowering" smell that so many of today's perfumes have. It's classified as a "floral", yet I wouldn't call it that at all. Most florals are sweet and give me a headache. It's neither spicey, nor flowery, nor powdery. It's very clean smelling and light, yet has a very warm and romantic side. This perfume has a scent unlike any other I know. It's sexy, yet extremely understated. It's delicate enough to wear during the day or in the office and alluring enough to wear at night. The only complaint I would have is that it doesn't last as long as stronger perfumes. However, the beauty of this perfume far outways the need for a second application in the evening. My husband loves when I wear it and I can never find another scent I like when I run out. This perfume has been a top seller at Sephora for years for reason. I've purchased this perfume from Amazon and Sephora and found them to be identical in scent and longevity. I suggest mixing this product with an unscented lotion to further extend the aroma (it's a much cheaper alternative to purchasing Aquolina's scented body lotion).

review_text:
I think this is the first time I have used a fragrance product where I thought the name was an excellent description of the scent.  I smell this and it really does remind me of pink cotton candy (maybe with a hint of caramel).

I'm not sure if this is an everyday scent for me, but I do like it.  It's fun and different from a lot of the other fragrances I've tried lately.  I think it also might appeal to (much) younger people.

It smells pretty similar on to how it smells in the tube (though your body chemistry may vary).  It lasts about half a day for me and even if I wear a lot, it's not too strong.  Glad I got a chance to try it. (Because the scent is a little different, it may be worth getting a sample from somewhere before committing to an entire bottle.)

review_title: Pink Sugar does not say 'Aquolina'; smells good though
review_text:
A salesperson in a perfume store recommended Pink Sugar to me recently because I told her I like Prada Candy and other sweet smells.
When I looked up the product on Amazon I read many reviews and a lot of people seemed to be wondering/questioning if Amazon sells the original product.
The bottle I received says Pink Sugar on it and on the bottom of it says the manufacturer is 'Selectiva S.p.a'  Made in Italy. Does not say 'Aquolina' anywhere.
If you go to Sephora or Nordstrom Rack, it will be the same one by Selectiva Spa. I guessed they changed it. I never smelled it when it came out in 2004, so I won't know the difference, if any.
However, Amazon should update details so there is no confusion for perfume fans out there.
I liked this perfume when I smelled testers in stores and I am content. The only negative here is that the bottle was stuck inside the tube it came in and I had to cut it open, thus ruining the pink and white swirl container. Other than that, the perfume is exactly what I tested in Sephora and $40 cheaper.

review_title: Aqualina Pink Sugar (new product does not have the pepper, so don't panic and assume it's fake)
review_text:
I read a lot of reviews before getting this product and I was really scared, but took a risk because I TRUST Amazon and their guarantees.

I read that many of you here have received fakes. I cannot speak for the vendors here and I'm positive that you can get a fake by easily buying a cheaper item, and not buying it from Amazon DIRECTLY. Yes, it's a tad more pricey, but I'm confident I got the real thing...

1. Make sure your product is SOLD BY and SHIPPED by AMAZON only.

2. There is no chili pepper on the PINK SUGAR products...(see their official facebook page and website page, (both in Italian) The confusing element of this product is that most of their older bottles of pink sugar, had the pepper on their logo, just as their other products do now...However, it appears to be one of the few products that don't have iconic pepper now)... (yes, i realize that in itself may sound confusing).

3. The official website link is pinksugar(dot)(i t) with no spaces and no parenthesis.

4. The package itself has a "velvety" like pink ribbon around the cardboard container.

5. The bar code should be written on the BOTTOM of the cardboard/plastic container, and reads 8 033866 164335. (for the 3.5 oz. Eau de Toilette)

6. The company's website is listed in tiny print, on the bottom label of the cardboard/plastic container and is : selective(dash) spa(dot)(it). On that page, you can see all the company products along with a link to the pink sugar product line. There are new Pink sugar products that came out in 2012 as well...

7. The container and bottle itself are both stamped "made in Italy".

I hope this helps someone out there...as I started to panic when I first opened the box and saw no "pepper" like others had mentioned... After doing some research online, I discovered that it's suppose to be like this...

I waited a long time to buy this perfume, because of the fears everybody talked about, but now I am glad that I finally bought this and realize that it's not AMAZON selling fakes at all...(beware of vendors or personal sellers though, which may not be the same stuff).

review_text:
This cologne was sent to me in the wrong formulation, so I ended up getting the higher priced EDP for the price of the EDT (About a $10-$15 difference). I clearly ordered the EDT as it's the formulation that shows up in my review section as a verified purchase. I have used Jaipur EDT before and always liked the light, airy quality of it. I had also smelled the EDP before and there's no way I would have ordered the EDP since it has heliotrope in it and I really don't like the heliotrope scent at all.

I'll stick with a 3 star since I hadn't bought my brother-in-law for the holidays and just gifted him the EDP bottle. For those interested in Jaipur EDT, it's a very dynamic cologne. It first goes on as a cinnamon/powdery "power" scent that eventually becomes light and airy with a few mild flowers like carnations. I would recommend the EDT to all those who work in closed spaces like offices. The initial top notes are a bit strong, but once it settles in it's a very nice, non-offensive scent with strong lasting power (upwards of 10 hours on clothes). As for the EDP, if you don't mind heliotrope, you might like it, but the heliotrope reminds me of all the mornings I spent as a kid in my grandmother's beauty salon. All of the ritzy, older women wore perfumes ripe with heliotrope and I've never liked the scent since.

review_title: Indo-French Pastry with Too Much Powder On It
review_text:
Fragrance starts with a vanilla / cardamom top note, that quickly turns powdery in scent. Did not get any florals in here, save for fleeting carnation in the first couple minutes of top notes. The odor is not really gourmand in sensibility (it is too powdery and artificial) so you smell rather like the potpourri in a patisserie rather than anything you might order there. To my nose, the fragrance feels rather inert and synthetic, and the evolution over time is not really interesting. After about 4 hours or so, the cardamom goes away altogether, and you are left with a lighter more subtle powdery vanilla that smells like a men's barbershop. This scent is by no means awful, but to me it is static and dull, suggesting lap dogs and overwrought pastries at first and then eventually a rather inexpensive oriental fragrance that is not in the least exotic. I like these odor ingredients used differently elsewhere (e.g. Black or Declaration) but Jaipur For Men does not hold much olfactory interest to me, and unless you want to present yourself as an inertly decorous maharajah to the world at large, you would be better advised to try something less pretty and more lively. Even the very "tasty" A*Men holds more interest and challenge over time, and the dry down of A*Men certainly is not routine...

That said, this is a well formatted fragrance with high quality ingredients, and you, the buyer, might very well like to smell like a pampered Subcontinental nobleman. I would probably have given this four stars for quality of the scent, especially at the current great price point, but I took a star off because this EDT (alone out of the 15 or so I have used) turns my skin a bright fiery red wherever it is sprayed onto, and the redness lasts for about 15 minutes. There is no pain or discomfort, just a redness, but it's obvious something in here does not agree with me. This relatively minor issue combines with my essential distaste for the scent to make this one likely to be shoved all the way to the back of the medicine cabinet.

review_text: In selecting a personal fragrance, I believe one should wear it for a time. A department store counter is not necessarily the place to make a decision. My suggestion is to apply a small amount and let it warm and mature on you. In some instances an aftershave will be more to your liking than a cologne or vice-verse. Wear it for a few hours and then make your decision. Do not allow a fragrance to overpower you or those around you. It should be part of you and who you are. And never allow a department store clerk to make a decision for you. Remember, their job is to sell you something...anything. Look for subtlety, not sharpness, That is of course unless you like a sharper, more direct scent. Again, all very personal. I found Boucheron to be just what I wanted.

review_text:
I ordered directly from L'Occitane (Amazon not involved in this transaction but posting here to give a heads up to others) for my last verbena order.  This is so NOT the original L'Occitane's lemon verbena or the citrus verbena of old, in my opinion.  I have some lemon verbena from L'Occitane left from a few years ago (stored in a cool dark place) and it still smells absolutely wonderful!  However, I recently ordered lemon verbena again directly from L'Occitane and it was COMPLETELY different. Blech!  I then ordered the citrus verbena, thinking perhaps that might be better.  Had some of that, too, years ago from L'Occiatne.  No better.  In my opinion, they have CHANGED the formulas on BOTH, and in speaking with them recently, I find that they have in fact changed the formulas - at least for the lemon verbena.  It now has a harsh bottom note and it's NOT the lemon verbena they offered a few years ago.  Not at all. In fact, their entire line seems to have changed in my opinion and I don't know why they had to go and ruin a good thing.  Their lemon verbena of old was the BEST on the market in my opinion, and now, well, blech!

The colognes I mentioned above just don't smell smell the same and leaves a weird "after note."  I returned both to L'Occitane, but again, they are not very forthcoming about their return policy.

I realized today that I don't play fair. I depend quite often on reviews when I shop online. The more specific and detailed the better. So many people leave extremely helpful reviews. I need to help others as others help me. So here I go!
I think, to understand why I love this brand so much, and this scent as my personal go to daytime favorite, I have to give you some details about me. I am 50 years old, my life is very complicated, and I have two very different businesses. I am a Professional Animal Behaviorist & Dog Trainer. I do a lot of charity work with abused animals. I am also a Pro Makeup Artist and Aesthetician, and I still do hair as well. Most of my time anymore is donated to time at women's shelters, teaching how to take care of skin and how to apply makeup for job interviews. I enjoy doing bridal & bridesmaid makeup and hair. My hubby is an attorney in the corporate sector, and there are certain social obligations there.

SO! I cannot go around working with women on their faces and their hair smelling like dogs, and the opposite is even more true: can't work with abused high risk dogs while smelling complicated and chemical. There are several perfumes that I love dearly, and only wear when I'm not working, or when I'm going out in the evening. Some of those are...Flower Bombe, Amarige, Fendi (old and new), Romance, and for daytime I love 8 by Abercrombie and Fitch. All florientals, most have patchouli and/or musk as a base note.

We all know that perfumes are complicated things, and what smells wonderful on you will also smell awful on someone else. Chalk that up to body chemistry and individual olfactory triggers. In other words, "The nose knows!" Why I mention the perfumes I love is because I know that when I bathe and moisturize with L'Occitane Verbena bath and body products, any of those perfumes go very well with the lemony scent. This is one of those very simple and pure scents that doesn't compete with other perfumes you might choose to wear over the layers of this scent if you use the bath and body products as well as the scent itself. To me, and on me when it's dried down, this smells softly of fresh lemons with a touch of sunshine, just like the verbena plant. That doesn't mean it will smell that way on everyone.
What I suggest, if you're interested but hesitant to buy the bottle before you even smell it or apply it, is to look at all of the products in this line, and perhaps choose one that's less expensive to try. I can guarantee that regardless of the scent, their body products are deeply moisturizing and feel wonderful going on. They melt right into your skin, without a greasy residue feeling. The upside is whether you like the scent on yourself or not, you'll still have nicely moisturized skin, which at my age is essential even though I don't have particularly dry skin, I do have time and gravity to contend with. Free radicals don't care who they stick to!
If you love the gentle scent of lemon, and single note perfumes and body sprays, this one is for you! If you enjoy the clean smells that come from other product lines, like Philosophy's fresh and simple scents that are clean and not flowery or powdery smelling at all, you'll probably like this. There are several brands of bath and body care that I recommend to women that don't cost a designer fortune, and L'Occitane is one of them.
For me, I was just jumping for joy inside when I found this! Many years ago I got hooked on a body spray called Lemon Verbena. They discontinued it, and I felt like I'd just lost a dear friend. Apparently, that dear friend's name is now L'Occitane! I love to layer the shower gel, the body scrub, the cream and the lotion and the body spray. They even have body towelettes in a resealable package, which are for me, for all those reasons I listed above, a much loved necessity, and I carry a pack with me in my purse everywhere!  I use them so often on my arms, my neck and dcollet! They don't just smell wonderful, they feel wonderful too. No dry or tight feeling left behind. L'Occitane Verbena is my special miracle, and I hope they never discontinue this simple, fresh, citrusy, lemony line. If you have ever smelled a verbena plant, then you already know what's inside this bottle!

review_title: Refreshing scent, lots of "what is that wonderful smell" as people look around
review_text: I first found this scent when I had a job that required me to travel a great deal, moving from city to city every day over 10 day stints. When you are on the go from sunrise until midnight with little time to freshen up, this clean, fresh scent is a wonderful pick me up. The best thing about this scent, though, is that often I find people looking around trying to figure out what smells so great until they realize it's me. It is such a light, refreshing fragrance that no one expects what they are smelling to be perfume -- rather, they look for something growing nearby. Of course, I do live in a region with lots of citrus trees and verbena, which also explains why folks look around for what's growing or blooming. It does wear off rather quickly, but the 20 ml size is perfect for a handbag, and it's a light enough scent that you won't overpower anyone's nose if you spritz in the bathroom and walk directly back to other people like, for example, at a dinner table.

review_text:
This is a strange one.  It is quite fruity & sweet - pomegranate is the main fruit here.  But even with that sweet fruit it has a very sharp top note which makes it a bit unisex.  It smells a bit "male" & then morphs in to wood, spice & musk.  Very little flower although there is some slightly powdery, synthetic orchid note in the drydown.

This has been reformulated so it is a bit different than the original 2005 version.  Personally, I do not think it is as good or interesting as it used to be.  This one is very moody depending on your skin - more so than a lot of perfumes, IMO.  On some people, this goes to a funky, spoiled fruit smell & on others, it's a seductive wood with sweet, ripe fruit & very "sexy".

Spray this lightly, it is very big & will easily offend others.  This lasts until the next day on my skin.

review_title: Boucheron Pour Homme Eau De Parfum
review_text:
Boucheron has long been known for their elegance, style, and unique vision which they seem to effortlessly put into all of their products.
For me, I fell in love with Jaipur, Boucheron's most recent fragrance, which in and of itself I find to be one of my all time favorites. However, Boucheron pour Homme presents a tale of refinement, re-interpreting citrus and wood notes to depict a quiet evening bathed in the emerging twilight: a stroll under a just starring Mediterranean sky, where lemon groves waft their fresh aroma from a distance and aromatic herbs are crushed underfoot. A traditional and romantic scent for a distinguished and elegant man, its charismatic presence is palpably felt. Don Draper of "Mad Men" would carry this one effortlessly...
Okay heres the deal on the fragrance,
Top Note: Orange, Lavender, Mandarin Orange, Basil, Lemon Verbena, Bergamot, Lemon Middle Note: Carnation, Orris Root, Jasmine, Ylang-Ylang, Lily-Of-The-Valley, Rose; Base Note: Sandalwood, Tonka Bean, Amber, Musk, Benzoin, Oakmoss, Vetiver, Incense.
It was only yesterday, after sampling Boucheron's Pour Homme Parfum for men, did I feel that the Jaipur which I love so adamantly, had only possibly met it's match.
 The bottle I saw at Macy's yesterday was selling for $125.00 3.3 fl. oz, 100 ml E. I ordered the exact same bottle from Amazon at 2:15 yesterday afternoon for $53.00, with no shipping fee, it was at my door by 9:15 this morning, less than 24 hours from the time of purchase, to having right here on my table, what more can I say, possibly the finest of all mens perfumes, delivered in absolute record time at a price which absolutely no one could possibly touch.
I don't think you can beat that, do have a look at Boucheron's Pour Homme, I believe it to be among the finest mens fragrance I've ever come across.

product_title: Lacoste Essential Eau de Toilette for Men
review_text: I got this for my then fiance who HATES strong scents.  In the past I've purchased Burberry for him and he doesn't wear it.  He threw out the Armani scents because they were too strong.  It is a challenge to find him anything he will wear other than Clinque Happy for Men.  I was looking to buy him a wedding scent, something he doesn't usually wear, and went to Nordstrom's.  Every scent the saleslady offered was too strong, too woodsy, too musky, too everything my husband can't stand.  Then she sprayed this scent and I knew it was the one.  It is very light and simple, not in the least bit overpowering, and he loves it.  Now he wears it daily, even on the weekends!  It has some "time release" system that does somehow work, because the scent still smells good in the late evening, despite putting it on early in the am.  The main notes are tangerine, bergamot, tomato leaves, cassis, black pepper, rose, patchouli, sandalwood and wood accord.  I know that sounds like a weird combination, but it works!  This is a great scent for a guy who doesn't want to overpower the room, but wants to smell good all day.

product_title: Lacoste Essential Eau de Toilette for Men
review_text:
Strong scents, the one criteria alone that can make me avoid certain colognes. I prefer to wear a cologne that will make me smell good, but not overpower so much that it will make people around me uncomfortable. I live in NYC  and everyday I use public transportation to go to school and work. I work in retail and I am very social in college, so it's safe to say I am always around people. I like to manage myself to be presentable, so I always love wearing cologne. One day I was shopping with my mom at Macy's, and we came across the Perfume/cologne section. While my mom was being bothered by five different salesman trying to make a sale, I decided to walk over to the men's section and smell some new colognes. Now prior to this, I have had no experience with Lacoste scents. For some odd reason, I decided to walk over and smell the Lacoste scents that were being offered. While other customers were trying out the different scents, I picked up the Lacoste essential and sprayed it on myself without having any idea what I was going to get. To my surprise, it was a beautiful summer smell, kind of soft but very manly. My favorite part was, as you can guess already is that it wasn't a strong smell. However, I did not purchase it at that moment and I will tell you why. Department stores such as Macy's charge way higher than you can get elsewhere. Especially, in my case because my dad has worked with perfumes/colognes most of his life. He is a distributor for the ingredients needed to make perfume/colognes for many companies. Since he knew a lot of sellers, I told him about the Lacoste essential and he acquired it for me for a much cheaper price. Now, the duration of the cologne is mind boggling. Keep in mind I leave everyday for college at 7AM in the morning, and by the time I come back home from work afterwards, its around 11PM. It's amazing how even after 15 hours you can still catch the scent from my shirt, considering I usually put on two sprays at most. My girlfriend likes wearing my sweater sometimes because of the cologne scent still lingering on it. Of course I have many other colognes but this is by far my favorite go to scent. This product is wonderful and I am glad that day at Macy's I decided to walk over to the Lacoste section to give this item a try.

Hopefully my review helped make your decision! Please let me know if you have any comments or questions, thanks for reading!

Even better, it is very long lasting, due to ingredients (like black pepper) that are heat activated. The top note is fresh and citrusy, with a woodsy middle, and very subtle musk undertones. review_title: Amazing light, summery scent, with even more amazing, but lesser known technology built into it.
review_text:
Lacoste Essential is an amazing scent. I have recieved quite a few compliments regarding this fragrance, the main tone of this cologne (haha, that rhymes..) is because one of the main ingredients is pepper (seriously). After the main, spicy tone, it fades off into a light-semi citrus end-note.
The cologne is perfect for spring into summer time, especially when you sweat. Why when you sweat? Lacoste Essential is probably one of the ONLY colognes in the world that uses a technology (forgive me, the name escapes me) in which it reactivates itself when body temperature goes up. It has a life of about 3-5 hours before it begins to fade, however, say you use this cologne, and after a few hours, begin to sweat, or get heated up by any event, the cologne will re-activate and the scent will return like it was sprayed not too long ago. Works GREAT for athletes or for those who work outside, even the nervous types will find this technology very useful. Don't forget, the scent of any cologne is amplified by each person's individual scent! I would definatley recommend this.

product_title: Billy Jealousy ILLICIT Eau de Perfume, 3.4 fl. oz.
review_text:
Billy Jealousy makes great products. It's that simple. I've been a fan of BJ's (hehe, sorry couldn't resist) for some time now. I can't imagine shaving or washing my face with anything else.

However, when it comes to cologne I am very picky. I am not the kind of guy who has a cabinet full of dusty old bottles that I like to rotate. Instead, I prefer a nice "signature scent" that smells great and is unique enough that you don't smell it on everyone else.

I recently discovered that my old favorite brand of cologne, Dolce and Gabbana tests on animals. And since I personally not believe a beagle needs to be forced to drink cologne, or a cat needs to have it rubbed in their eyes, I threw out my bottles and sent a nasty letter to Proctor and Gamble (makers of D&G fragrances.) Unfortunately, this meant I needed to find a new smell.

I've been wanting to smell this product for some time, but living in Northern New England I was unable to locate it in a store. And the online retailers that I purchase from never seem to offer it as a checkout sample. So I traded some emails back and forth with the company's president (yes really, very responsive company) I decided to just go for it and buy it. The scent finally arrived and I could tell from the very first spray, this was for me. It's clean and fresh. It reminds me a nice summer vacation day. I've been wearing it every morning since. My wife is a fan too, except one minor problem. I commented to her recently that I noticed a couple female co-workers kind of sitting extra close to me in meetings and sort of leaning into me in hopes of smelling it. It's definitely intoxicating and the sort of smell you want to smell ever more. The design is simple and includes a few crisp notes like bergamot citrus, ivy, ginger accord, nutmeg and sandalwood. I would classify this as a fresh, green-citrus fragrance. While some scent experts might call this a summer/daytime scent, I plan on using it for everything since I personally thing that heavy oak/wood scents are a bit too grandpa and going way of of the doe-doe bird.

In short, another great Billy Jealousy hit. My next purchase is an small travel atomizer so I can have this scent in my travel bag for work.

My profile (since this is important in reading scent reviews) - A 32 year old, married, Supply Chain/Operations Manager for a billion dollar BioTech corporation. I typically like fresh scents and men's products from hip and trendy companies that do not test on animals.

review_text:
I have worn Michael Kors original "Michael" for years because I love wearing a mild, fresh, and clean smelling perfume. I tried several times to switch things up a bit and spent way too much time in department stores smelling and sampling suggested fragrances...although I did purchase new fragrances (and use them until they ran out) I always went back to Michael.

In a fragrance rut, I decided to visit online "perfume forums." I took down the names of fragrances others recommended as "clean" smelling scents. Clean Ultimate was one of these....one sniff of a sample of Clean and I knew I had found my new signature scent. It's the kind of scent that suggests you've just stepped out of the shower after using an expensive designer soap. You enter the room before the aroma of CLEAN does...which is a good thing, right? People will have to be near you to smell this fragrance and you'll notice they want to linger because you so smell so good.

Base Notes: Creamy Musks, Peach Skin, Amber Droplet

review_text:
CLEAN Fresh Laundry is a nice fruity-floral scent.

I've tried a couple of the CLEAN scents and I really like them because they are refreshingly different from other perfumes I buy.

CLEAN Fresh Laundry has a fruity-floral scent that I enjoy and I feel like CLEAN Warm Cotton smells more like my laundry than CLEAN Fresh Laundry dose.  That could be because I don't use overly perfumed laundry detergent.

There's a nice zing to this scent which has top notes of Brazilian Orange, Mexican Lime, and Fresh Mown Grass.  (I don't smell the grass, but there is definitely a hit of citrus!)  Mid-notes are Rose Otto and Night Blooming Jasmine, which definitely come through in the floral scent.  And the base notes are Heliotrope and Woody Musk.  Personally, I get no musk scent from this perfume at all.

The CLEAN scents I've tried are definitely a departure from my other fragrances and something that I can wear every day.  Fresh Laundry is a very pretty scent that I'm enjoying right now.

product_title: Juicy Couture Women's Perfume
review_text: This is my 'special occasions' perfume.  I'm probably the pickiest perfume picker (tongue twister?) ever but I LOVE the scent of this.  I could sniff it all day.  It's not too strong, but it smells amazing and lasts all day.  I usually do a spritz on my neck and wrists, and I can always smell it at the end of the day, even if I wear it to school have gym.  Also, it lasts soooo long!  I got my current bottle Christmas 2009 and I still have a little more than half left.  Plus, the bottle and packaging is really pretty!  If this is too expensive for you (even though it's totally worth it), you can get the travel roll on one for about $15 at most department stores and Sephora.  It works just as well.  The other Juicy perfumes are a little too strong and sweet for me, as most perfumes are, but this one is PERFECT.  I think it's great for women in their teens to 20s.

review_title: Men LOVE it (and so do I)
review_text:
I have had this perfume for a month, and its been quite interesting!

I have always worn perfume, but this is something I have never experienced before. Of course, I have had a date, or my husband tell me I smell nice, and a friend here or there tell me they like my perfume...but never like a random stranger guy.
I have had this perfume for only a month, and I have been complimented on this perfume 3 times from 3 Men, of various ages, all complete strangers, who had to tell me how good I smell. One gentleman was riding me in the elevator and asked men what perfume I was wearing YESTERDAY, as in he remembered smelling it on me from the prior day and just had to ask and tell me how much he liked it the next day!

All that aside, since I am not wearing it to impress men (I am a happily married woman). I love this fragrance, its so light and soft. Not over powering at all (unless you put too much, only a little on your hot spots is needed ladies!). Its a nice mixture of floral/fruity, so you can't really pin point which one it is.

I highly recomend this perfume (I found it cheapest at Marshalls BTW), I will definitely be wearing it for a long time. And if you so happen to be looking for a scent that men seem to love. This is it :D

review_title: The perfume of an anti-perfume girl
review_text: My boyfriend's mother gave me the Juicy Couture lotion as a gift.  I loved the smell, but the lotion dried out my already dry skin.  To my surprise, the next year my boyfriend gave me the Juicy Couture perfume.  I didn't even realize it existed!  As you can probably tell, I have never been very interested in perfume.  Since then, my boyfriend and his mom have given me plenty of other perfumes to try (she is manager of a makeup store).  Nevertheless, Juicy Couture is the only one I like and the only one I wear.  I guess I have good taste because I've been complimented on it by various people on pretty much a monthly basis.  I seem to have gotten my sisters hooked on it, too.  Over the past two years or so since I started wearing Juicy Couture perfume, I've gone through several bottles of it and am hoping to receive another bottle this Christmas.  I strongly recommend Juicy Couture perfume for those who are hesitant about wearing perfume, unsure of which perfume to buy, and those who consider themselves perfume experts, too.  It has a subtle, pretty smell perfect for just about any occasion.  Best of luck!

This one has notes of floral and citrus (for me the floral stands out above the citrus but both are present) and once applied leaves a nice layer of fragrance that outlasts my typical body sprays. First, Im impressed with the bottle that belies its quite affordable price. The multi-faceted vintage glass look prepared me for quality contents. product_title: Laura by Laura Biagiotti Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text: This perfume smells like cheap (and strong) shampoo or highly fragrant dryer sheets. I sprayed some on a piece of blotter paper, recoiled at the onslaught of aroma chemicals, and then put it back in the box. About a half an hour later, I saw a friend who knows I love (and collect) perfume. She commented, "You smell like cheap perfume!" What she was smelling was merely a few scent molecules that had wafted off the paper and "stuck" to my clothes. This supposedly "soft feminine" fragrance is one of the reasons perfumes are increasingly banned in public places. This fragrance was popular in the '90s; perhaps it's been reformulated. Perhaps not. Either way, this iteration is simply awful to my nose.

product_title: Laura by Laura Biagiotti Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text:
Love fragrance and have collected quite a few over the years.  This one, starting with the extremely old school (and old lady) packaging, failed to impress on every possible level.  Not even one ounce in the extremely bland looking bottle.  And it doesn't even look full!  Fragrance is pleasant but offers no OOMPH whatsoever.  Very mild in strength and barely lingers.  A combination of greens and fruit that has been done so much better elsewhere.

Even as a woman of a certain age, I scratch my head and ask who is the target customer for this?  Everything about this eau de toilette is such a THROWBACK (from 1994 actually),  but not in a good way.  VERY conservative and very underwhelming.

Never heard of Laura Biagiotti before.  And now I know why.

product_title: Laura by Laura Biagiotti Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text:
This is a very 1990's scent (created in 1994).  It was the early days of the frooty tooty, flower explosion.  This is a scent I wore for a very short time in the late 1990's - I quickly tired & grew out of it.  I recently smelled it on my teenage niece & it took me back in time - I knew this scent immediately.

There is a lot going on.  Begins & ends with watermelon & peach, freesia, violet, lily of the valley then on to woody notes, musk, cedar & watery green notes.  Somehow, this kind of works but it is not for me anymore.  This is a young girl/young woman fragrance - a more sophisticated young girl than the "Fancy" wearing girls but still, young.  It is not overly cloying sweet but still fruity sweet.  The fruit is not terribly fake but it is definitely not sophisticated either.

Has moderate sillage - I could smell it on my niece when I was next to her.  It is not a really long lasting fragrance - when I tried her bottle, it lasted more than 3 hours on my skin.  This was a trip back in time for me but one I will happily leave behind.  But I do enjoy smelling it on my niece - this would be a good gift for a young girl/woman.

review_text:
Before trying "Laura," the only two perfumes I liked that didn't also "turn" on me were Juicy Couture "Couture Couture," and Vera Wang "Princess." Now there is Laura Biagiotti "Laura." All three have something in common: fruity scents. Couture is fruity and woodsy and Princess is fruity and musky. Couture and Laura have amber, vanilla and sandalwood in common.

Laura is very fruity at first -- I smell watermelon and peach. On me, these soon dissipate, leaving something a little darker, yet still appealing -- violet and sandalwood. Other scents that are in there, but not detected by me are lychee, freesia, iris, vanilla, vetiver, amber and musk. (Vetiver -- new to me -- is a grass, known as khus in India.)

I opened the package and started spraying it all over myself. My husband came in and said, "It smells good in here!"

Pretty blue box suggestive of water (aquatic is one of a balanced blend of notes in Laura, along with fruity, floral and woody and others). Lovely glass tear-drop bottle with blue water drop on top.

product_title: Laura by Laura Biagiotti Eau de Toilette for Women
review_title: Reformulated to new EU standards; similar but different to original 90's scent
review_text:
This is a beautiful bottle reminiscent of Halston's bottle by Elsa Peretti.  The scent itself is a classic 90's fruity floral.  The top notes are peach and lychee over middle notes of freesia and iris held down by a base of amber, sandlewood and vanilla.

This is the new formulation after this classic fragrance (originally launched 1994) was reformulated in response to new EU regulations regarding potential allergens in scents and perfumes.  Sadly many natural essential ingredients are now banned and these reformulations are often pale (artificial) shadows of their former glory.  This particular scent is no exception.  It does not seem to have the staying power of the original and seems slightly more dry-floral overall when compared to remnants/dregs in an older bottle.

My advice for fans of the original version of any fragrance is to try it on at a department store to decide if you are still in love with it in its new reincarnation before committing to a purchase.

review_title: An Underappreciated Classic. Much Higher Quality Than the Price Indicates
review_text: This is one of my two current favorite scents for daily wear. The other is Cerruti 1881. [Update, this is now part of a 3 product rotation with Cerruti 1881 and Guerlain's Vetiver] Today the more modern Azzaro Chrome is more popular, but even though this scent has been around longer than I have, its the version I prefer. Sellers tend to call this "A spicy lavender amber fragrance", and Amazon says it contains "Wood, Musk, Basil. and Sandalwood", but neither of these matches Azzaro's description. According to them, the notes are "Lemon, Star Anise, Basil, Vetiver, and Oakmoss". IMO the Vetiver is the key to this fragrance and whether or not you will like it. I've seen complaints about a "dirty", "foul", or "musky" note and that's the Vetiver, which is obvious as soon as you spray. Personally, I didn't find it THAT objectionable, but it did seem a little discordant (or more specifically a little bit earthy) to me the first two times I wore it. By the third time I was used to the Vetiver, and I fell in love with Azzaro for men. It's got a wonderful drydown, the perfect combination of strength, projection, longevity, and subtlety. This is always noticeable, and lasts all day, yet in my experience it will not overwhelm the people around you. 3-4 sprays will typically last me well over 12 hours. Who is this for? Anyone who doesn't mind the Vetiver punch up front and who wants a classic, classy, super high quality, perfectly executed fougere style cologne. This amounts to a slam-dunk for me personally. It's not mysterious, to me it says "barbershop" "gentleman" and "I'm well groomed yet I don't smell anything like a chick" all at once. This is as near as I've found to a universal cologne for myself.

product_title: Crabtree & Evelyn Eau de Toilette, Nantucket Briar, 2 fl. oz.
review_text:
First, this product is definitely unisex and IMO actually skews masculine more than feminine. The ambergris and woods notes give this a fairly dark and only mildly sweet base, and the rose scent is quite subdued and "green". The overall effect is of a pleasantly floral barbershop type scent, which for me was just perfect. An inexpensive woods / rose mix that is not overly sweet or fake smelling is a great thing, and at this reasonable price point, it is even better. Cabaret by Gres is the closest competitor (in the rose / woods alleged feminine that guys can wear) and Cabaret has a far sweeter and more synthetic smelling rose to it, though Cabaret also is the more complex scent and has better silage and longevity (and is even cheaper!).

Longevity was decent, about 4-6 hours of noticeable proximity effect (about 2-3 feet of projection) and then becomes a skin scent for another 2-4 hours. Silage was moderate, not a room clearing force field. Compared to many other "mall bath and body store" scents, this is pretty impressive. L'Occitan for instance is famous for not inexpensive scents that last an hour or so and then vanish utterly. In comparison, this C&E frag comes close to giving you what the big fragrance companies offer and at a fraction of their price.

What's not to like? Some men do not want to smell like any flowers, ever. This is not for them. Many men and some women do not like powdery smells. This is a little bit powdery, kind of a resinous grassy note mixed in with the powder, and is not overwrought at all. Still, if you loathe powder even in small doses, you may want to try before you buy.

review_text: Perfume is very personal. I prefer scents that are earthy, clean, hints of citrus.  This scent comes out very strong and very rose scented.  I don't like it straight out of the bottle, but I do like it.  My grandmother used rose scented soaps, and this smells like her hands, and I miss her, so I  both love and dislike the initial scent.  The lasting aura is softer, vanilla and rose and ambergris (which reminds me of a Bob's Burgers episode). Perfume is personal, and how a perfume smells on you is personal.  If you enjoy the smell of roses, this might be a real hit with you.  This is not really my scent, but I find myself wearing it regularly because it really does remind me of the soap in my grandmother's home, and I miss her. Scent can take you places, remind you of things, set the tone.  Pick something that is distinctly you.

product_title: Crabtree & Evelyn Eau de Toilette, Nantucket Briar, 2 fl. oz.
review_text:
I wanted to love this. The description sounded just like something Id like and i hoped that the toilette parfum would be light enough to wear to work and not offend anyone. Plus I have used other products from Crabtree and Evelyn and been pleased. Alas, it was not to be. I have a sensitive nose, overly sensitive probably. But this was all kinds of no. No with a capital NUH uh. The was to lavender as banana popsicles are to bananas. I adore a good fresh lavender but this was not a clear astringent lavender, it was a chemical maelstrom of lavender. It has a heavy alcohol top note, which is to be expected with a toilette water but it hung on much longer than I wanted, but the powdery middle note was just odd and it lasted much too long in that middle range of too strong to be two hours old. Then the bottom note is too much Grandmas hankie drawer for me, though it was more in the muted range I expected.

My advice if you want to try it because you like that old fashioned type of scent is to apply it properly- spray into the air and walk through it, never apply directly to the skin. Or try using it as a light room spray or closet spray. I don't want to preach here but gone are the days of women wearing heavy scents into work and getting away with it. So many of us are crammed into more reconditioned air and we all need to be sensitive to the noses of our coworkers. No one wants to be remembered as that strongly stinky person in the office. Your scent should be special to you and to anyone who is close enough to share it in your personal space.

review_title: If You Like Rose, Vanilla, Citrus and Patchouli, You'll Love Nantucket Briar
review_text:
From the female side of the family. I've tried this fragrance and it's not for me -- but at the same time, it is entirely what it claims to be, and that is why I give it 5 stars. There's nothing like a perfume or "eau de toilet" (as this is), to divide the reviews. Some love it -- "my go-to fragrance! 5 stars." Some hate it and give it 1. The thing is, perfume is about the most personal thing you can choose.

Crabtree and Evelyn is a renowned brand, the product comes in an attractive glass bottle with a good quality nozzle, and it delivers exactly what it promises. So if you're wondering if the fragrance is for you, take a look at the ingredients. Do you like sweet rose scent? This is full of it. How about vanilla and citrus? They are strong notes. Then there's patchouli -- it's here. Bergamot is another ingredient: it's what gives the perfume to Earl Gray tea. Then there's ambergris, not necessarily something you can smell, but a rare and expensive oil produced by sperm whales, and a classic ingredient in perfumes (fitting for one named for the whaling town of Nantucket).

Overall, the fragrance smells to me of vanilla and rose. It reminds me of the scent of traditional talcum powder. As I say, it's not my favorite -- but then, it is exactly what Nantucket Briar Eau de Toilet claims to be. You decide!

review_title: Just not my kind of perfume
review_text:
Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette

The description says that "This feminine scent possesses a blend of crisp and fruity resins, evening flowers with base notes of vanilla and musk."

It just smells kind of sweet and heavy for me.  I haven't worn perfume for a long time since so many people are allergic these days and it's discouraged at work. The last perfume I used and loved was Oscar back in the 90s.  So I was excited to get this one and try it out.

I have to say, I don't really like it for myself.  It doesn't smell crisp to me but rather heavy and sweet.  I won't be wearing it but will give it to my Mom (who is 92).  Someone mentioned it's a cologne for mature women.  I'm definitely mature at 66 but it's too heavy for me.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text: Scent is a very personal preference.  I found this eau de toilette overly sweet and flowery...not too distinct from the other perfumes.  I only had 1 spritz in the air and my husband and boys all complained about the "old lady" scent.  If possible, try on some before buying.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text: This is a lovely scent, not very floral but more musky. When first applied, it's more floral but the residual scent after wearing it for several hours is the vanilla musk scent, which I prefer.  It comes in a cool, Roman column-like bottle.  I also like that it seems to be quite concentrated, which means you need just a little so the bottle should last a very long time.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text:
I have learned that few fragrances react well to my body chemistry, so I was careful to use one short spray on the inside of my wrist.  My first reaction was "Different, but nice."  After about five minutes, I decided the heavy vanilla component was becoming sickeningly sweet.  Within ten minutes I was rinsing it off -- I thought -- but the scent remained.  Next, I covered my wrist in liquid hand soap and SCRUBBED.  That was enough to banish the scent -- unless I put my nose to my wrist.  Amazingly, I could still detect a slight trace of it.

Body chemistry and personal taste are too unique to enable one person to objectively criticize or recommend a perfume or cologne.  If you find a heavy, sweet vanilla aroma appealing, this scent is made for you.  Just don't be offended if I don't stay in the same room.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text:
LAURA BIAGIOTTI ROMA EAU de TOILETTE

This cologne smells differently every time I smell it on my wrist.  A little bit goes a long way; it tends to be heavy and over-bearing.  While I like it, I don't like it.  The first time I smelled it the odor of citrus was high, then that citrus odor seemed to disappear, bringing forth flowers, vanilla, and musk.  The vanilla and musk scent I pick up on I do like.  ROMA reminds me of something; then it hit me -- to me, it smells rather like a cologne a man would wear, not for a woman at all.  It has a spicy manly odor.

I love a variety of scents -- some of my favorites include TABU, EMERAUDE, RED DOOR, WHITE DIAMONDS, and Dolce & Gabbana LIGHT BLUE.  I'm thinking ROMA will not fall into the category of one of my favorite colognes.

I love the bottle it is in, a frosted pillar style certainly reminding one of Italy.  I also think the name ROMA reminds me of my favorite tomatoes instead of a women's fragrance.  It is 0.84 ounces in a spray bottle form.

To sum up, for me, this cologne is three star, just OK.  I would certainly not purchase it and probably will have to remind myself to wear it -- very sparingly.

Thank you.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text:
Perfumes, eau de toilettes, powders, etc. are essentially a matter of opinion when it comes to their scent.  For that reason, I feel like the Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette is a bit of a downer as far as I'm concerned.  Why?  For lack of a better description, I'd say that it has an "old lady smell" to it.  To bring a bit of clarity to this description, I suggest trying to remember back to the old lady or grandmother that smelled nice, but wore a perfume that smelled like an old lady would wear it.

This eau de toilette does not stink at all.  It has a pleasant vanilla and musk scent to it, it just doesn't smell like something anybody under the age of sixty might want to wear on their body.  It's a nice fragrance and it lasts a long time, it just smells a bit....dated.

So, if you enjoy dated or "old lady" fragrances, this eau de toilette gets five stars for you.  If you are under the age of sixty, though, you might want to skip this fragrance.

review_title: Nice perfume.  From my male perspective, this is nice.
review_text:
I was given the chance to review this item and I was intrigued.  My wife was the test subject, but I will give my impressions as a male.

First off, I was initially skeptical because I was not familiar with the brand and didn't know what to think.  However, other reviews and the willingness to take a chance made me get this item.

I received the package and the bottle is nicely put together.  The scent is really nice actually.  I noticed the pleasant smell right off.  I would describe the scent as being somewhat fruity, but light.  The scent is not overpowering or 'daring' but it seems rather middle of the road.  After a number of minutes, it fades to a pleasant background.

My wife really liked the perfume straight off, and she is very particular with what she wears.  She describes the scent as being perfect for a daytime/afternoon freshen up kind of scent. As I mentioned it is not a daring scent, so this isn't really a nighttime going out for a date kind of scent. It also appears that this scent is probably more appropriate for a wee bit older person (this isn't teenybopper material).

Overall:  I like smelling this perfume.  My wife is enjoying this new scent and has used it for a number of days already.  This is a nice product.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_title: Very strong and smells like a scent from the '80's
review_text:
Perfumes are hard to review since they react so differently on everyone's body and because we all have such personal preferences.  I really wanted to like this since I love Rome and thought it might bring back nice memories of visiting there, but the smell on this feels really dated to me . . . like something I would have bought back in the 1980's.

I usually love vanilla and musk, but these are so strong that they were really overpowering.  This does have excellent sillage (the "wake" left by a perfume), and the scent lingered on my skin even after I took a shower.

The bottle is cute, and is shaped like a Roman column made of frosted glass.

Overall, this scent might be good for someone who likes stronger scents, but for someone in her early 40's, this just felt too strong and dated for me.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text: I initially kind of liked this fragrance but after a couple hours the top notes faded and left a very heavy musk scent on me that made me a bit nauseous. Perfume does different things on each person, this one was not good on me at all. I may also have had a reaction to it because I couldn't stop sneezing and became very stuffed up after it was on a while so I had to scrub it off. My husband also liked it on me at first but agreed the lingering musk was quite heavy and overpowering on me.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text:
I got this for my wife and she decidedly did not like it.  I personally found the scent a bit strong and probably more suited for a different age bracket.  I first thought "powder-puff" when I smelled it but my wife said it was a sophisticated scent with elements of citrus, musk, wood, vanilla.  As I have learned from Modern Muse, a parfum intended to be interpreted differently by different people, this fragrance could be interpreted in a highly subjective manner.  Thus, it is quite difficult to write prose tdescribing a fragrance which is interpreted differently by various observers.

I found that this product did not last more then 1 hour at which time the scent faded to nothing.  As such, I suppose it would need to be applied more frequently than some products.

Overall - we ultimately gifted this product to someone who loves it.  Neither of us preferred the scent and our daughter didn't like it either.  However, each person is different.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_title: Doesn't work with my body chemistry
review_text:
Everyone's body chemistry is different, so this EDT will have a different scent for each one wearing it. I'm happy to read many reviewers like this scent. For me, it simply does not work.

For those familiar with the fragrance Ambush by Dana that was so popular years ago, on me ROMA initially follows that same scent line. My immediate first impression was, Wow! This is Ambush all over again." It has that bright, sweet, floral-ish vanilla overtone at first, but unlike Ambush, a lemony fragrance studded with faint licorice soon begins to emerge. The sweet vanilla top note fades quickly as does the citrus, replaced by a strong alcohol/soap scent. Once that is gone, the bottom note is woody - not spicy or musky wood - just plain 2x4 wood beam. Although the scent is quite strong and aggressive when first applied, it fades to almost nothing within two hours. It is an EDT after all. They just don't last like cologne or perfume.

I do like the cute, chunky bottle. It is easy to grasp and spray as well. However, I will not be wearing this fragrance. Unfortunately, it does not mix well with my body chemistry.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text: It would be an understatement to say I really like this perfume a lot. I was surprised that my wife thinks the aroma is a little strong in her opinion. However, that's the way I prefer it because my sense of smell isn't as sensitive as a lot of people. But I absolutely do know when I like an aroma or conversely don't like it. I don't have a clue where or how to start to describe the sensation or the aroma.  All I can say is I really, really like it a lot.  And I've spent a considerable amount of money on perfumes for my wife and I can honestly say this is the best ever.  Even perfumes triple this price don't smell anywhere near this good in my opinion and I've spent that much in times past.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Roma Eau de Toilette for Women
review_text:
This is not a scent for everyone. It is not easily approachable and it smells dated. It is a bit unusual compared to today's fragrances. You should like oriental, woody, resin scents to be a fan. This fragrance was very popular in Rome during the 1990's, for good reason. It is elegant without being over-the top.

This opens with a slightly medicinal scent of myrrh; a little bitter, minty & woody. This is mixed with a citrus scent that leads on to an amber with slight balsamic, vanilla undertones. There are flowers here, jasmine, rose, spicy carnation but they are discrete. As you let it settle on your skin, you will notice more Oriental spicy notes (sandalwood), green (patchouli) & dark smoky notes along with some powdery resin.

I think a man could wear this with no problem. It's feminine on a woman but not ultra flowery. It has that spicy, woody note that male fragrances often have. This is well made without being pretentious. There is also a male version of this fragrance. It is a more bitter resin, sweet, boozy vanilla, pine & citrus scent - very "Roman" type of fragrance. I prefer this "female" version, even on a man.

I find the sillage quite heavy so one spray is plenty. More sprays & you will fill the room & probably offend someone. This lasts until the next day on my skin.

This cologne could certainly qualify as unisex, and I love the idea of it being labeled as natural spray, because the scent is not strong whatsoever.

The glass bottle is a smoky color and the lid is artsy (a rigid finish) with a neat six-point star on the top. The box is an attractive mysterious blue, which is appealing to consumers. The product is made in France, and like most French beauty products, the price might be high, but the product is worth the purchase. After one light spray, the scent lasts about six hours, slowly fading away hours after application.

product_title: MONTBLANC Star Walker Eau de Toilette, 2.5 fl. oz.
review_text:
MontBlancs StarWalker mens eau de toilette is attractively packaged - as one would expect from Mont Blanc - and it has a pleasant light woody spicy scent.

My husband and I both like it because its light and not overpowering (as many mens colognes tend to be).  We both like the orange/bergamot notes.  I also like that the scent doesn't announce itself from across the room.  I have to be close to get a whiff and my husband likes that.

The scent is a mix of mandarin orange, bamboo and bergamot, with sandalwood, cedar and white musk middle notes, and base notes of nutmeg, ginger, amber and fir resin.  No, Im not the owner of a really really good nose; I researched the composition of the scent. And I also learned that the scent was originally marketed in 2005.

I do like the scent, but my internet travels indicate that savvy shoppers may want to shop around a bit, perhaps sample StarWalker, and, as always, check out prices.

review_text: Montblanc never disappoints! I am a huge fan of their fragrances. The smell of Starwalker is on the sweet and youthful side. It shares some similarities as Armani's Gio, which is my old-time favorites. I love it when he wears it out with me in a casual afternoon or summertime. I can see that it could also be a perfect gift for young men. It smells fresh, manly and slightly sporty.

product_title: MONTBLANC Star Walker Eau de Toilette, 2.5 fl. oz.
review_title: Mont Blanc Star Walker Men's Eau de Toilette
review_text:
Understated sophistication. This cologne is made in France. The scent is clean and fresh but complex and very appealing. Pulling out all of the individual fragrance notes with accuracy is beyond my amateur skill level but the main ones are citrus, woodsy  perhaps sandalwood/cedar and spicy notes, with the latter two developing as the cologne dries and is worn. The components combine to create a truly excellent fragrance.

So much of this is subjective, but when it comes to mens cologne, actually womens cologne, as well, I prefer a fragrance to, as closely as possible, be a natural extension of the person, not something that seems overtly artificial. The person is wearing the cologne rather than the other way around. Granted it is kind of an elusive balance but you know it when the wearer has succeeded or failed.

This fragrance is one that seems fail-proof unless looking for something that makes a loud statement because it speaks at a lower volume. I lightly doused the other adult with the scent and he instantly liked it very much and so did I. This scent makes me want to lean-in rather than back away.

And, since fragrances smell differently from person to person, I lightly sprayed some on my wrist to compare how it developed on my skin. It smelled quite good but unlike some fragrances for men that also work for women, this one definitely seems unabashedly male.

The smoky colored glass bottle is simple in design  classic and handsome. The pull-off, push on top is gear shaped -- chrome and black. The spray is fine and accurate. A couple sprays of the fragrance is enough to last for an evening.

product_title: MONTBLANC Star Walker Eau de Toilette, 2.5 fl. oz.
review_text:
With Mont Blanc I expect luxury and the packaging of Star Walker Eau de Toilette announces this.  The square glass bottle projects high quality as one thinks about a solid piece of heavy glass with what highly resembles a machined metal cap with the Mont Blanc snow cap on top.  It/s not a stretch to say expectations are high as one of my all time favorite scents is Mont Blanc's Legend Intense.  By this admission you can guess I prefer bold scents just as long as they're refined and complex enough to warrant being so.  But, this is a review for Star Walker, I went in to some of the former to make a point, however, and that point is the differences between Legend Intense and Starwalker.

Star walker a mixture of bergamot, tangerine, bamboo, ginger, sandalwood, white musk, amber, and nutmeg according to the manufacturer.  It's much more light and sweet than one would imagine by the ingredients.  In fact it was so light and sweet minutes after you put it on you won't be able to personally smell it - as this mixture is one of those your nose will acclimate to, and null out, within a short period.  However, others will still be able to pick up on Star Walker and this is where it gets mixed reviews from me.  While it was a pleasant primarily sweet smell when I applied it to both neck and undershirt, my wife thought it was way feminine smelling.  Bingo, she got it in a nutshell!  While not necessarily bad, my penchant for bold fragrances does not in any fashion include what I will bottom line as:  airy, sweet, and feminine - my take away on Star Walker.  This fragrance fits into what I call UNI-SEX FRAGRANCES.  In this realm its appeals to the few women I've asked if they'd wear it.  If you're interested in Star Walker it seems to be available at attractive prices at present.  This may be a result of Mont Blanc no longer showing it on their website.  One last thing, while I couldn't smell it almost immediately I asked my wife if she could at the end of the day when we both came home.  She could still smell it within a reasonable close proximity she said.  I would have not thought this possible since right after putting Star Walker on my nose was immune.  Mont Blanc's Legend Intense is still their best fragrance IMHO.  This could be considered their answer to a warmer weather scent.

product_title: CoSTUME NATIONAL Homme Eau de Parfum Spray, 3.4 fl. oz.
review_text:
I detect no cinnamon, very little sandalwood...and cloves, cloves and more cloves followed by clumps of cloves in this fragrance; it's a clove bomb and, sadly, a scrubber. Sad for me since this was blind buy.  Since I work in The District, I picked-up the phone and dialed my local EFD (Explosive Fragrance Disposal) Unit. Unfortunately, they were ill-equipped to deal with this level of toxic spillage.  CNH is a must buy for anyone wanting to exfoliate and looking for a baseline product in which to measure success. Seriously, I agree the sprayer is horrible...the damn thing lets out this fluid. (Lol)

But on a positive note, I did receive some encouraging words about this fragrance. I was told that I wouldn't be escorted out-of-the-building should I shower with lye soap. Now that's encouraging!  Scrub-a-dub-dub Costume National Homme down the tub. (Lol) Thank goodness I keep decants of Aventus, Green Irish Tweed, Fahrenheit and others at the office...and maintain my sense of humor. Still, CNH is a clove bomb; clove outnumbers all other ingredients combined, 3-1. This is a true piece but, much like a fungus or a cyst, perhaps this fragrance will grow on me.

The one highlight of this fragrance was early-on I detected a very nice peach-pie vibe for about 10-15 minutes...just long enough to remind me just how much I detest peach-pie. Finally, the pre-scrub dry-down had a sour disposition...much like Cinderella's wicked stepsisters trying to squeeze their horse hoofs into a size 5 narrow glass slipper.

I would not recommend this fragrance to anyone...well, perhaps to members of Al Qaeda and ISIS...but that's it.  Finally, if you're looking for something off-the-wall, on the niche side, without being overly expensive then take a took at Arabian Oud Kalemat and Kalemat Black (Seher Al Kalemat).  You'll thank me later.

review_text: After having tried many different colognes- from Davidoff's juvenile Cool Water to Issey Miyake's well-balanced L'eau d'Issey, from Paco Rabanne's trashy XS to Dior's wonderfully sweet Eau Noire, from Kenneth Cole's understated Black to Gaultier's exciting Le Male, this picky reviewer must conclude that Vintage by John Varvatos is the nicest cologne that he has ever tried. Sweet but not sickening, elegant but playful, sophisticated but not stale, and masculine but not rough, Vintage has a unique combination of scents that will never be mistaken for any of the "generic-smelling" colognes so often turned out by even the designer perfumeries. Perfect for a date and suitable for a dressed-up day, I find that Vintage might be just a touch too casual for evening wear- but don't necessarily let that stop you. This is one fragrance that smells so good, you might just want to wear it all the time. Keep this on your shelf together with a bottle of Dolce & Gabbana, and you'll have an unstoppable combination of complementary fragrances that will bring you through any occasion smelling better than anyone else.

product_title: John Varvatos Vintage Eau de Toilette Spray, 4.2 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text: As a fragrance connoisseur, I keep a rotation reserved exclusively for summer (cool, clean, citrusy, aromatic) scents and a separate rotation for the winter months (warm, spicy, deep, woody) scents. However, the shoulder seasons of fall and spring don't always cooperate with either rotation; too cool for aquatic fragrances while still too warm for the spicier ones. Vintage by John Varvatos has become a staple within my collection because it fits perfectly in those shoulder seasons. It is lightly warm due to the tobacco, fir balsam, and Tonka bean notes but the white lavender and jasmine notes balance it out nicely so that I can wear it almost any time of the year. I would classify it as equally well suited for casual events, work, or an evening out; it smells pleasant, very masculine, and classy. However, it is probably a little too casual for a black tie event. Nevertheless, a great fragrance to have on hand for any season or when you can't decide what to wear.

product_title: John Varvatos Vintage Eau de Toilette Spray, 4.2 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text:
I had bought a fragrance sampler as a gift last year from a high end beauty store, which was awesome. It gave my boyfriend the opportunity to try out about 15 different men's fragrances, so that we could determine which one works with his body chemistry and was pleasing to both of our noses together. It actually turned out to be a pretty awesome gift and was a lot of fun. That particular gift set came with a voucher for a full size one of his choice, and in the end we had trouble deciding. This John Varvatos was our second choice, so I made sure to add it to my amazon list as a future gift.

This not only smells amazing, the price buying for the 4.2 oz direct from amazon(I wouldn't buy from a 3rd party seller, personally) was unbeatable! It was the same bottle and box as I saw in the store. Buying this at Sephora or Ulta, it's about $75 bucks, so I was a huge fan of the price here. I would say this fragrance would span a variety of ages. We're in our early 30s, and it really suits him well. It's woodsy and rich, a bit mysterious. The notes are Ashwood, Tonka Beans, Santolina, Madras Wood, Quince Paste, Oak Moss, Silver Absinthe, White Lavender, Marine Fennel, Cubeb Peppers, Tobacco Leaf, Juniper Berries, Jasmine, Orris Root, Patchouli, Fir Balsam & Suede. A really delicious, masculine scent.  He alternates between this and a more aquatic fragrance depending on his mood. This is definitely my favorite of the two he uses. When he first started testing it out, I thought it might be too old for him, but after getting used to it, I really favor this scent. He sprays 1 spritz in the morning and when he comes home after work I can still smell it. I'd buy it again in a heartbeat!

review_text:
It's important to know where reviews on products like these are coming from. I'm 29 and a female who happens to enjoy wearing fragrances marketed towards males and females. If it smells good on my skin, I will gladly wear it. Other fragrances I use are JPG Le Male Terrible (for men), D&G Light Blue (for women), Burberry Brit Summer (for men), Armani Code (for men), John Varvatos Vintage (for men and my present favorite), CK Euphoria (for women) and Versace Dreamer.

This is by far my favorite scent. I think it's a little immature to think that only a man or only a woman can wear a certain scent, if you like it, you should wear it! That being said, this cologne makes me think of someone who is refined and neat and secretly a bit of a sexy bad ass.

The entire life of this fragrance is amazing. From opening notes to the dry down to the last little bit of fragrance that lingers at the end of the day. The worst thing about it is that it only lasts about 3 or 4 hours on me. I have been told that I leave my smell behind on other people's clothes or their furniture, so maybe it just becomes undetectable to me at 3 or 4 hours. Also, the only people to ever compliment me on this product are people (women) that come within a foot or two of me- this is fine as I don't want to be the ass that is creating scent pollution in the office! I have only purchased from retail stores, so I cannot speak to the service or product delivered by Amazon but, If you're looking for an original fragrance that is spicy and sweet but not too sweet, you should give this stuff a try! The most noticeable notes all throughout are cinnamon, leather and vanilla. Words cannot express how much I love this juice!

product_title: John Varvatos Vintage Eau de Toilette Spray, 4.2 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text:
For a new user of this cologne, you wouldn't know wether or not it's the real deal. But any normal user can the that this cologne is not legit. A price that is almost $30 below retail value should be the first clue. After receiving this product, knowing it was a knock-off, I went to the local Ulta and purchased a legit bottle for comparison. Surprisingly, the Amazon knock-off doesn't hide the fact that it is a knock-off. The obvious differences were the (1) ingredients listed on the bottom of the package were different; (2) the website listed on the bottom of the package was different; (3) the distributor was different; and the (4) bottle's bottom label was different.

Specifically:

(1) main ingredients oak moss extract and coumarin are missing
(2) johnvarvatos.com (Amazon) vs. johnvarvatosfragrance.com (Ulta)
(3) EA Fragrances Co. (Amazon) vs. JV Fragrances and Skin Care (Ulta)
(4) completely different design

The less obvious signs were, (5) the pattern of the leather wrapped around the bottle was different (diamond is vertical-shaped on Ulta and horizontal on Amazon); (6) the box texture signifying the leather-look was not embossed on the knock-off; (7) the smell was noticeably different; and  (8) the symbols and language through the packaging was misplaced and/or different.
