review_title: What a deal for a unique cologne!
review_text: I have received more positive comments when wearing this cologne than any other one I wear. It has, so I was told, an "intoxicating" scent to it. It's long-lasting, very unique smelling, and, surprisingly, relatively inexpensive. It's a value-priced cologne that has impact and attributes that pleasantly surprised me when I first wore it. It may very well become my "signature cologne" and replace my current one: D&G The One - Gentleman (another very good cologne, in my opinion). Colognes,of course, are subjective - one man's "love it" may be another man's "hate it". All I can say is that it has a clean, crisp, strong (but not overpowering) fragrance that suit me just fine. For the record, I am not a young man - to me it doesn't seem too youthful for my age group, however, can see it being of appeal to the young as well. It's a winner!

review_title: Nice fragrance once it settles in
review_text:
I love vanilla scents, and this Comptoir Sud Pacifique had great reviews so I decided to give it a try. I'll admit, at first I was not sure about this one. It goes on strong, and when I first spritzed it I got the dreaded "Play Doh" notes that other reviewers have mentioned. However, after a few subsequent uses, the smell seemed to shift for me and has since settled into smelling sweet and sugary, like fresh vanilla frosting or toasted marshmallows -- in fact, on separate occasions, I have had coworkers say I smelled like both of these. It's delicious! I now look forward to putting it on every day. The scent also has pretty decent lasting power (I still get whiffs by the end of the day) and mixes well with other sweet smells -- it has layered well when I tried it with vanilla and coconut lotions.

I think the sweetness of the fragrance might be a little too cloying for warmer months, but it's really nice for fall and winter. I'm glad I gave it a try!

product_title: Comptoir Sud Pacifique Vanille Extreme Eau de Toilette Spray, 1 fl. oz.
review_text:
Comptoir Sud Pacifique Vanille Extreme is truly an extreme vanilla fragrance!

With a name like Vanille Extreme, I was worried that this fragrance might be too strong for me, but I found it to be personal and it smells delicious.

Top Notes:  sugar vanilla, heliotrope
Mid and Base Notes:  absolute vanilla, milk

Personally I don't smell any of the heliotrope, but the vanilla and milk combine to make a beautiful caramel scent.  While Vanille Extreme is a pure vanilla scent, it's not extreme in the sense of overpowering.  It doesn't leave a cloud trailing behind me, which is something that I really don't like in a fragrance.

The scent stays with me through lunch.  By the end of the day, it's not as noticeable, but it's still there.

I tend to gravitate toward fruity or floral scents, but now I have to add vanilla to my list.

Vanille Extreme is a great scent when I'm in the mood for something sweet and pure.

review_title: don't be fooled by the negative reviews - this stuff is AMAZING!!!!!
review_text:
i actually received the brand new "eau de parfum" version of this and was immediately turned off, since i'd read so many horror stories about the new "parfum" version smelling HORRIBLE!! i e-mailed the seller and was told that this was the only version currently available, and they graciously offered me a refund. so, having said that, i was fully prepared to send this back. i cannot tell you how many negative reviews i'd seen about how this new formula smelled nothing like the original "eau de toilette" version and how it smelled cheap and all the rest.

well, on a hunch, i decided to try it...and i was immediately hooked. i did get the dreaded "play-doh" smell right off the bat, but after about 10 minutes, it softened up into the most warm, creamy, luxurious vanilla i've probably ever smelled. now, i'm a "gourmand" connoisseur - so i've got about 5 different "vanilla/maple syrup/cotton candy" type fragrances in my collection, and this immediately became another fast favorite. i mixed it with two really great smelling "maple syrup" and "vanilla fantasy" body oils, and it smelled so good that it ought to be illegal.

warm buttery pancakes, cinnamon rolls, vanilla buttercream frosting, cupcakes, sweet sugar cookies...you name it. this stuff is truly unbelievable. and if what people are saying is true - that the "eau de toilette" version smells better than this one - then holy cow, i can see why so many people love this stuff. i'll be buying this for years to come!!

so if you love sugary sweet fragrances, you will LOVE this one!! it's good enough to eat!! warm, creamy, rich, and lasts for hours!! really terrific stuff!!

review_text:
Vanille Extreme has a lovely, light edible vanilla scent.  Some vanilla scents are strictly for kids, but not this one.  I've been wearing it for many years and I still get compliments all the time, in doctors' offices, crowded stores, elevators, my hair salon, the checkout line at the grocery, often when I think the scent has worn off.
This is the best thing I can tell you about Vanille Extreme:  My dermatologist's office -- like all of them and most doctors' offices these days -- has signs everywhere insisting patients should not wear perfume, cologne, scented lotion.  The first time I went there, the office manager was quite complimentary about how great I smell (she still gushes about the scent every time I come in).  So then I met the doctor for the first time -- and she asked me to write down the name of it so she could buy it for herself..
This is the essence of Vanille Extreme:  So pleasing that not only will it be welcomed in your dermatologist's office,  your dermatologist could end up wearing it too.

review_title: Finally achieved my goal of smelling delicious
review_text:
This is what you wear if you want to smell edible. For a long time I've said my scent goal is to smell like a cupcake.  Done!

Actual comments I've gotten while wearing this:

"It smells like *deep inhale*... I don't know. It smells really good in here."
"Does it smell like cookies in here?"
"*Sniff* Do you smell like vanilla? Yum! You smell like candy!"
"It smells like Pixie Sticks in here."
"Is that vanilla you're wearing?" I responded yes, I found a new vanilla perfume that I'm obsessed with.  His response: "Yeah, well I am too, now!"

My only note would be that it could last longer.  The scent does stick around for hours, but only when you directly sniff your skin. So you and your significant other who gets very close can enjoy it for a while.  As far as other people smelling it, it probably only lasts an hour - maybe two.  I'm okay with putting on a ton of it and re-applying as needed, but of course that means I'm going to go through it way too fast.  Oh well, WORTH IT!

product_title: Comptoir Sud Pacifique Vanille Abricot Eau de Toilette Spray, 1 fl. oz.
review_text:
At some point or another, I received a tiny sample of this perfume and immediately fell in love with it. The scent was to die for, you could almost eat it, it was so yummy. I'm always drawn to scents that are more sweet and/or fruity. I used every last little drop of that sample and was dying for more. However, I just don't like spending money on myself, let alone spending $30-$100 on certain perfumes where you get around one ounce of product. It seems a little outrageous.

So, when I asked for this but didn't receive it for Christmas, I was a little sad and still wanted it. I kept my eye on it and debated just buying it myself but never did. Then, I finally bit the bullet a few days ago and bought it to treat myself. Imagine my disappointment when it arrived today and the bottle had leaked profusely and the scent was NOTHING like the sample I had. I actually went digging through my room to try and find the little sample vial to confirm that they were, in fact, the same scent.

I read reviews before I purchased and saw a few had noted the different scent, but the overwhelming majority seemed pleased so I thought maybe those few who were leaving negative reviews were wrong. I even scoffed a little at the review that mentioned it smelling like a crayon, but now I see exactly what they were talking about. It does have some type of weird parrifen like smell that is reminiscent of wax. Although the scent is not completely awful, it's not at all what I was wanting and it's extremely disappointing to have waited so long in anticipation to finally get this and it's just not the same.

product_title: Rochas Eau Sensuelle Eau de Toilette
review_title: Fruity beginning, musky dry down, a light and juicy fragrance for summer.
review_text:
Delightful, warm and juicy, and feminine are the adjectives that come to mind when describing this perfume. Eau Sensuelle comes in a gorgeous bottle that remind you of enticing layers of chiffon and spring turning to summer days. This fragrance was launched in 2009 after Rochas was acquired by P&G in 2003.

The top notes are fruity - blood orange, mango and bergamot. Middle notes -  Jasmine, Orris Root, Orange Blossom. Base notes - Dried Fruits, Musk and Pink Pepper. The blood orange and mango notes lends it a bitter and almost too fruity fragrance in the opening notes and then you start to smell the orange blossom. It almost smells like Juicy Fruit gum, almost. But then the flowery middle notes take over. The jasmine is fainter but the dry down is slightly musky and slightly spicy. The dry down works for me the most and therefore makes it a more complex fragrance than the cheap drug-store variety. It lasts 3-4 hours on me and the sillage is moderate making it suitable for work.

I will add it to my spring summer collection of fruity-flowery fragrances like D&Gs Light Blue, Burberry Brit, DKNY Be Delicious and my cheap go-to Shi by Alfred Sung. This is another lighter, fruitier and fresher sort of fragrance to add to this collection, but since it's new and light it will probably be gone by end of summer this year.

product_title: Rochas Eau Sensuelle Eau de Toilette
review_title: Well made and subtle enough for work
review_text:
In my opinion, the base o fthis perfume smells citrus and white flowers while there is a distinct note of fruit balanced by what seems to smell of jasmine.  I do note there is a light "pwedery" scent to it, but not overpowering.  Under average office conditions, the scent lasted about 4 1/2 hours.  I did not find it overpwoering in the workplace and consider it great for that application.  No associated headaches or sinus reactions.  I received a few compliments on the scent.  One person however simply did not like it and called it "fruity."

If at all possible, I recommend first smelling the scent locally and testing it.

I didn't detect the citrus notes that were mentioned in the description.  Initially I didn't think it was too bad, but the longer I was around the scent the more I disliked it.  After about twenty minutes the scent just started to feel entirely overpowering. product_title: Rochas Eau Sensuelle Eau de Toilette
review_title: Fruity Flanker to the Original Eau de Rochas
review_text:
I like citrus fragrances & I like white flowers so this should be a scent I adore.  I like it fine but the mango & dried fruits make it a bit too fruity for me.  This is not over-the-top fruit, the jasmine & neroli keep it in check but I'm really OVER the frooty tooty scents.  This one is not fake and cloying but just not my taste anymore.  If you like fruit scents but not too sweet, you may like this one.

This starts out with blood orange; a nice fresh & not-too-sweet blood orange but then the mango comes on a little stronger.  It's not too sweet, it has a bit of pepper note but I just don't care for it; the mango ruins this for me.  Luckily, bergamot & jasmine save the day, bringing a lemony, fresh flower note.  This is not the lush jasmine of Arabian scents but a fresh/light jasmine.  Underneath it all but not too heavy, is the musk & powdery note of orris.  It is not a dirty musk but more of a white musk.

The sillage is not huge & it lasts about 3 hours on my skin.  It is a well made and inoffensive/generic fragrance.  Much better than many other fragrances of this type. I prefer the Rochas fragrance "Tocade" - it's more serious & adult. Or if you like a more light/fresh Eau de Rochas, the "Fraiche" flanker version has no sweet fruits.

A bit of trivia:  Rochas is now owned by Procter & Gamble (2003).

But this product has a chemical-type odor (the 2nd or third ingredient, right before lavender oil, is "fragrance"--this is a chemical mix, and not an essential oil.)  I found this to be a very acrid scent, and, it doesn't last--which begs the question, why would I want to wear something that smells this bad?  Sorta like, "the food is terrible, and such small portions."

I thought I could use it as an air freshener, but the odor was so bad, even my husband complained about it "what IS that?  It smells like new car odor mixed with Pledge furniture spray!"  He was right.

review_text:
I'm one of those ladies gifted with the inability to buy fragrance without wearing it first. My body chemistry rarely agrees with the scents I fall in love with on paper making them smell utterly putrid after the topnotes settle. It's frustrating to the point I never trust my nose until I've worn a scent but good luck getting samples.

I happened to be lucky to get a sample of Especially Escada from their website and I am so pleased that I did! Florals are not a favorite of mine but I'm in the market for something fresh to wear and this fragrance is surprisingly pretty on me. This is very youthful and feminine scent but it didn't last very long on me. It is most definitely more of a spring and summer wear fragrance.

If you hate rose this fragrance is definitely not for you. It is the dominant note from start to finish. Think lush pink cabbage roses in springtime. Though I decided it isn't the scent I am looking for in regards to my style I couldn't help but review it because it is a very lovely scent. I would recommend this for a bride on her wedding day or someone in their 20's looking for a floral that's not too girly, nor too mature but ultimately feminine.

review_title: Second review of a very fine men's fragrance (parfum!)
review_text: I have read quite a few comments on Jaipur, none in the middle, but from one extreme to the other.  Two issues come to mind:  There are so many knock-offs out there that quite a few of the commenters were sold a knock-off.  Secondly, there is a huge difference between the cologne and parfum.  The colognes, even when fresh, are not near the scent of the parfum; if they get a little old, they behave just like the negative commenters described - weak and not very long lasting.  I bought a small bottle of the parfum in Singapore 3 years ago; to this day it is still very fragrant, albeit the bottle is about gone.  I just bought a new one and quite frankly, it smells as good and long lasting as the last one.  I sprayed a dash on in the store, took a shower at night, and got up and it still had a pleasant odor.  Even my bathroom smells nice.  I have an original Boucheron, (the forerunner of Jaipur) supposedly the winter scent that has actually finally gone rancid but it is still handy to dilute any unpleasant odors!  In my first rating of this product, I suggested that if you use this, your ladyfriend will almost certainly comment very favorably on its scent.

review_title: An alluring exotic scent that's irresistible and appropriate for use during the day as well as night.
review_text:
This is an amazing scent.  It has a deep sandalwood tone and a slightly musky ring to it that sets off all my alarms.  It is also a little powdery around the edges.  It smells divine on Mr Pixels and Bits and it's going to be a while before I encourage him to wear a different scent.  I like it so much I wear it myself, though I much prefer it on him.

It's not an overpowering scent.  It was useful to wear it as I was able to judge from two perspectives how it wears throughout the day.  We found that after about 8 hours, it loses the main thrust of its bloom.  It requires another application if you've worn it all day and are heading out for the evening.  It wears just as well during the day as it does at night.

product_title: BOUCHERON Jaipur Homme Eau de Parfum, Spicy Oriental, 3.3 fl. oz.
review_title: Interesting powerful scent for men(and some women!)
review_text: I have been using cologne for many decades and this is the first time I have come across a men's scent in eau de parum strength. Maybe that is because I am not a member of the "A" List, I don't know. I have seen many women's scents in this strength but not for men. For both men and women(less so for women) parfum strength is difficult to apply because it is so very strong(in case you are not aware, scent strength in order of strength goes as : eau de cologne, eau de toilette, and eau de parfum also called perfume; the price also rises with strength). One way to apply a light scent is to "walk into" the vapor, but that wastes a lot of expensive vapor! Anyway, let me try to describe this scent: In order of dominance, spice, wood, candy, and cookie. By candy I mean spicy candy, such as black licorice. Of course, it is difficult to describe such a complex scent but that is my take. It is, indeed, very, very strong and most men would find this unusual and, as I have said, a bit of a problem. This is expensive but for the price, you really do get a generous quantity. This is a hefty amount of perfume(compare women's perfume where for this money you usually get a thimble full!). The bottle is rather attractive but the box is nothing special. Finally, many women like to wear some men's scents and this scent is probably one many women would like to wear so, guys, if you don't like this, just give it to your lady and she will probably like it! Some people claim this(and many other perfumes) don't last long; that is a misconception. What happens is that the nose becomes quickly fatigued with the scent and you stop smelling it, but it is still there. To see this, when you apply it, make sure you also apply it to a clothing item, such as your shirt or coat; you will notice that the next day, the scent is still strong on the clothing and maybe even you! By the way, Boucheron is a French company but you may wonder if this is actually made in France; well, it says on the box "Made in France" so that is pretty clear.

It has a sandlewood cinnamon spice odor without perfume overtone. The alcohol base burns off quickly leaving a mild warm masculine scent, the warmer the skin the deeper the scent. Doesn't overpower the room and makes you want to get closer to the person wearing it. Each person's own body chemistry can alter final smell, I suggest trying in store sample to see if it will work for yours.

review_title: Great fragrance, but this newer formulation is not as long lasting.
review_text:
This does not seem to me like the original scent. I still have a bottle of that, it used to be shaped like a bracelet so it's a circular shape. The original description that I copied from the site Fragrantica says it best, "This is a legendary and exotic feminine perfume. Jaipur invites you to discover mystic and enchanted Orient. The bottle is shaped as a bracelet which is considered a lucky charm in Rajastan. This rich floral bouquet with sweet fruity notes was created in 1994. It starts with sweet notes of juicy plum, apricot and peach with a hint of violet and then it becomes a fresh floral accord of rose, locust-tree, heliotrope and peony. In the sensual, powdery trace there are gentle accords of iris, white musk and sandalwood. Jaipur was created by Sophia Grojsman and Jean-Pierre Mary."

I've been using this fragrance for 10 years now, it's so long lasting that I can take a bath and it still lingers, the sillage is also heavy. Although it's called spicy oriental, it's more sweet, almost sickly sweet on some due to the heliotrope. The amber and sandalwood base with white musk is also very strong. The funny thing is that it can smell old lady on some, due to the sweet and powdery notes, but with my body chemistry it smells more floral at first and dries down to a ambery base. It reminds me a bit of Samsara from Guerlain but that one is a bit more sensual and feels more oriental than this one. I just wish that this bottle from Amazon smelled the same as the one I purchased 10 years ago!

review_text:
I've been looking for a perfume to replace my favorite but discontinued Kate Spade Beauty. I chose to get a sample of this from another site even though it was nothing like what I was looking for (a white floral), merely because I think Roberto Cavalli designs some of the most beautiful, feminine, and sexy dresses I've ever seen and I had hopes that the perfume would have these same qualities. I was NOT disappointed.

I loved the sample so much that, even though I had already bought two floral scents (Jennifer Anniston & Pure Grace), I decided to totally splurge and get a bottle of this.  I adore it!  I don't know enough about perfume notes to tell you if it matches the description, but I can tell you I can't stop smelling my wrist!  To me, this is a more grown-up, mysterious, sexy scent than I have bought in the past.

I like it so much I was tempted not to review it so I could keep the perfume for myself. If you can't find a sample, consider getting a rollerball ($22 on other sites) to try it out.

To me it is like magic how it plays out on my skin, just beautifully addictive and sexy without being skanky. If you're in the mood for a sweetish floral that's different from the onslaught of generic fruity florals out there, give this a whirl.

The designer of the fragrance is Michael Boadi, a London-born hairstylist and very talented "nose".

review_title: Alcohol, chemical cleaner... then fades to grassy nothingness
review_text: I could easily overlook the Pine-Sol-ish top note of this at first application, because it wears off in about 15 minutes. But what replaces it is a vaguely grassy chemical scent with no depth or subtlety. And it only lasts a couple hours, so by the end of the day it disappears without a trace. Kind of reminds me of the old joke: One old lady says to another, "The food at this place is disgusting!" and the other replies, "Yes, and such small portions!"  Incidentally, since this is allegedly a man's scent I had my husband try this out a couple times for my enjoyment -- though it turns out I didn't enjoy it, and neither did he. And I (a woman) tried it myself a couple times, since I find many grassy, woodsy scents work for me. No dice. Unfortunately, this is a miss for Varvatos.

review_text: I'm not a scent-wearing person. But I was cajoled into giving this a try. I really liked the smell - it had a nice non-overpowering slightly citrus scent that didn't overpower anyone near me nor make me sneeze profusely as some cologne does. However, the smell faded away in about an hour, which was disappointing. Supposedly the scent lingered for a while after that, but it wasn't noticeable to me. I don't know if it's watered down or it just fades away quickly, but it didn't last as long as I'd like. It was nice smelling, however, but I don't want to douse myself in it so it lasts more than a few hours.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text: The bottle itself is indicative of the care and attention-to-detail going in.  This is the first  Varvatos fragrance that I've tried and this blend hits the right notes for me.  Very importantly, it's not overpowering or too much of any one scent.  This one is actually better than my previous all-time favorite, which came from a different decade.  I thought the wear-to-fade time was satisfactory, because I lean to the lighter side anyway, as the day wears on.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text: I don't usually wear cologne mostly because most are too strong for my liking but this has a subtle and very nice citrusy scent. The spritzer also doesn't overload you with product, I found one spray to be the perfect amount. On top of all that the bottle looks fantastic.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text: A rich blend of citrus, dry herb, and wood, Artisan reminds me of a slightly-younger, more hip version of Tommy Bahama's signature cologne. While the item description spends a lot of time talking about the beauty of the rattan-wrapped bottle etc etc, that's not going on a date with me so I wanted to know how it smells and how it lasts. The scent has top notes of semi-sweet citrus like blood orange or tangelo. It's not the over-the-top sweetness of a Calvin Klein cologne, but the subtle, masculine take Varvatos is famous for. This is further cut by wood and dry herb mid-notes, using majoram, thyme, and ginger in place of the more common tobacco leaf, patchouli, and musks. This makes a cologne with a sharp initial hit and heavy in its mid-range, but without the musky bottom of a Drakkar. All of which should be fantastic, but... This cologne faded really quickly, and not in a cologne-vs-eau way. Having tested the same cologne at Nordstrom, I'm stunned at how watered-down the bottle from Amazon seems. Having worked with high-end colognes sales in my past, this can happen if the incoming supplier does something shady like actually water down the product or, more likely in this case, if the product is being warehoused poorly, with temperatures and age deteriorating its potency. I'll give Ammy the benefit of the doubt and hope it's the latter. To be clear: Varvatos has (yet again) created a brilliantly good men's cologne. Just maybe pick it up someplace else.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_title: Fresh, masculine scent that doesn't quite last all day
review_text:
This is a very pleasant scent. I find it hard to review cologne, but here goes:

This is fresh, masculine, and clean smelling. It sprays fantastic and is not overtly strong.

The trouble is that this doesn't last long enough. I find that after applying at 6A, the scent is basically gone by noon. You have to get your nose planted on my clothes to smell it beyond that time.

So, overall it's a great scent that just doesn't last long enough.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text: I've always been a fan of John Varvatos fragrances. I can be picky too.  I hate when a fragrance is too much, shouting "I'm trying too hard". Artisan has excellent lasting power. Sophisticated with a beautiful warm, woodsy dry-down. This Artisan fragrance is really lovely.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text:
I wanted to try this Eau de Toilette spray from John Varvados on myself first.  Why?  Because it is my nose that smells my husband's scent.  He is not one who often puts anything on except aftershave, and I am picky in terms of anything scent.
This Eau de Toilette spray starts out with a fesh citrus scent.  But now, four hours later, I can only detect the wood and sweet undertones which now dominate.  The citrus has retreated far into the background.

Perfumes and Eau de Colognes/Toilette sprays interact with body chemistry, so it never smells the same on another person.  I am curious how it will smell on my husband.

I read reviews that claimed that this spray does not last all day.  But four hours later it is still going quite strong.  Cold it be that the wearer's nose just can't discern it anymore?  That seems to happen with habitual perfume wearers, and some end up dousing themselves to the point of fumigating their entire surroundings.  Please, never do that, just because you don't smell it doesn't mean it's not there anymore.  And a lot of people are quite sensitive to perfumes and can get sick.

I do like the scent of this spray.  While it comes through as sweet, it still has a masculine property about it.

The packaging is very handsome with the bottle enclosed in wicker.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text: Very nice fragrance. This is a first for me but was impressed by light, not overwhelming fragrance. Great gift giving idea, this has a unique appearance, an ample amount and scent that is fine for daily use. It's notable but not overwhelming - different than most. Has a hint of citrus with an earthy undertone....but not "old hippy". Refreshing!

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text:
The great thing about scents is that they smell a little differently on every person and mix with your body chemistry to sometimes change the scent into a fragrance that is entirely pleasing or one that is totally nauseating. This one, Artisan by John Varvatos, worked great for my husband -- who is a die hard Acqua di Gio fan (and I love that cologne too). I am really into scents that are more "fresh" and lighter than the heavy stuff like Drakkar Noir, etc. so I was very happy he liked this too. I actually wore this myself to work one day just because I like the smell, and I didn't mind that it sort of 'wore off' slowly over a couple of hours.

On him it has a citrus start when he first sprays it on and then after it dries it has a more woody scent though I find it very hard to analyze the different components of a perfume or cologne. I didn't smell the floral component as strongly as others have mentioned. I like that it is pleasant and not overpowering, and actually, I'm glad it doesn't stay at max potency for hours and hours. I don't want a man's smell to overwhelm my senses while I'm eating or on a bus or plane. Just a hint or whiff of fragrance works -- not like he's bathed in a tub full.  I think that liking or not liking a scent is a very particular thing for each person. That's why it is so important to "try on" a scent just as you do with other things you wear. Fragrance can make a statement about you and it might take awhile for you to find one that says what you want it to.

It presents with a caramel-colored rattan woven cover over the spray bottle inside a cardboard box. If you like citrus and woody smells on a man, you would probably like this but I'd suggest you try a sample first before you buy the whole bottle.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_title: Citrusy and fresh, but short lasting and slightly forgettable fragarance.
review_text:
Whatever its original origins, JV is now yet another muti-dozens-of-millions-of-bucks MBA-managed exercise in niche branding and market cultivation.  But, beyond that, heck, they make nice stuff (I have a couple pairs or JV shoes that I like).  And this cologne, while not super, is nice stuff.

My view on eaux de toilettes is that i get what i like more or less regardless of the cost, since amortized over the actual use, it doesn't cost very much at all, assuming you don't swim in the stuff.  This has not necessary led me to buy the most expensive things - as i said, i get what I like.

I wore this on two cold winter days so far.  In both cases it seemed to wear off quite quickly.  But, it smelled nice while it lasted.  Maybe i'll spray a bit inside my car just to horrify the people who use terms like "sillage" and "frangipani" without blinking :)

I can definitely feel the citrus scents that they refer to, overall it's just ok.  I found it a bit harsh on my very sensitive skin, but that should be tempered by the fact that i found most other products to be harsher than this.  This is probably too "citrusy" to be worn on cold weather days like I have for testing purposes, so I'll put in back in its place for now until it warms up a bit and then will give it a go.  I kind of imagine this working well on days when you decide to break out the linen suit.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray, 2.5 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_title: Fantastic If It Didn't Fade So Quick
review_text:
I have been a long time user of Aqua Di Gio Essenza, which is very expensive. I can justify the cost because it lasts all day long and into the evening. Di Gio has a wonderfully fresh, just out of the shower smell, which always elicits comments from lady friends who say, "damn, you smell good."

Upon first "smell" of Varvatos Artisan, I was impressed with its citrus burst, which transports you to the Caribbean or Jamaica. Has a hint of a lemon/lime freshness to it. My wife immediately commented on how wonderful it smelled and that she absolutely loved it, BUT, 2 hours later...nothing, unless she literally put her nose to my skin. There is a very slight lingering odor similar to fresh linen, but it can't be detected beyond a foot or so. TOO BAD, because this stuff is fantastic. So, I would say that it is a "bedtime" spray but not something to expect any kind of longevity, through the day.

Varvatos, why not add oil of parfum to the mix, to extend its life. You would capture a sizable audience of repeat customers, beyond those who made an impulse one time buy at a fragrance counter. They liked it in the store, but after a day of use, they will abandon it and not purchase a second time, due to the "fade" issue. It is a 5 Star fragrance, but a 1 Star longevity, so I had to at least recognize it for the quality of the fragrance itself, with 3 Stars.

review_title: What can I say about Pink Sugar that hasn't already been said?
review_text:
I was so happy to find this in a rollerball! Even though the full size bottle isn't a bank breaker, I like roller balls. They're easy to pop into your purse or makeup bag and they last a while. For me, the convenience of a rollerball usually wins out over spending tons of money on scents that can only sit on my vanity.

Pink Sugar is one of my favorite scents...it's not going to be for everyone and if you aren't a fan of sweet, warm vanilla or fresh baked sugar cookie type scents you are probably not going to like it.

Despite its sweetness there is a warmness to it that settles nicely and subtly. Some sweeter scents are accompanied by this chemical, artificial scent which makes me nauseous. Pink Sugar, does not.

This little rollerball comes just like the full size version...in a pink and white tube and the clear glass (yes glass and not plastic) has the same pink design on it that the full size has.

It took awhile to get here and was obscenely over packaged in a box 50x it's size, which was totally unnecessary, but it definitely got here safe lol.

The only negative thing I'd say about the rollerball version is that it doesn't seem to last quiiiiiite as long as the spray, but I guess that's the glory of being able to carry it around with you.

All in all, great price for a great perfume. I'll definitely repurchase when this one runs out.

review_title: not quite as citrusy as I thought it would be....
review_text:
It is always difficult to read a description of perfume because everyone's chemistry is a little different.  I think that is the case with this eau de toilette.  My attention was drawn to the product for a few reasons, it is a good brand, I like citrusy/fruity scents and am willing to try something new.

At first spray I was a little disappointed because it definitely smelled more woodsy, like sandlewood with a little vanilla, but as I sniffed my wrist throughout the day I found that by the end of the day it took on a more citrus scent, not sharp by any means, but moreso than when I first sprayed it on.  It stays on all day and I would say it is a pretty smell.  No one note really takes over, so it it seems to have many layers to it and is a more sophisticated/elegant scent.

My husband tends to like fruit/citrus scents on me the most but said he thought this was a pretty feminine scent and not overpowering, just right in his words.

Overall, I enjoy the perfume and have worn it for a few days now.  It won't take the place of my favorites, but it definitely has a place in my perfume rotation.

review_title: Burberry Brit for Women is a lovely scent that is long lasting
review_text:
Burberry Brit for Women EDP is a lovely scent that I found to be long lasting on my skin. The top notes of the scent are fruity - greenish citrus fruit - which is refreshing. After the green notes wear off, the scent becomes floral and softer. The final scent is a vanilla, woody scent that is warm and long lasting.

Burberry Brit is great for daytime and evening wear. I have a number of old stand-by scents that I wear and it's difficult for a new fragrance to break into the line-up. This scent has managed to do so. I have enjoyed wearing it and having people ask me what perfume I am wearing. It seems to agree with my skin.

review_text:
I'm picky when it comes to perfumes, so I was delighted to discover that this is exactly what I've been looking for! The scent is clean and classy, avoiding the highly alcohol-y undertone of old lady perfumes and the over-wrought forced brightness of a lot of the perfumes targeted towards younger sets. I love that the scent is feminine and alluring without being blatantly flowery or "exotic".

I am also thrilled that this perfume is perfect balanced in strength. It's subtle - it won't knock anyone over when you walk into a room or cause grief for people who don't tolerate fragrances well - but still strong enough to be pleasantly noticeable and to last the day. I love it, my husband likes it, and it's balanced enough for daily wear. This is decidedly my new favorite, and I will be highly recommending it to others!!

It is a light fragrance that is not overwhelming and that is my preference for a perfume.  I want to smell it when I move my arms but not be assaulted by it. product_title: Burberry Brit For Her Eau de Toilette Spray, 1.7 fl. oz.
review_text:
I've tried the Burberry perfumes before, more specifically Burberry Weekend. I loved that it was a light floral scent that wasn't overwhelming and could work in most situations. I've never really gotten into some of the other scents as much because I tend to like lighter scents more and they tend to work better on me with my body chemistry. I'm both blessed and cursed by the fact that most scents will become 3-4 times as strong once I put them on. It's good because I can use less of it than others do, but it's bad because some of the stronger, muskier scents just won't work regardless of how sparingly I put them on.

This was supposed to be a lighter scent, so I decided to try this one.

So far I really like the scent. The alcohol scent is fairly strong when you first put it on, but wait that out because that goes away after about 30 seconds. There's a nice floral tone to this backed up by a deeper scent, which gives it a little added maturity in my opinion. It's the type of scent that you can wear if you want to put off a more serious countenance, although it can easily lend itself to a lighter atmosphere. This is an all purpose type of scent for the most part.

The one thing I'd warn you about is that a little bit of this goes a long way. The Burberry scents tend to work better with my body chemistry than others so I can put a normal dose on (about 2 squirts) but this is one that I'd recommend testing out around the house first. It smells great, but one pump was about all I needed with this. Take in mind though, that this is with my body chemistry and the average person will likely be able to do the normal dose or maybe a squirt or two more.

I really like that this doesn't fade away easily, something that can happen with some of the body sprays that I tend to use on a regular basis. This is probably due to the difference in how they're made since the B&BW sprays are mass produced to be sold on the cheap while Burberry things would likely be made to last longer.

So would I recommend this? Yes. It's pretty hard to go wrong with Burberry scents and while I still prefer my Burberry Weekend, this would make for a good alternative.

review_text: This fragrance is the one that gets the most questions about what I'm wearing. It's light & timeless, if you've never owned a Burberry perfume this is the one to start with. After your first purchase, you will always remember  and distinguish the Burberry Brit.

product_title: Burberry Brit For Her Eau de Toilette Spray, 1.7 fl. oz.
review_title: Feminine and sweet, hard to stop smelling!
review_text:
I have purposely not read the adjectives they used to describe this scent, in an effort to go in clean and describe just what I smell in this fragrance!

Words I'd use to describe Burberry Brit:
Sweet
Feminine (definitely feminine!)
Orange
Jasmine
Vanilla (just a hint, I actually don't care for vanilla scent, but it's a very light touch)
Floral -- maybe hyacinth, hibiscus, a hint of sweet rosewater
Light, not musky or spicy
A hint of Asian influences (I don't know what I mean by that, just that it has a touch of "exotic" undertones)
Reminds me slightly of a grown-up version of the scent "Exclamation," a popular teen-oriented fragrance in the early 90's!  (But in a good way...this isn't a Walgreens scent like Love's Baby Soft or anything!)

This scent is absolutely impossible to stop smelling!  It is even nicer as time goes on -- an hour or two after applying it, it smells just heavenly.  SO feminine and refined, but not your grandmother's fragrance by any means.

It plays well with others -- it has a distinctively beautiful scent, but will mingle nicely with other unintended scents vying for attention (such as my mango shampoo) -- it just seems to blend nicely with other scents, and with your body's natural scent.

It lasts a good long time -- I hate it when you can't smell your perfume an hour later!  It's not overpowering, but it can easily become a "signature scent" that people associate with you, because its sweet, pleasant scent will still be detectable several hours later.

I am really in love with this scent, and I have gotten so many positive comments on it, even from coworkers who usually hate perfumes!  It always seems to be the same reaction: closing their eyes and inhaling deeply.  I have done that myself so many times with this Burberry Brit that I was in danger of fainting once after inhaling the scent too deeply over and over.  :-)

I think this is a fragrance I would "risk" giving as a gift to someone -- I haven't found anyone yet who didn't love it!

review_text:
I like the classic Burberry for Women for it's sensual practicality but I love Burberry Brit even more as it's lighter and more wearable. Burberry Brit is a great perfume for a woman who is transitioning from the more casual drug store or flowery variety of perfume to an older more defined and distinctive fragrance. She wants to smell more mature but not too old. Burberry Brit is perfect. It's flowery but fresh and sporty at the same time, musky but subtle.
I've been a fan of Brit for the past 12 years, ever since it launched and always have a bottle handy. I love it in the summer, it smells fresh but not too flowery and sweet. It's got more staying power than D&Gs Light Blue, which has a similar flowery, lemony fragrance. This is a great fragrance for those who want to avoid heavier fragrances.

There is a Brit Sheer version that's just too mild, and a Brit Summer version that adds Green Tea for a lighter effect. If you ask me the original Brit is the best as it has more staying power. When you spray it on you smell the lime and pear, and then the middle notes of white peony, and as it dries down it leaves a delicious musky, vanilla finish.

Apparently, my nose is nowhere near as sensitive as theirs, and I'm not sure I caught the "fresh and playful top notes with Italian lime, icy pear and crisp green almond," nor the "sensual notes of vanilla bean."  I did however notice the sweetness of the scent, although I couldn't say if it has anything to do with "sugared almond" or not.  My wife and daughters use this, and when it first goes on it has a very *clean* smell, but after a moment I can definitely sense a sweet scent to it.  And I realized for the first time last night that as the evening wore on (we were at a friend's party) I could still smell it on my wife and there was definitely a floral feeling to it.  So, I guess they really do know what they're talking about when they describe it as they do.  Regardless, I think it's a very nice fragrance and it lasted very well outdoors on an evening where temperatures stayed in the mid 80s.  A very pretty bottle, too.

product_title: Burberry Brit For Her Eau de Toilette Spray, 1.7 fl. oz.
review_text: This is a very British scent.  It's a classic scent, with strong tinges of nostalgia.  The notes I smell most significantly are lime, pepper, vanilla, and some faint woods.  The opening is mostly lime and pepper, but the vanilla is quickly apparent, and rounds out the scent.  This is by no means a sharp lime.  Given those notes, it's hard to really imagine the experience of the scent, and I've found that what it evokes is more important to me than the notes.  This scent reminds me of an old manor house, classy and classic, but slightly down at its heels.  It needs repairs, but it is still putting its best face forward.  It brings to mind the old wood parlors, the sprawling grounds, and the titled family living inside.  For an interpretation more in keeping with those of us living stateside, it brings to mind New England college campuses in the fall, not at the beginning of the semester, but around November, when the leaves are falling off the trees, and everything is dampened by a cold rain, and people seek shelter in a wood-paneled library.

product_title: Calvin Klein ETERNITY AQUA Eau de Parfum
review_title: Light, Crisp Day-time Scent Ideal For Summer
review_text:
Whether you like a perfume or not is such an individual preference, it's impossible for words to tell you if you're going to like it, especially as it blends with your own body chemistry. A quick glance through the reviews on Amazon (and elsewhere) of Calvin Klein Eternity Aqua (and every other fragrance) proves that some women adore, while others loathe, the very same product.

That said, I got this for my wife, who is a mature woman (not in the trendy 20-something youthful market). She has had a few weeks to try this perfume while we move into the warmer months. Her analysis is that she enjoys it, finds it refreshing and not overpowering, and feels it is her daytime, go-to, summer scent. As one of her choices for going out in the evening, she prefers Calvin Klein Euphoria. I happen to like the Euphoria better, both in scent and the bottle itself -- a little more creative in design.

It's hard to beat those Manhattan copywriters for description! "A fragrance like a clean crisp ocean breeze. Top notes - White peony, crisp pink lady apple and cucumber water. Mid notes - Tiare, magnolia, gardenia, jasmine. Base notes - Sundrenched woods, cedarwood, transparent musk." Those things are important to read! I saw one woman's review where she said she hated it, because it smelled like peonies. LOL! The first "top note" is "white peony," so if you despise the flower, you are not going to like this perfume! In fact, both my wife and I note the apple as a highlight. This fades after an hour or so to more of the mid-notes, which include flowers we both enjoy, including magnolia, gardenia and jasmine. Some other reviewers hate "something woody" in the base-notes. Not our experience. Cedar and light musk are both fine.

By the way, Calvin Klein's fragrance line is famous for "Eternity." This won a coveted FiFi Award as the top women's fragrance back in the late '80's. It was inducted into the Fragrance Hall of Fame in 2003. You could be forgiven for thinking that Eternity Aqua is something similar. Not so! They were created by different perfume makers and have little other than (part of) a name in common. I was a little surprised to learn that the male versions of these eau de parfums also bear nothing other than name relationship, also made by other designers. Therefore, if you like "Eternity," you will have to try "Eternity Aqua" for yourself, as it has no scent-relationship to it's famous older sister.

You might not know or even care that Calvin Klein has not owned his perfume companies for a long time. The CK fragrance lines used to be owned by Unilever, which owns billion dollar brands including Axe, Dove, Lipton, Hellman's, Becel Margarine, Fudgsicle, Popsicle -- and even Ben and Jerry's ice cream, just to barely scratch the mega-corp surface. In 2005, Calvin Klein fragrances were acquired by cosmetic giant, Coty, Inc. Coty also owns Adidas, Chloe, Davidoff, Marc Jacobs, and even Playboy. Coty also sells you the beauty products fronted by Jennifer Lopez, Beyonce, Kate Moss, Madonna, Lady Gaga, Vera Wang, Lagerfeld, Guess, and a whole galaxy of celebrities. Very big business indeed!

Just thought you'd find that interesting!

Eternity Aqua (for women) -- "an aquatic floral scent."

Recommended with this caveat: you'll have to try it for yourself.

product_title: Calvin Klein ETERNITY AQUA Eau de Parfum
review_title: A clean scent that reminds me of sitting on the beach
review_text:
One of my favorite scents and one I am quickly adopting as my signature scent is Calvin Klein's Euphoria. It's got this woodsy, yet feminine and floral scent that I just love.

I loved Euphoria so much, I thought I would expand to try Calvin Klein's other scents. Hence why I chose Eternity Aqua, a scent that's been around since 2012.

Top notes - White peony, crisp pink lady apple and cucumber water
Mid notes - Tiare, magnolia, gardenia, jasmine
Base notes - Sundrenched woods, cedarwood, transparent musk

When I used Eternity Aqua, the words that came to mind were "fresh summer breeze at the beach" and "clean". The cucumber was definitely apparent to me, not so much the peony or the apple. It almost smelled more like clean towels or blankets without the nasty chemical scent. After a while, it settled into light, airy floral mix - I can't say that I detected gardenia and jasmine, but it was a light floral scent, not too heavy and still harkening to spring and summer and sitting by the beach.

The scent lasts a decent amount of time. The initial spray isn't too strong, and it lasts about the standard 15 - 30 minutes. The next few hours, the scent is much, much more muted - I found I had to sniff the application spot to detect it (though to be honest, isn't that what adjusting to your own scent is all about?). I think I can go about an entire work day with the scent on. One of the things I do love about the scent is that it isn't too strong and in your face. It smells clean and breezy, not too girly, not too husky.

That said, I don't know that I would put this as one of my "signature scents". I like girly scents like "Intimately Beckham", but it smells just a wee bit too "clean" like detergent for my tastes. But it's a great scent for a day on the beach or for summertime or to give yourself a nice aroma without burdening your coworkers with a nasty scent.

*C.S. Light*

review_title: Attractive, subtle scent that works well for summer
review_text:
I have always liked the Calvin Klein fragrance line, as I have found their scents to be high quality and generally long-lasting as well. I have had tried ETERNITY, but not ETERNITY AQUA, so I was excited about the opportunity to sample this new-to-me fragrance.

Upon application, ETERNITY AQUA gave off what were both watery and powdery notes to me--a very soft, pleasant combination.  I can't say that I picked up any of the particular notes listed in the scent description.  I definitely would not describe the fragrance as "cucumber water," which is go for me since I don't like the smell of cucumber.  I may be picking up on a bit of gardenia/jasmine, and the more powdery note that I detect might be the musk undertone.

I will say that compared to some of the other CK fragrances (such as the original ETERNITY and OBSESSION, both very powerful scents), ETERNITY AQUA is VERY subtle.  It is quite light going on, and just about three hours after application, I can hardly detect that I am wearing perfume, even when I put my nose directly to my wrist.  This is a bit disappointing--my fragrances don't have to be strong, but I do want them to last, especially when I enjoy the scent.

So, in the end, this is a fragrance that I like quite a bit, but I gave it four stars instead of five due to how quickly it fades.  Still, it is an attractive light scent that would work well for summer, and I would recommend it.

Calvin Klein Eternity Aqua is aptly named since it's fresh, ever-so-slightly floral aroma contains top notes that are redolent of a sea breeze on the beach. The artistry involved in designing a perfume never ceases to amaze me. The Aquatic, Oceanic, or Ozonic, which is the newest category in perfume history, first appeared in 1988 and this is a particularly fine example of the genre.

The top or head notes are described as white peony, crisp pink lady apple and cucumber water and crisp is the operative term because your first impression of this Aqua will be its exceptionally pleasing crispness, directness and distinctiveness. After a few minutes following application, the aroma of white peony and crisp pink lady apple will yield quite subtly and the cucumber water will assert itself, announcing the long-lasting fragrance (it was still softly fragrant after 24 hours on the wrist) that distinguishes this Aqua.

As the freshness of cucumber water begins its aromatic dominance, the mid or heart notes of tiare, magnolia, gardenia and jasmine add a lovely floral complexity which categorizes the main fragrance notes or theme of Eternity Aqua. This combination of cucumber water and floral bouquet is the single most distinctive and assertive aspect of Eternity Aqua. It is a pleasant and fresh scent that I have never found to be either cloying or unbalanced.

After some additional time (30 minutes or so) the base notes which are described as sundrenched woods, cedarwood and transparent musk add depth and richness, with the wood elements and musk augmenting the fragrance with a distinctive dryness and strength, amplifying the persistent bottom notes that serve to frame the freshness of the cucumber water fragrance. Calvin Klein Eternity Aqua is a refreshing, elegant and long-lasting fragrance which can be applied any time of day.

review_title: Great For Spring-Summer: Reminds me of Breezy Fresh Linen and Sweet Flowers
review_text:
This perfume is perfect for the spring-going-into-summer weather right now. It is an interesting fragrance combination of fresh and floral that works really well together and can be playful, sophisticated, and feminine all at once. Meaning...it can be worn day to night and on the weekends, too. It's got high notes that remind me of breezy linen freshness over a sweet floral body. One does not overpower the other and doesn't give me or my husband headaches. And it doesn't have any low notes like musky, woodsy, or spicy aromas pulling it down.

Some complain that this perfume doesn't last long but in my experience I think perfumes that don't have the low notes seem to not last as long because it's usually the musk, woods, and spices that really cling after the high notes other smells fade. This is not a problem for me at all and I actually think this perfume fades to a really nice floral scent that is pretty and super soft. But if you want to smell the way the perfume smells out of the bottle all day long, just reapply throughout the day.

I would recommend this to anyone who likes oceanic/linen/floral perfumes. Also I would recommend to those who like citrusy perfumes but want to try something more floral but worried that they can't stand the overly floral stuff.

It has a pleasant color and dispenses easily.

review_text:
I have no special expertise in reviewing perfumes. It's never been something to which I gave much thought, so my main point of reference for this is the reaction from my wife when I gave this to her.

First: Excitement.
Second: A bit of disappointment after the first use.
Third: A much more positive reaction after she realized she should use a lot less of it.

I think it smells pretty nice, though I'll again mention I don't have a very sophisticated sense of this. I do agree with my wife, though, that a little bit goes a long way, and it's very pleasant when just a little bit is used. That's good news, too, because it means a small bottle will last a long time.

Overall, I definitely feel like the description of this scent is accurate, and it makes for a nice gift, especially if you judge by the first rule of gift-giving: happy wife = happy life.

product_title: Calvin Klein ETERNITY AQUA Eau de Parfum
review_text: Perfume is such a personal thing, not only can one person find appealing what another does not, a perfume can also smell different on different people.  I always loved the smell of Calvin Klein Eternity, and was excited to try the Eternity Aqua version.  Aqua is a much more subtle scent to be sure, but to me there is no main scent so while it is pleasant and fresh, it just doesn't really have depth to it.  I like a scent that makes me want to breath in more deeply and this one just says "I'm clean."  Although I found it went on strong, it wears off very quickly.  Bear in mind, this is just how I felt it smelled on me.  If you are considering purchasing this, I would recommend trying it in a brick and mortar store first, possibly get a sample, and it you like and it works for your body chemistry then go for it, but unfortunately it didn't work for mine.

As with any cologne, I recommend going to test it out before making any investment in larger size bottles like this one (for that reason, e-shopping for any first-time cologne is a bad idea), but if you've used it before you know how long a bottle this size is going to last (hint: a long time as long as you aren't needlessly drowning yourself in it) and will realize that this is actually a nice purchase. I'm very happy with it, and my wife adores it, so I give it my highest recommendation.

product_title: BURBERRY London Eau De Toilette for Men, 3.4 Fl. oz.
review_title: Skip this and just get Bulgari Black!
review_text: This is the men's scent du jour, the way sweet fruity fragrances are produced in hundreds of iterations for women. It's not a bad scent, but a bit artless. All the components just try too hard: the spicy cinnamon is over the top, the woods are perfunctory but not particularly beautiful and well-done, there is an ozonic edge with becomes terrifically cloying and it's just too sweet in a potentially headache-inducing way. Bulgari Black pioneered this type of combination and remains the benchmark. It's gorgeous for both men and women, completely wearable, and still unique, with the faintest whiff of rubber tire. I know that sounds weird and awful, but the best (and most expensive) Scotch ever had reminded me of Bulgari Black, being in a motorcycle garage with a bit of rubber, diesel and leather. Plus, the Bulgari Black bottle is fabulous and the little shred of cheap (polyester, rather than the actual Burberry cashmere) fabric covering the bottle is tacky and annoying. It can be removed - as it is only glued on in a couple of spots. It's a let-down.

review_title: pleasant, surprisingly complex scent for men, understated rather than overpowering
review_text:

review_title: A hard to define but wonderful scent!
review_text: My husband likes wearing scents, but he's never really tried any of the more expensive, not-drug-store scents, so we were excited to try this, and we both love it!  I'm not good at describing scents, but it has a little bit of a Maine woods smell, and somehow also takes me back to when I was very little and my father used to smoke a pipe---not smoky, but something that reminds me of that.  It lasts well---just a little spray in the morning and I could still smell it when my husband got home from work nicely.  I got this to review, but it's good enough so that if I could find it on a bit of a sale, I'd buy it again.  Somehow it just says "class"!

review_title: Interesting and attractive masculine fragrance in a stunning package and spray bottle

It has an interesting and complex and distinctly male fragrance BUT DON'T APPLY TOO MUCH. Notes of pipe tobacco, old wood, brandy. Nothing flowery or floral that I can detect. If you wear a tie to work, a little spray of this ought to suit you just fine. This would make an impressive gift for a husband or boyfriend. Do not overdo it, a little bit is more than enough. This kind of product is like a nice set of cufflinks or a good quality necktie, subtle finishing touches for a man. Not overstated but substantial the way that a subwoofer reproduces bass notes in music, a solid foundation, but not in your face. Again, more is not more in this case. Do not overdo it!

product_title: BURBERRY London Eau De Toilette for Men, 3.4 Fl. oz.
review_title: What sort of fragrance, if any, one likes is a personal and enormously variable thing
review_text:
People's views about what is a pleasant scent, and what scent (if any) it is good to wear are enormously variable, and personal.  (E.g., I like the scent of lavender, but find it unpleasant when used as (or in) perfume.). So it's hard to provide much useful general information in a review.

That said: the man who will wear it likes it, but only if it is diluted and not slapped on.  Both of us are more soap-and-water people, and agree that--while it is nice to be able to wear some fragrance at (e.g.) holiday parties--a little bit of this stuff will go a long way.

product_title: BURBERRY London Eau De Toilette for Men, 3.4 Fl. oz.
review_text: A very powerful cologne! A manly scent that lasts a good long time. This can be problematic for people with sensitivity to strong odors. My wife has a highly sensitive olfactory system and I have to be careful not to overwhelm her with colognes, soaps, or lotions that have strong scents. Burberry is pretty strong, but with attention to application it can be fine to use even around my wife and her hypersensitive nose. I do wish there was a screw on top for more control over application, but I can still spray a single pump onto a cotton swab and dab it on to control the amount applied. This seems to work best for me and I still find the scent to be lively and long-lasting. A single 100ml bottle should last me a very long time.

product_title: BURBERRY London Eau De Toilette for Men, 3.4 Fl. oz.
review_text:
This is my first experience with the Burberry line of fragrances.

The bottle has their characteristic tweed design.  It's an attractive bottle.  Packaging was virtually frustration free.

The scent.

There are two types of scents that I tend to assess when it comes to fragrances or colognes.  First, how does it smell from the bottle, onto a card?  I get an airy scent of citrus, followed by pine and spice and finished with a hint of soft high grade leather.  It's fragrant but not overbearing or too powerful.  Next, how does it react with my skin?  That is most important.  Each person will perceive or radiate something completely different.  For me, it has the initial scent of citrus with a spice finish.  The scent is subtle and clean.

Overall, it's a great scent.

review_title: The first one I'd ever actually wear
review_text:
I'm not a fan of aftershave, perfume, cologne, etc...  I've never worn any, since they always seemed to just be too overwhelming or too generic.

I thought I'd try this just out of curiosity.

The bottle is unique - the wrapping is a material, a fabric, that's glued to the bottle.  But this was part of the reason for me taking a star off.  It's crooked, it's glued too high so I have this fabric up over the top of the bottle, and it's only glued in a few spots, so it isn't SECURE when you hold it.  And when you are holding the bottle "normally" and go to depress the plunger to spray some, it pushes the bottle "down" and you can feel this outer material sliding.  I wouldn't be surprised if after a little time of the adhesives getting pulled and pushed at, suddenly one day it slid right out of this material.

But on to the main part, the scent.  As much as I dislike colognes and such, I really, really do like this scent.  Another reviewer mentioned cinnamon, but I don't get that.  My problem is, I can't quite nail down exactly what this underlying bite of odor is trying to remind me of.  Might be a bit of red-hot, cinnamon, something else all mixed.  I can't put my finger on it, and if I ever do, I can update this.

But the bottom line is that it's actually a nice smell, not at all like the other things I've smelled people wearing.  Definitely a masculine smell, and this time that's NOT a bad thing.

review_title: A Sophisticated, Long-Lasting Masculine Scent. Strong at first, but mellows out very nicely.
review_text:
I'm not exactly a connoisseur of perfumes but I really do like this scent. I like the fact that it smells a bit rustic and woody, and it has presence and body without being overbearing. I think the Burberry London for Men goes on a bit strong at first, but within a few minutes, it mellows out and feels pretty natural. I found that just one or two spritz is just right and it's detectable even after 6-8 hours or so from a couple inches away.

I'm not sure how to describe it, but I think scent is a good middle ground between being old and not too young ~ It's more sophisticated and lasting than CK One, which is the only scent I've used recently (and I think it tends to be a bit too sweet). All in all, I really like the Burberry London for Men Eau de Toilette, and I think the Burberry checker fabric around the bottle really rounds out the package.

review_text:
I think it's awesome smelling for anyone.  It does seem a little more masculine but if I smelled it on a girl I would still love it.
Probably not using perfume nomenclature properly here but.....

It has a strong sweet cinnamon overtone smell that fades a little over the day, underneath that it has a sort of base/moderate leather  and tobacco smell (this sounds like it would be bad or stinky but it's extremely pleasant.. it's like the pleasant parts of leather and the molassesy rich parts of tobacco, and I love it),  then the very faint undertones are a little flowery and mossy/woody.

So between the overtone of sweet, the base sort of musky tones, and the very faint/light floral tones... you end up with this really well balanced delicious spicy scent that I can't get enough of.  That aside, it doesn't have a huge staying power so you have to use several sprays, particularly the initial cinnamon blast of it which fades the more than the other parts of the scent.  That's okay with me though it smells so good ill drench myself in it or just reapply it later if I want it to last.

Note: I've owned two bottles one from the initial run and one from the reissue which probably all bottles are from now, they were slightly different but both good.  I feel like the initial run stayed a little longer, but it could be my imagination... overall very similar. Also I did not buy these on amazon, I know perfumes on amazon can get a bit dicey from what I've heard.

review_title: Beautiful scent that is both casual and elegant, not overpowering. Nice gift set.
review_text:
Buying a scent without sampling first is a real crap shoot. You're either going to like it, hate it, or it will be just "meh." It's best to obtain a sample first if at all possible. That said, I will do my best to describe Lacost Eau de Lacoste.

Lacoste Eau de Lacoste is a eau de parfum that smells lovely. It's a feminine, lightly floral and cotton scent that is casual yet understatedly elegant. It smells cotton clean but not the "April fresh scent" of a fabric softener. The scent is not heavy and cloy, it is light and endearing. Eau de Lacost reminds me similarly of Avon's Real Gold, but lighter and fresher. My mom, who is not one for heavy or crazy scents, has not once complained of my wearing of this perfume. It's a good scent to wear that makes one feel pretty without knocking everyone else's olfactory sense out.

The body lotion goes on smooth and absorbs quickly. A little bit goes a long way and the scent is not overpowering.

Lacost Eau de Lacoste, in my opinion, is for those who want a clean fresh scent that is still yet feminine and pretty but not overpowering. It evokes the feeling of waking up happy in freshly laundered sheets on a bright Spring Saturday morning. It a nice scent to wear daily.

The bottle is also quite pretty and the price is fairly good for such a gift set.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Femme Eau de Parfum Spray for Women
review_text:
This eau de parfum has a very light fragrance. It is reminiscent of flowery cotton, but it is so light that after a couple hours when I held my wrist up to my friend to ask if she could smell it she could not. This is wonderful for those who are sensitive and hate those elevator chocker scents.

It comes in a handsome spray bottle. The lotion that comes in the package also has this light scent but the lotion itself is very runny. I would use it for the scent to rub on my skin, but as for it to be used as an effective lotion for skin softening/ body lotion for example it would have to have a creamier/thicker base.
The box makes a nice gift set and for those who like light fragrances this would be a good choice.

product_title: MONTALE Eau de Parfum Spray
review_title: Vanilla With A Little Wood & Spice
review_text:
This is a fairly simple vanilla - especially simple for Montale.  It is vanilla (& a heavy dose of Styrax Benzoin, I think) with slightly bitter wood undertones and just a hint of spice; maybe cinnamon, nutmeg & cloves.  It's not really sweet but has a candle wax note that is a bit off-putting to my nose.  It just doesn't smell as deep and rich as most Montale parfum.  Perhaps too much styrax benzoin which often smells cheap to my nose.

The sillage is beyond arm length with a single spray & this lasts about 8+ hours on my skin becoming an even more simple waxy, vanilla scent.

product_title: MONTALE Eau de Parfum Spray
review_text:
On my skin I get mostly cedar, lavender, and vanilla with an underlying powdery iris & fresh green patchouli (not the funky/hippie kind).  There is some kind of delicious spice and nothing very flowery.  It's not sweet, not musky, not dirty.  I barely get any notes of lemon or bergamot.  I think they are there just to freshen it up, kind of like adding lemon to the end of cooking. To me this is a unisex fragrance; it's neither masculine nor feminine.

This has a huge sillage; a little goes a long way.  One tiny spritz will fill the room & it lasts until the next day on my skin when it is mostly lavender.

product_title: MONTALE Eau de Parfum Spray
review_title: Huge Boozy, Oriental, Vanilla, Apricot, Floral
review_text:
Opens with a big boozy vanilla and juicy apricot, then the flowers arrive - jasmine, ylang ylang & peach blossoms.  The jasmine is a little sharp at first but calms down to a distinct, lovely flower.  It's a full, juicy apricot but the sharpness of the flowers keep it from getting too sweet.  I would actually like a bit more apricot because this is a really good one - not the fake, rotting fruit type.  Underneath all of this is an exotic mix of sandalwood, wood and spice,  This is a huge Oriental-Vanilla-Flower-Boozy BOMB - delicious if you like these notes.

Not a standard vanilla.  It's not sweet, no patchouli & no musky notes.  Very adult fragrance and very well made.  It's like standing in a tropical garden with a glass of the most delicious, aged rum in your hand.

Even though it's supposed to be a female fragrance, I really think a man could wear this one.  The flowers are there but it's not girly and the boozy vanilla with spicy sandalwood say, "Seduce me, I know what I'm doing!"  I think men would have women wanting to sniff & get closer ;)

As with most Montale Parfum, the sillage is huge; it can fill a room so go easy.  One spray is plenty.  This lasts and lasts on my skin.  I still get the vanilla/flower scent the next day.

product_title: MONTALE Eau de Parfum Spray
review_title: Smells Like An Expensive Beeswax Candle
review_text:
This is a linear fragrance; it really doesn't change that much over time but it is a complex potion & not for the faint-hearted.  This is a brilliant, grown-up scent that I consider unisex.

My first thought was beeswax candle & when I asked my husband he said (unprompted) - "You smell like a candle".  Now, this isn't just any old cheap candle scent - it's a very nice honey/beeswax, sweet almond & a bit of really good dark/dry vanilla.  I barely get any flower in this at all - maybe a hint of rose but I have to really sniff to find it.  Perhaps heliotrope?  There seems to be something almost powdery & a tiny hint of spice - maybe nutmeg?  Marzipan or some other almond-based candy? Oud?

This is really lovely and really well made.  No fake, cheap notes but it is sweet.  No musky/dirty notes.

review_text:

I'm not exactly sure which note is the standout that i small the most but it has a powdery smell. It could be the cardamom which naturally is very strong.

Top Notes:
Ginger, Bergamot, Cardamom, Cinnamon
Heart Notes:
Sage, Apple, Heliotrope
Base Notes:
Sandalwood, Teak, Amber, Tonka, Musk

product_title: MONTBLANC Presence Eau de Toilette
review_title: Classic meets modern in a masculine fragrance.
review_text:
Testing this as a free product from the Amazon Vine program.
I like this scent, it's quite a timeless masculine scent with plenty of woody overtones a little oriental spice and some musk but not overpowering.
Fragrances are so subjective so it's difficult to recommend this for everyone, but from the point of view of everyday wear it seems to last well through the day and into the early evening, something some more expensive or well known fragrances do not.
Presence was launched in 2001 so it's been around a while, top notes are ginger, cinnamon, bergamot and cardamom; middle notes are apple, sage and heliotrope; base notes are teak wood, sandalwood, tonka bean, amber and white musk.
Nice mix of a fresh modern scent combined with some classic tones that lasts.
A little pricey for EDT (Mine as tested is a 2.5oz bottle)as the listing at $55 is for a 1.7oz or 50ml , and this price range is usually 3.4oz or 100ml

product_title: Carven Le Parfum for Women Eau de Parfum Spray, 3.33 oz
review_text:
Carven Le Parfum is a sweet and fruity perfume with notes of pear, guava, and jasmine.  The high quality fragrance remains consistent after multiple hours of wear on bare skin and clothing.  It does not decompose into powdery or artificial scents like cheaper perfumes.  I would characterize it as a youthful and flirty, fit for all occasions.  Had I encountered it during my dating life, I would have been swept off my feet.

I tested a small dab on myself and a full spray on my wife.  The scent was strong up to the first four hours, and gently declines until it is just a hint after 12 hours.  The EDP concentration rating is the strongest available, and one spray should last all day.

Advice from a former perfume seller- if you buy Carven for below full price from other sellers, beware that the bottles are often sourced from other countries and there is no guarantee of authenticity.  Go to Neiman or Nordstroms to smell the true scent if buying it for the first time, and don't hesitate to complain to Amazon if you receive a dud.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Essenza Di Roma Eau de Toilette for Women, 0.84 fl. oz.
review_title: Very Powdery and Feminine With Florals - Daytime Scent - Girly
review_text:
When I saw some of the same notes as my favorite perfume I ordered this to give it a try. My favorite is an oriental: Obsession by Calvin Klein. On me the scent of Roma is strong at first especially of powder or "dry down" and dying down a great deal after two hours into something I like better. I feel it is strong of powder and florals with base notes of my preferred woody, oriental scents with vanilla and amber. I figured out what the confusion is. The product info on Amazon is incomplete for describing the scent. What it says at the time of writing this review is only a partial listing of the notes in this perfume. It says: "This scent captures the essence of femininity built around a core of woodsy notes that form the base. Layers of vanilla and almond continue the theme of warmth, while mandarin orange and cyclamen round out the top." That description is far too short and gives the wrong impression.

For the purpose of writing this review I wanted to know more about what was in the scent to give it that powdery aspect and why I felt it was not as oriental as I prefer. The official site has no words only images. I then turned to Fragrantica who describes it as an oriental spicy with "top notes are black currant, sicilian bergamot, pink grapefruit, mint and hiacynth; middle notes are carnation, jasmine, lily-of-the-valley and rose; base notes are amber, sandalwood, singapore patchouli, musk, civet, vanilla, oakmoss and myrrh".

To me this is very feminine and powdery while oriental spice, musk, patchouli, vanilla, oakmoss and myrrh are all unisex and dominant earthy scents. Trust me, this is more of a daytime feminine scent than a sexy evening scent.

I rate this 3 stars = It's Okay. It's just not for me.

product_title: Laura Biagiotti Essenza Di Roma Eau de Toilette for Women, 0.84 fl. oz.
review_title: Pleasant floral/citrus scent that packs a punch initially and dries very powdery
review_text:
It's difficult to describe perfume without sounding extraordinarily pompous, but "it smells nice" doesn't seem sufficient for an amazon review. So here I go -- 'm not sure this scent "captures the essence of femininity" but it is a very feminine scent.  Seems more formal than playful to me, something I'd wear for an occasion rather than every day.

The box reads:
This scent captures the essence of femininity built around a core of woodsy notes that form the base. Layers of vanilla and almond continue the theme of warmth, while mandarin orange and cyclamen round out the top.
An elegant, sensual and classic scent to make you feel unforgettable like Rome.

This scent comes on strong right out of the bottle and it smells very formal and floral to me. Pretty overwhelming -- very "perfumey" and old-fashioned.  I want to say grandma-ish, but nearly all of my friends are grandmas . . . and they sure don't smell like this.  The initial pow dissipates quickly, and fades to a light, pleasant, powdery citrus scent.  I do not detect warmth, muskiness, almond or woodsy notes, nor do I detect the kind of fresh, green scents I usually go for.  I smell citrus and powder, with floral overtones. Pleasant and feminine.  Nothing earthy or exotic of woodsy, and no hint of vanilla.  Does it remind me of Rome?  Not exactly.  But it does smell nice.

The more I wear it, the more I like it.  It is very long-lasting!  Although it's an eau de toilette, it is longer lasting than most perfumes I have.
