review_title: Very sweet, a touch saucy, vibrant and extravagant
review_text:
This scent is a bit too rich for me, but I can imagine a youthful, fun-loving and vibrant individual would just love it.  Just a touch of spray makes me smile--actually I can come close to a cute-sy kind of giggle.  The product I received definitely has staying power.  I moved the spray head further away from my skin and shortened and lightened my finger's press on the pumper for subsequent applications.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Acqua Eau de Toilette Spray, 4.2 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text:
I really love this scent. The scent is definitely evocative of the name and design of the bottle. It's a scent you could easily imagine greeting your nose as it blows across a warm, sunny, sandy beach. It opens strongly enough without being overpowering, and the dry-down is even and pleasant.

There are a couple of caveats I would add: the longevity and overall projection of this cologne is average, and that might be a generous statement. Having applied it six hours ago, I can still smell the scent but barely, whereas other colognes in this price range seem to have much longer legs. Projection is fine at first it quickly falls off during the drydown. Within the first hour or so, one needs to be pretty close in order to pick up this scent, at least on me. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, as this limited projection would make it a nice office scent...if only the longevity were a few hours longer.

I do recommend Artisan Acqua, but just keep in mind that it offers a more ephemeral experience than most colognes and should be utilized with those shortcomings in mind (e.g., a summer evening out that you expect to last three or four hours).

review_text:
Lacoste offers an elegant, hearty and sophisticated perfume.  From the appearance of the bottle to the fragrance, it proves classy and up to the standards of the best evening out or professional gathering.  It is a perfect gift for a woman who wears perfume and is open to trying to fragrances.  This subtle and pleasant scent should draw the right kind of attention.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_title: Love this sweet and subtle scent
review_text: I requested this for my wife to try.  It has a sweet smelling scent that initially makes me think of cotton candy or bubble gum.  The scent starts out a bit strong when first applied but settles into a more subtle and warm sophisticated scent.  Once it settles in, it becomes noticeable without being overbearing.  Two to three sprays is enough for a nice projection.  People nearby will catch a light whiff when standing within  a couple feet or closer to the wearer.  Thankfully, it's not one of those overwhelmingly strong scents that would make your eyes water from across the room. I love this fragrance on my wife.  We're both a tad shy of middle-age but I think this fragrance is appropriate for any age group.  It's sophisticated without coming off as too mature and versatile enough for any event, whether she's wearing an evening gown or jeans and a sweater.

The perfume itself I would describe as a sweet smell. It smells good on my wife and she likes it. To me it is a rather simple fragrance and not overpowering and not overdone. product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_title: Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_text:
Sensuelle radiates sophistication from its unfussy bottle to its complex feminine fragrance - sweet but not overpowering. It has depth and a touch of mystery. Category-wise this is what is referred to as a gourmand scent which means it contains significant food-based notes such as vanilla, chocolate, coffee and berries.

In this particular fragrance, I noticed nougat, black current and pepper. I found nougat to be prominent in the middle and base notes, the part of the fragrance that lingers for hours. The initial scent is black currant, which is layered with a light floral fragrance. The longer it was on the more pleased I became with how the scent developed. Although not the same, it reminded me a bit of Lauren by Ralph Lauren.

This is not a light fragrance so I will probably wear it only in the evening and I will use it judiciously because it is strong. I sprayed the smallest amount I could control on the inside of my wrist, from a distance of about seven inches, and let it air dry, and it easily was noticeable for seven or eight hours. I recently learned that something I had been doing for years, rubbing wrists together after applying scent, actually alters the balance of the fragrance and should not be done.

Allowing time for the fragrance to develop rather than judging on the initial sniff is wise, and often offers some pleasant surprises. I do not have a signature scent but rather select what to wear based on my mood, and this is a very welcome addition to my usual group of fragrances.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_text: Well I'm giving this mixed reviews, because my wife likes it, but I hate it. It's REALLY REALLY potent. It smells like a flower threw up on a hundred other flowers, who then got sick and threw up all over each other. Ugh. My wife thinks it's nice, though she agrees that it's very very strong. And because it's a spray, you can't exactly control how much you get. So, mixed results for us.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_text: I'm always hesitant to buy perfume without smelling it first but was very pleasantly surprised with Lacoste Sensuelle! My go to perfume is usually Dolce & Gabanna Light Blue or Cartier Baiser Vole and now I'll definitely incorporate Lacoste Sensuelle into the rotation. Light Blue to me is a bit masculine, sexy smell and while Baiser Vole is more elegant, feminine. I think Lacoste Sensuelle falls somewhere in the middle. It's definitely not overly floral or fruity  - I'd describe it as more of a sophisticated, grown-up scent; "sensual" that Lacoste uses in its description is very appropriate. I'd also recommend letting it settle in for a few minutes before decide whether or not you like it - it smells completely different once it settles on your skin.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_title: Love how it smells on my skin
review_text: I had no idea what to expect when I ordered this perfume since I'd never smelled it in person. To date Love Struck Eau De Parfum Spray for Women by Vera Wang, 3.4 Ounce has been my signature scent but as it is becoming increasingly difficult to find so I've been open to trying something new. If Love Struck is my more floral, warm weather scent, this feels more appropriate for the cooler months. It has a nice warmth and richness about it that I found really appealing and quite different than a lot of fragrances for women I've tried. Initially when I sprayed on my skin I wasn't sure I liked it, but after it settled into my skin I LOVED the fragrance. It's lightly sweet without being cloying or smelling artificial and every time I smell it I get a hint of a different note, which I love. I'd highly recommend it.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_text:
This was gifted to me by a friend who knows how into fragrance I am....this is not one I would choose on my own.  It is sweet - too sweet for my taste.  But if you like sweet gourmand fragrance, you may like this.  It is well done for a sweet gourmand & not sickly sweet fake fruit like so many are today.

It starts out a bit sharp & fizzy with pink pepper & moves quickly on to black currant followed by nougat (sugary, a bit of nutty sweetness).  The nougat scent lasts the whole way thru.  The flower notes are just background.  A bit of rose, a bit of sweet pea but barely there; they just keep this fragrance from going too far to sugar overload.

It doesn't have a huge sillage but go easy with it.  It does radiate more than arm's length.  This lasts at least 12 hours on my skin and I get whiffs of it the next day.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_text:
Scent is a very personal thing. What works for some does not work for others. In this case I am in the "other" category. To be fair to Lacoste very few perfumes interact well with my body chemistry. About the only two that work without changing chemically after I apply it are Joy and Byblos.
That said, I didn't care for the smell of this at all. I looked at the description which describes it as: "an elegant, sensual fragrance that captures the natural intensity of soft floral notes on a relaxed, warm evening. Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle opens with the tangy tartness of ripe and lush blackcurrant. The heart has the rich elegance and femininity of Turkish rose. The base finishes with the enveloping sensuality of the nougatine accord."

I didn't find it to smell at all floral let alone that of a black currant or Turkish Rose."  And actually the smell reminded me of Thierry Mugler's Angel which also reacts badly in terms of smell with my skin. After about 30 minutes, the perfume had a very chemical type smell.

My rating of three stars is my personal feeling towards the smell of this perfume right out of the bottle. As I said it smells similar to Mugler's Angel. I didn't get a real feel for the above described floral notes.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_text: First, I admit I will have a hard time accurately describing the nature of this particular fragrance. Definitely sweet, definitely complex. To me, more fruity than floral. Another reviewer used the phrase "sour grapes" and "black currants", and these would be the closest I'd come to. I generally liked it - definitely a "grownup" product you wouldn't find a teenager getting excited about.  It lingered a long time, perhaps a bit on the strong side. Maybe the kind of fragrance you wear the evening after a grueling tennis match or something...I'm sure this is what they were aiming for. But I'm not sure words are an adequate way to describe a fragrance like this, so definitely try to sample it firsthand if you can.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_text:
A dark shade of violet is the hue that comes to mind while inhaling the fragrance of this sultry, spice tinged mix. The scent will work wonders when worn in a setting with soft mood lighting, delicate flirtatious conversation in tow and a libation or two to dull the edges downward a notch or two.

Dried cherries, red wine, toffee, nutmeg are the scents that stand front and center upon initial whiff while gently tapering down with hints of musky, floral components (jasmine?). Remnants of the aroma will stay on your skin through the entirety of a day/night and within a few hours softens up by revealing more pronounced baby powder inflections while still carrying forth the primary accent of dark spice.

The fragrance is well packaged in a beautiful dark blue glass orb that lends an air of mystery and sorcery that complements the contained scent perfectly. Excellent fragrance and presentation for a mid-tier range perfume.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_text:
I seldom wear perfume, but when offered this product I decided to try it.

I am not sorry. It is a much fruitier and more flowery scent than the one I otherwise use very occasionally---a musk oil I've had for eons that is quite subtle and (I think) unusual, as it was custom made.

I could never have accurately described the scent as well as the perfume connoisseurs who likewise grabbed this offering. They did remarkably well. One reviewer agreed with LaCoste---it is "tart" and further noted the scent of "bitter grapes," as well as the sensual and youthful nature of the floral tones that give this perfume a gravitas appropriate for the board room. Agreed.

Like my musk oil, this scent requires only a dab to do the trick and lasts a very long while. Over use can also over-power those around you, and is not recommended.

I would not pay $68 for this (or any scent) but I am very glad to own it and am sure the contents of the beautiful cobalt blue jar will last me for years.

product_title: Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women
review_text:
I'm very much a fragrance addict - I have dozens of bottles of cologne and perfume that I mix or save for certain occasions. Part of why I like to mix my scents is because I'm rarely 100% satisfied. Perfume these days tend to be either too sugary and sweet or too old-fashioned and flowery. Adding a musky cologne can tone down an overbearing perfume and, alternatively, a hint of sweet perfume can make a cologne less intimidating.

The reason that I have chosen to give 'Sensuelle' 5 stars is because I feel like it is pretty much perfect as is. There is a brooding darkness that lingers just underneath the floral overtones that is the perfect combination of naughty and nice. I like that they describe the blackcurrant as 'tart' because there are some notes of bitter grapes. The floral aspects are indeed sensual, but in a youthful modern way. It's very much a strong, powerful businesswoman fragrance. It's not something I would wear to the club. It smells too important for leisure and frivolities.

My only warning is that you should not overuse this fragrance. A little goes a LONG way. Too much will have a dizzying effect that will be counterproductive to the mystique that makes it work so well. The bottle is simplistic, but perfect. This fragrance doesn't have a gimmick or celebrity sponsor, it's just classy. The dark, purplish blue color of the bottle is an excellent representation of the scent in a hue.

OVERALL: To be honest, some of Lacoste's fragrances have left me underwhelmed. This one, however, is worth trying. It doesn't try to pander to a youthful audience but it doesn't repeat the same problems of 99% of the floral fragrances that are on the market. I love the darkness mixed with sweetness. Highly recommended!!

review_title: A Very Floral Scent With Fruity Overtones - Very Pricey As Compared To Competitors
review_text: I'd first like to throw out the disclaimer that my wife rarely wears perfume. It isn't because of any physical issues on either of our parts (we both enjoy the smell of her perfume), but she is a very no-nonsense gal who doesn't wear alot of makeup and thus she prefers a minimalist approach to her daily beauty routine - which rarely includes perfume. So when we both smelled the "Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women" our first impressions was that it was VERY strong. The only way I can describe it is it has a main floral scent with fruity overtones. I don't know if it smells exactly like "blackcurrant", but the fruity-ness is clearly there. I sprayed it into the air and then stepped into the falling mist and it was not over-powering, but still somewhat strong. When my wife sprayed a little on her wrist about 5 min later she said she was starting to get a headache. Kind of reminded me of the flowery scents that I remember my grandma and her friends wearing... So I guess we weren't that impressed. As far as the price goes, apparently "Eau de Parfum" describes an entire subset of fragrances distinct from "perfume". Perfume/Parfum is the highest end of the fragrance scale (and the most expensive) and will contain at least 15% of the "essential fragrance" (and typically up to 30%). Eau de Parfum is the next level and contains 8-15% of the essential fragrance. The last two levels are Eau de Toilette and Eau Fraiche/Eau de Cologne which have 5-8% and app. 3% respectively of the fragrance. So looking at the other Eau de Parfum's on Amazon.com, "Lacoste Eau de Lacoste Sensuelle Eau de Parfum for Women" is on the top end of the scale - much, much more expensive per ounce than almost all of its competitors (such as Guess Eau de Parfum Spray for Women, 2.5 oz - $22.47, Curve Vintage Soul By Liz Claiborne For Women, Eau De Parfum Spray 3.4 oz - $28.28, and Organza By Givenchy Eau De Parfum Spray, 1.7 Oz - $48.70). However, this may just be a byproduct of it being new on the market as several of the Eau de Parfume that I looked up, were steeply discounted - some 60-70%. This is somewhat typical for new products. The original price comes out at a level that the retailer hopes to get and then after the market is established for the product, the price is then adjusted (usually down). Overall, I think I am being somewhat generous in giving the product three stars. I didn't particularly like the scent and I think its priced much too high. However, at $20-$30 for this product, which I think it will eventually fall to, my opinion is slightly less negative.

review_text:
I absolutely love this perfume. It is light and rose-y without smelling like an old lady. It does have a slight sweet fruit smell also, but it very light and compliments the rose sent wonderfully. You smell this and instantly think of a sunny spring day in Paris.

I normally wear Chloe by Chloe but at $130+ for a 2.5oz bottle at Sephora it is not exactly budget friendly so I am so happy I found this to wear day to day. Like another reviewer stated at $50 for 2.5oz it is a steal!

The only down side I have found now is that it is not compatible with most refillable travel perfume bottles. The pump under the cap is shorter and fatter than most.

product_title: L'Occitane Fresh & Delicate Roses et Reines Eau de Toilette, 2.5 fl. oz.
review_text:
In my search for the perfect rose perfume, this was nowhere near the top of my list of contenders, but after I saw it in a limited edition gift set in November, I saw my opportunity to give it a go.
I am incredibly happy I did -- I was considering purchasing the more complex Roses de Chlo eau de toilette, which is a very similar scent, but I'd say this is just as pretty, if not prettier.
The sillage isn't great, but when layered with the soaps and body lotions (and spritzed in the hair at the nape of your neck), one can increase the longevity of the scent.
At $50 for 2.5 oz, this is quite a steal compared to similar designer rose perfumes (Roses de Chloe, Dolce & Gabbana Rose The One, Balenciaga's Rosabotanica, etc.).

review_text:
I have been searching for a subtle rose fragrance to wear and this one is it.  Too many rose fragrances are pungent or they change from a feminine floral fragrance into a harsh scent as the day wears on.  This perfume smells the same all through the day although as the day wears on, you might have to reapply it.  It also does not trigger any sneezing or allergies.

The faint rose fragrance is very feminine and sexy.  The scent is most apparent to those who get close to you and is not overpowering when out in public as some rose fragrances tend to do.  When I wear this scent I get compliments from both men and women.  I have a rose garden and the scent reminds me not of the powerful smell of roses in the morning but rather that smell that comes right after the flowers have been hit with a bit of sunshine.  I am so satisfied with this fragrance that it has ended my search for a rose perfume to wear.

review_title: Too strong and floral for me
review_text:
Because the base notes are bamboo, sandalwood, bare musk accord, I thought this would be a more natural, deeper scent.

When first putting it on it is very strong, even the littlest amount is very overwhelming and it actually gave me a headache.  After a couple hours the scent is more subtle, but still very flowery.  I was hoping that initial floral scent would fade away and the musky undertones be left, but it's just flowery and too strong for me and I only put a tiny amount on.

If you like strong floral type scents and perfumes, you'll probably like this.  The scent is lasting and the bottle it came in is pretty.  It's not the scent for me though.

review_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum Smells Heavenly!
review_text: The Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum is now my girlfriend Tammy's favorite perfume. She has been smitten by it. I gave it to her as an early Valentine's Day gift without telling her I got it from the Amazon Vine Program. She thinks the world of it. She likes it much better than her Chloe Eau de Toilette Spray (Chloe By Karl Lagerfeld For Women. Eau De Toilette Spray 3.0 Oz) that I normally buy for her. Tammy likes to spray the endless euphoria on her wrists and neck. She has to be very careful with sprays and oils because her extra-sensitive skin breaks out. So far, she hasn't experienced any allergic reaction with the endless euphoria. I like to call it endless love because of the hit movie, "Endless Love," starring Brooke Shields and Martin Hewitt. Out of curiosity, I sprayed some of the endless euphoria on my own wrist and loved its heavenly scent. However, according to Tammy, the scent doesn't last more than a few hours. This isn't a deal breaker with her because normally, after coming home from work, she takes a shower and sprays more perfume on her. It wouldn't be a deal breaker for me either. I normally use Obsession for Men (Calvin Klein OBSESSION for Men Eau de Toilette, 2.5 fl. oz.), which, coincidentally, is also manufactured by Calvin Klein; I always spray some more on me when I want to freshen up before going out for the evening. I seriously believe that Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum would make an excellent gift for the special woman in your life.

review_text: In my wife's words:  "I liked it well enough when I put it on in the morning, but by the end of the day, I was ready to get it off of me."  She describes the notes of this perfume as being far too bright for her liking.  Her preference in perfume is Spellbound by Estée Lauder, and something called Candide (I have no idea who makes this).  I compared the three perfumes, and I tend to agree with her:  the notes of her preferred scents are more muted and subtle compared to the Calvin Klein, which is a bit overwhelming for my tastes.  My wife & I are both in our 50's, so maybe this perfume was not designed with old fuddy-duddies like us in mind.  It definitely strikes me as being something which is designed for a younger generation.  So if you aren't an old fuddy-duddy, this may be a great scent.

product_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum
review_text:
I have bought my wife lots of perfume over the years, but find that I can't stand the powerful ones.  So I was on the look for something very light.  I like the light smell, but it matters if the person wearing it likes it more.  So I asked my wife to comment.  She says,

"A light, floral scent, definitely suited for Spring and Summer.  I don't have a "nose" so can't tell you exactly what florals I do smell.

According to information found on the internet, it has "top notes" of: cherry blossom, mandarin, bergamot; "mid notes" of: violet, pastel rose accord and syringa; and  "base notes" of bamboo, sandalwood and bare musk accord.  I don't smell musk (which I don't like) and it's not a heavy scent.  Not too sure about sandalwood, either, (but I do like that scent on my man).

Information from the internet also states that Endless Euphoria is the "daytime counterpart to Euphoria.  Now we have daytime and night-time scents?  So I have to buy two kinds of perfume - daytime and nighttime?  Good marketing ploy - for the rich or those who have too much money on their hands.  (Say, if you have too much money, why don't you send me the amount you would spend on either the daytime or nighttime version, and we'll both be happy!)

Not an overpowering scent, and I'm noticing it doesn't linger/last "forever", so you might want to get a small, purse-size one to carry with you to refresh scent throughout the day, if you're one of those ladies (me, I'm just a once-in-the-morning-does-it kind of gal), or layering is good - body-wash, powder/lotion, scent."

Now my wife gives it a 4, as it is light and disappears after awhile.  I give it a 5 because it is LIGHT.  A heavy or even medium perfume is too much for me to be around.  So since I am rating it gets a 5.  However, to the ladies who would actually wear it, please think about what my wife said if you want a stronger scent.  I really hope this helps.  It is so hard looking for the perfect perfume that everyone around can like.

product_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum
review_title: Endless Euphoria is good... but not for me.
review_text:
Calvin Klein makes a good variety of perfume, and Endless Euphoria is one of the better ones based on most.  This one is good for those who may enjoy floral scents.  However, it was not to my liking.

UNBOXING:

This perfume bottle comes in a small pink and purple box.  It is cellophane-wrapped, smartly packaged without too much insert material, and is easily removed.

REVIEW:
Endless Euphoria comes in a unique shaped bottle--very aesthetically pleasing.  However, it is slightly prone to tipping over if you're not careful due to the oblong shape and small base.  The fragrance is sweet and floral.  I disagree with many who say it's a fleeting scent.  Once put on, I could smell it for over an hour.

However, the biggest detractor for me was that it was a cloying scent that reminded me too much of what older women wear.  Do you know what it's like to run into a bunch of older women in a gathering, such as in church, or at a party, etc?  Perhaps it's my fault of what scents remind me of, but I could not wear this much beyond the first day.

OVERALL:
Is Endless Euphoria a good perfume?  I would say, to most yes: it has a lasting fragrance, is in an attractive bottle, and is priced well.  However, I can't give it more than 3 stars due to the fact that I'm just not into the scent.  If you don't mind heavy floral and sweet smells (that remind me of what older women wear), then this is probably for you.

product_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum
review_title: A real winner.  Good value and long-lasting floral notes.  Compares well to Pleasures, Beyond Paradise.
review_text: This perfume is definitely a winner.  My wife has used primarily softer perfumes in the past--Pleasures by Estee lauder, Beyond Paradise, etc.--but she really likes this one.  Endless Euphoria is stronger both in terms of length of time it lasts on the body and in terms of intensity of smell.  But it is not overpowering and has floral tones that soften the stronger sandalwood and musk.  I also really like it on her.  This is a perfume that can be worn in any season but can take the heat of summer, I think.  It will be a winner for women who like floral perfumes that have a full-bodied, long-lasting sense to them.

product_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum
review_title: Lovely scent, but it will require some reapplying throughout the day.
review_text:
My wife isn't a fan of perfume. She's actively avoided it for many years, but when I decided to get Euphoria for her, she was not ecstatic at first, but trying it, she was very pleasantly surprised.

Thankfully for all of our olfactory tastes, it's light and flowery. There is nothing overpowering about it, although if one were to apply it liberally, as some users are won't to do, it would become as unpleasant as the $6 knockoffs you'd find elsewhere. Just a spritz or two, and there's a fresh and extremely pleasant scent that doesn't last overlong. However, it doesn't last too long, period, which is really her only complaint.

It's Calvin Klein so it's going to be expensive, but it should last long enough for many wearers.

product_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum
review_title: Very nicely and subtly scented, and not overpowering...
review_text: I don't like women to wear heavy, overpowering scents that arrive to a destination a half-hour before they do, so thankfully, this was a very light, pleasantly scented perfume. When I gave it to my girlfriend, I noticed it had light flowery notes, with a little spice, none of which I could identify, but both of which were subtle and very pleasant. What was most important is that she liked it, and was a nice, elegant, pleasantly scented surprise gift for her.

product_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum
review_title: Slightly too sweet and wears off, but pleasant scent
review_text: This is a lightly sweet, floral fragrance. It's rated as an "Eau de Parfum", which should be less concentrated than Perfume, but stronger than Eau de Toilette. However, my wife feels that it is a much weaker scent than some of the typical Eau de Toilette fragrances she uses. With 6 sprays onto her clothing, it was barely noticeable (smelling the clothes & skin directly) 3 hours later. Even though its supposed to be more concentrated, it did not seem to last very long or have a strong scent to begin with. I don't like a fragrance that is overpowering, but of course you want to notice it. I do like the scent itself. But my wife would not choose this as a "summer fragrance" (as it is advertised), but thought it was ok for evening wear in the semi-tropical climate where we live.

product_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum
review_text: I really like the scent on this. Of the notes used, I can definitely smell the citrus but it's toned down with the base notes of sandalwood and musk and then there is that wonderful hit of floral from the cherry blossom and rose. An very nice well round scent, only one spray is necessary anything more would be overpowering. I would definitely wear this for special occasions as I don't wear perfume much but did enjoy the wonderful mix of floral, citrus and wood/musk.

product_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum
review_text:
This perfume has light, fresh overtones, but it also has a definite musky heart.  The airy breeziness of the topnotes is definitely the most euphoric thing about this scent.  On me, however, it dries down into a rather musky fragrance, something that is not especially euphoric, and something that I don't particularly like.  My skin tends to amplify the musks in perfumes, and that's absolutely the case here.  I've also used the original Euphoria perfume, and I do prefer Endless Euphoria to the original.  I find that Endless Euphoria is lighter, and maintains its floral notes better than the original.

Scent aside, the packaging is beautiful, and the bottle fits nicely with the concept.  This is a generous-sized bottle; there's quite a bit of fragrance in here.

product_title: Calvin Klein endless euphoria Eau de Parfum
review_title: Euphoria is euphoric... Light, airy, long-lasting...
review_text:
I knew I liked this perfume from the moment I spritzed some on my wrists. It's an awesome fragrance; not too strong, not too light. It lasts for hours, which is good enough for me.

It's been a long while since I have braved going from the milder colognes to genuine longer-lasting perfume, but after reading the reviews I decided to get this Calvin Klein Euphoria... and I'm glad I did.

It's just the right blend of floral and woodsy to suit my tastes... and the men in my life agree.

With the cost of living so high now, everyone appreciates a good buy and since this name-brand perfume is $20. cheaper than my favorite department store, I am beyond pleased.

In addition to the fragrance being so pleasant, I think the bottle is well-designed... pretty, elegant and rosy pink... It looks lovely on my dresser next to a family photo in a mother-of-pearl frame.

I recommend this highly to anyone who likes their fragrance more light, airy and lasting. To describe it in one word... well, that would be "euphoric." :-)

Reviewed by Betty Dravis, February 23, 2015.
Author of "The Search for Bobby McGee"

product_title: Lacoste L!VE Eau de Toilette for Men
review_text:
Lacoste L!VE is a brand new fragrance for men launched in the spring of 2014.  It falls under the crowded "male oceanic fragrance" category.  The top notes in this fragrance are citrus with middle oceanic notes and a dry light woody base - a classic non-offensive oceanic male fragrance. The twist in this fragrance is that there is a subtle hint of anise/licorice as the scent wears.  This scent is definitely worth a try for those who like oceanic fragrances and either like or are not offended by anise/licorice.

As a new fragrance launched after the updated EU regulations on the scent industry, this was developed strictly adhering to the new guidelines. Therefore this fragrance is exactly how it should be - exactly how the perfumer designed it to be.  In terms of wear, this fragrance lasts for most of the day.

product_title: Azzaro Azzaro Pour Homme Eau de Toilette Spray
review_text:
Before I really get into this cologne by Azzaro I feel there's a few comments to throw into the wind. For starters I don't think this would make an instant satisfier for someone that heard of it's past tense reputation but hasn't smelled it before. Speaking in terms of gift giving for Christmas or birthday present. Give 'em Drakkar Noir,Red For Men by Giorgio,Aramis EDT, or Halston 1-12(another personal favorite of mine).I love Azzaro EDT personally but as a herbal/spicy cologne if I was inquired about it in person I'd say 'how do you feel about anise'?.Still intrigued? well let's get to the bottom of this scent...

Azzaro's Scent:
Well it's lightly soapy for starters with a good hit of anise/black licorice that makes it spicy but not cloying. Spicy,semi-bitter,and lightly sweet. There's a nice minty like quality that fuses with the anise but it's actually the herb known as basil. Lastly there's a musky padding under all of this that sort of softens the edges out.

Has Azzaro EDT been watered down/weakened?
In my opinion no it has not nor do I consider it reformulated as it would be easy to detect in Azzaro's straightforward scent. Back when I started wearing Azzaro many years ago this was in a splash form in stores. Then over the years spray bottles replaced a lot of colognes in splash form. Through the spray bottle giving a noticeably smaller dose than a single hand splash I found Azzaro to be become mild unless I sprayed more. Someone's rebuttal might be 'well that's because it's cheap'.Take Safari for Men by Ralph Lauren-smells awesome and costs a little over twice as Azzaro. But Safari gives the same perception lightening to a low projection/close encounter as Azzaro's spray would...and always has. Every cologne's potency varies cheap or expensive but it shows some were just destined to come in a splash on form for the better.

Highly Recommended if you see it on a tester stand to give it a shot and not let the negativity fool you. If you're convinced and like Azzaro does make a 13.6oz size splash bottle too!

review_text:
I reported to Amazon that the product was FAKE.  The 5 star amazon CS promptly refunded me the money- no questions asked.

So why am I calling the product FAKE. I wanted to post a video review to explain the issue but I cannot do it for this product so here I will try to explain why the product was fake.
I always read reviews about the perfume not smelling right, not lasting long enough, etc as the reasons for calling them fake. But this is subjective and not a good test to distinguish original vs fake.  I will try to provide a more objective reasoning for my complaint.
1. When I opened the package, I noticed that the box of the perfume looked very very cheap. Designer houses may occasionally sell cheap product but they will always ensure that the packaging is top class.  Not the case with this product. The lettering looked a little smudged. Looked at the box more closely and there was black tape around the box, as well as a few patches at the bottom. Pulled the tape gently and the box was cut. Pulled out the patch tape and there was a small square cut as well.  At this point without even opening the box, I wrote to amazon to complain and they did issue a immediate refund.
2.  Went back to the box and decided to take the bottle out.  I have not seen the original Azzaro bottle but I can say that this bottle definitely looked cheap.  I then pressed the atomizer and it was a little hard to press it. Also the spray that came out was not even. It smelled ok but another indication that something is wrong with the bottle.
3. The packaging or the bottle again are not enough to call the perfume fake right. So lets get more objective. If you have ever purchased ANY perfume (forget designer brands), there is one unique thing that you will see on each packaging and the bottle. Every package will have a text ( combination of letter and numbers) imprinted on it . This is not a barcode but a unique identifier. The exact same number will be imprinted on the actual glass bottle as well. This way the bottle can be associated with the exact packaging. If they are missing, this is a sure indicator you have a fake product.  So on my package or the bottle this unique combination was missing all together. So there you go- the absolute test to know if the product is a fake.
4. If it is a tester, you will notice the word tester ( not just a sticker) on the bottle some where. In most cases it will be etched on the bottle but I would imagine different designer houses may do it differently.

If if your bottle fails test number 3  you are 100% sure that you have a fake product.

DO NOT HESITATE TO CALL AMAZON IF YOU HAVE SUSPICION. But do your due diligence  to ensure that  you were shipped a fake product.

review_title: A very fresh scent, Crabtree's replacement for India Hicks Island days
review_text:
CarIbbean Island Wild Flowers is Crabtree's replacement for India Hicks Island days which was my favorite among their scents for many years. They are similar, but not identical, with the florals more prominent in this scent and the citrus a little brighter in the other.  Of the two, I prefer the India Hicks, but, alas, it is no longer available.  They both remind me of the scents of the Caribbean (but the India Hicks more so).  It is a classic, very clean and fresh.  Some would classify this as a daytime or summer scent.  I wear it all the time, but then, I live on a tropical island where it is summer year-round.
I wound up at Amazon when I was shopping at Crabtree and they were either sold out, or do not carry this scent other than in their deluxe gift set.  I purchased the entire line, and so would likely have done as well to buy the gift set.  It is my favorite among their current scents, although the Heritage series is quite nice as well.  Our local Crabtree shut down some time ago, so we have  less access here in the islands. I am glad to see Amazon carrying this line, particularly since it is so difficult to get the Eau de Toilette directly from Crabtree.

If you are not sure if the scent is for you, try their little luxuries gift set, which has travel sized bottles of the shower gel, lotion and scrub.

product_title: English Laundry Arrogant Eau de Toilette, 1.7 fl. oz.
review_text:
English Laundrys, Arrogant, is a beautiful composition of notes where the end result is a masculine scent that leaves the user feeling clean and fresh.  I have five English Laundry fragrances in my collection and it is beyond me why there is not more positive attention and accolades given to this line. Out of the bottle, I get the lavender notes followed by the cedar and sandalwood finish, and agree with other reviewers there is a shared DNA between Arrogant and Le Male.  Arrogant is safe, office friendly, and while geared for more formal or business type engagements, it is wearable to most events across any season.  Performance is decent  Arrogant lasted greater than 7 hours on me, even longer on clothing, at arms length distance for the first 4 hours and at skin level thereafter.  As with the other fragrances in this line, the presentation of Arrogant is first class  English Laundry is at the top of designer fragrances for presentation.

All said, my final tally for Arrogant is 4.2 stars out of 5 stars.  If the projection/sillage were greater, Arrogant has Top 10 potential.  This fragrance smells great and is a best kept secret that exudes confidence and gentlemanly aura.  Further, Arrogant will be a welcomed addition to any collection and comes with a solid Love for the fragrantica following.  Enjoy your day and happy fragrance hunting.

review_title: A sophisticated scent in a nice presentation bottle
review_text:
As background, I rarely wear perfume, and prefer Bath and Body Works cream instead, but was intrigued by the description of this perfume.  Here's a description of the scent of this Juicy Couture Gold Couture Eau de Parfum according to the manufacturer:

Glamorous, Golden Composition

Viva La Juicy Gold Couture opens with luscious wild berry notes and deepens to a heart of sambac jasmine and honeysuckle. A sensual base of melted caramel, vanilla cream, praline, and sandalwood combine to create a warm finish.

Top: wild berries, gardenia, muguet

Mid: vanilla orchid, honeysuckle, and jasmine sambac

Bottom: sandalwood, melted caramel, vanilla cream, and praline

I really like this perfume, but I don't catch the top notes at all, primarily what I experience is the bottom notes of sandalwood, melted caramel and amber (which is not mentioned).  The scent is pronounced but not overpowering and lasts.  It is a sophisticated scent, not a bright floral or fruit.

The eau de perfume comes in a very heavy bottle that looks like it is lined in a gold foil.  The "crystal" on top is plastic.  All in all, it makes a nice presentation.

review_title: Don't Judge a Book By It's Cover
review_text:
My favorite fragrances tend to fall into two broad categories - rich oriental spices or masculine scents with notes of cedar, tobacco and/or leather.  Even in the summer, I don't gravitate toward lighter perfumes that are fruit or floral forward.  Therefore, I was hesitant to give this one a go, since the top note is berry.  But the list of base-notes (sandalwood, musk) intrigued me enough to go for it.

Upon first applying, the ultra-sweet berry is very prominent, which was a big turn-off.  To me, it smelled a bit juvenile and cheap.  But after a couple of minutes, it dried down to a very warm, sophisticated scent as the base-notes came to the front.  My husband commented that the fragrance was very sexy.  Plus it has real staying power (sillage, as it's called in the industry), which is a big selling point because even some of the most expensive perfumes can fade away after an hour or so.

My only real complaint is the packaging.  It's extremely gaudy - the gold bottle, the mesh bow and the pink plastic Juicy Couture logo - it's all a bit much.  But you can't always judge a book by it's cover.  This is an exceptional fragrance and a very good price.

review_text:
Overall, this is a good, bright perfume that isn't too sweet. Fortunately, unlike other Juicy Couture perfumes, it doesn't have overpowering sillage. In other words, you won't find yourself enveloped in an offensively strong, one-note smell.

When first applied, it has a strong, sharp smell that's disappointly like the cheap fake floral perfumes I avoid. However, it quickly calms to a warm, gently spicy floral with sandalwood and amber notes.

It lasts about four hours, and even then it isn't completely faded - just noticeably more difficult to pick up.

It's suitable (in my opinion) for day and evening wear. Because it isn't particularly sweet, it'll work for any age range, as well.

I'm very pleased and plan to wear it often. Definitely recommended.

review_text:
This has a pleasant scent. It is not too floral, and it does not have the strong alcohol-esque odor properties that is a turn off for me and can be found in many scents. It's a nice, somewhat sophisticated, and not typical for a "masculine" scent, so it may be appropriate for unisex.

Others have noted that this does not last long. I suppose this is true, but I could smell it for many hours. I am sensitive though, so this is probably different for different people.

I'm no connoisseur, but from what I can tell, this is was a good price for a product with this quality. I'd compare it with other varieties in the same price range at a department store.

The packaging is nice, too. I don't care, but some may!

Plus: My wife likes it.

review_title: This price? It cant be real but it is!
review_text:
Ive been looking for that right cologne for the last few years now, since I decided to move on from Abercrombie Fierce and smelling like a 20 year old walking through a mall. Im 33 now, and Jimmy Choo Man is hands down my favorite cologne. But at below $50 for a 3.3 oz. bottle on Amazon, my thought was it has to be fake. But, I feel very comfortable saying, the one I received is the real deal, and that was my biggest worry with this product at this price.

I did my homework, and even went as far as to walk into a beauty supply chain, asked them if I could compare the boxes, the bottles, and the scents, and they let me do so!

1. The Wrapping - the appearance of the plastic wrapping was on point. To be honest, mine looked a little better. Come to find out, they had an older batch, Ill get to that later. Essentially though, it looked like every other sealed box.

2. The Box - The box itself was the same. Same edges, same insides, same weight, same feel, same text, same everything! I didn't catch any misspellings, grammar, punctuation or other errors.

3. The Batch - Next, I went to checkcosmetic.net to check the batch number on my box. It said my cologne was produced in March 2015, which worried me a little at first. I then checked the batch number of the box at the store I was comparing with, that batch was produced in September 2014, which made me feel much better.

4. The Bottle  At first, I was concerned about the bottle. The top/molding seemed a little cheap, but when comparing to the other bottle, it was the exact same bottle. The bottle's shape, height, width, and design were all spot on. The primary label on the bottle, or the writing/font, was the exact same as well.

5. The Fragrance They smelled the same. After wearing samples of this cologne for the last week, then moving to this bottle I purchased, I can say they are one in the same. In regards to the fragrance itself, it is an Eau De Toilette, which apparently is only supposed to last approximately 2 - 3 hours. So while it isn't very long lasting at its peak strength, it does still provide those faint glimpses of smell throughout the day, so long as you wear it on all the right spots.

review_text:
From all the hype of the Jimmy Choo women's fragrances, I was tremendously excited to try the men's version.  Out of the bottle, I was impressed with the blend of fruit, patchouli, and suede notes.  Very nice.  Then the drydown - or better said - the "let down".  I get four (4) hours max longevity from Jimmy Choo with modest projection/sillage at arms length for two (2) hours. I have worn this fragrance twice, each providing the same results.  I will, however, admit the second use performed better in cooler weather and lasted longer on clothing.

Given the complexity of the notes, I would suggest that Choo does provide flexibility to be worn during any season and for most events.  It is definitely office safe for those with more sensitive noses.  With the hype of the fragrance, I do see Choo worn by a younger crowd and out "clubbing" (or whatever it is called these days - my "clubbing" days are long gone..!!).  Additionally, this fragrance is almost borderline unisex and I could definitely see that "daring" young lady pull this off, or perhaps layer with one of her favorite fragrances.

I do love the bottle - clear with a "smoky" finish and subtle curvature that is a nice touch.  The price is moderate and average for any designer fragrance - if you give it time, I am certain you will see it at discount department stores - just like the Choo women's editions.

A final tally for Jimmy Choo for Men is 4 stars out of 5 stars.  It is a very pleasant scent, but the performance is on the weak side.  I like it, but it falls short of loving it status.  If you are a collector and "want to join the crowd", pick it up and add to your increasing collection.  Otherwise, pass on Choo and "save it for a rainy day".

Enjoy your day and make it count.  Invest your time rather than wasting your time...

The scent isn't all that original; but it does have a very pleasant, clean smell.

The real problem is that is has no "holding power" . The life of this scent on the body and clothing is 2 hours maximum. I originally tried it lightly on the skin. Nice mix, but gone in an hour.
This morning I tried cotton clothing and the skin. In two hours it was gone.
Now, I don't look to overpower my coworkers or company for lunch. But I do expect a lingering fragrance to halo, or surround my body space. This had none a short two hours later.
All in all a very average experience for a plus $50.00 cologne.

review_title: I don't love the top notes, but give this one time -- it turns into something nice
review_text:
When I first put this on, I actually got a hint of fruitiness that I thought was a little strange (not unpleasant, but strange). However, after having had it on for most of the day, I am really liking it. (It did lose a bit of intensity so you may want to reapply partway through the day.)

The product page describes this as "solar oriental" and that's actually a really good description. This has the sandalwood and woody notes I love in fragrances but this just has the feel of a daytime fragrance. (I am really not noticing the salt at all, although maybe that was part of my initial impression and those notes have worn off? At any rate, I'm happy with what has stayed around after a few hours.) I don't really notice the peppery qualities, either, but that may be my body chemistry at work.

The bottle design is attractive but a little obnoxious. You have to twist the top pretty hard to get it off. But I like the fragrance quite a lot.

Please note that this item is flammable and can only be shipped via ground shipping methods, so it will take a longer time. Also, please note that it is probably not able to be returned. So if you are unsure if you like this, I would suggest trying to find a sample first. As of the time of this writing, Amazon is the seller. However, if a third party seller does add a listing and you plan to buy from them, check seller feedback before purchasing. A seller with good feedback is more likely to send you a genuine item. (Sadly, large bottles of designer perfumes are often counterfeited. So only purchase from trustworthy sources.)

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_title: Is this what sexy smells like?
review_text:
I need to preface this review with the fact that I hate all those floral 'LOUD' perfumes.  If you get headaches from certain scents then you can fully understand what I mean with my LOUD statement.

Now CK's Reveal is something different that I can't necessarily pin.  The bottle is a glass, rounded square shape with the uppper triangle portion being the lid.  The lid is a metallic goldish/silver that is a fingerprint magnet!  The scent is something different... as time wears, the scent subtly changes.

This is the type of perfume that should be labeled, 'Less is more'.  A simple short spritz on my wrist fills the room.  Right out of the bottle the scent smells peppery with a few masculine notes thrown in.  When I am in the Department stores I find myself drawn to the Men's section.  The frilly, floral Ladies department always gives me a headache.  This scent has that earthy, masculine, musky and at times, peppery aroma.  It's sexy, yet can be worn in a professional environment without overwhelming others.  When you first spritz, it is just too strong!  Given ample time it wears wonderfully.  I can't specifically nail all the nuances... peppery, powdery, ambergris ( is that the salty pick-up?) with a hint of Playdoh!  Personally the scent lasts 24 hours on my body, but by that time it has evolved into something completely different.  It is a wonderful little memory the next day when I open my eyes and catch a slight aroma.

Highly recommend if you are the type that loves masculine scents with peppery and salty undertones that isn't overtly flowery.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_title: Worth a Try......But How Would YOU Know
review_text: Reveal is a nice fragrance. It's musky with a hint of fruit, not heavy or overpowering. Sprayed on in the morning, it was still detectable hours later and was true to its original application, no degradation. Some perfumes have very distinctive notes and become signature scents. While Reveal is very pleasant, it didn't trigger immediate recognition each time I tried it during the review period. As a side note. I did a little research. Reveal is sold by a number of vendors but it's only available on line. I don't know about you, but I wouldn't invest in an expensive perfume if I didn't have a chance to try it first.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_text: This was a gift for my wife and I love it on her. She HATES anything floral so this passes that very important test because there is not a note of floral in this at all.  It is very a very concentrated parfum and a little bit is all you need. The primary notes that I pick up are a little salt, some pepper, vetiver and very sexy sandlewood in a nice musky finish. I love when she is getting ready for work in the morning and I catch a little drift of the Reveal on her just as she is ready to depart. I highly recommend!

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_title: Pleasantly peppery, not too floral (at first)
review_text:
I like this scent.

I got it because a few of the reviewers had mentioned the pepperiness of the scent. And on first spritz, I definitely agree. It's nag champay, It reminds me a bit of Fendi.

As the day wears on, it lingers (good) but it slowly became more floral (not so good for me). Of course, this is my body chemistry and finer parfums (and this is one of those) really have different scents on different people.

To me (and this is my odd scent brain) it started smelling like college and ended the day smelling of  preschool-teacher.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_text:
This Eau de Parfum presents the wearer with a host of contradictions.  It is light and airy for daytime, yet salty, spicy, and sensual enough for evening. It really is unusual and not like the other scents out there.

A great combination of sandalwood,  musk, salt, pepper, and flowers!

Even the "bottle" is unique and complex. Kind of reminiscent of one of those children's folded paper puzzles.  The presentation package is great- this would be a wonderful gift.

Like an interesting wine, this perfume is a bit of a conundrum-musky, salty, sweet, spicy- all at the same time.

Neither heavy nor cloying, this scent leaves a nice cloud of mystery in its wake.  The scent lasts a while, but is clean, crisp and not over-powering.

Highly recommended for that unique individual...................

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_text: My granddaughter found this product to be too strong.  She said it had a very heavy scent that smelled too much of musk and not enough of the described salts.  In fact she thought it was a scent for a male when she first smelled it.  Her opinion is that it rates about 3 Stars but that's the opinion of a 19 year old college girl so bear that in mind.  I also thought it was very strong but I kinda liked the scent and found it to be a bit titillating to say the least.  So if the opinion of an old guy counts I think it's sexy!!

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_text:
This Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum is just too strong for me.  I am not knowledgeable about perfumes at all so I can't tell you how this is formulated.  I can tell you that I smell a woody, deeply musky scent.  I put the first spritz on my left wrist at 1:00 in the afternoon and had to fight the urge to go wash it off.  However, I left it alone and about three hours later it had settled down enough that I could smell other scents instead of just the perfume.  Somewhere around 9:00 it was giving me a nice background scent which I liked, but it was still easily noticed when I went to bed at 11:00.  The next morning I could still smell the fragrance, but it was gone after my shower.  Personally I know any perfume that takes hours to dissipate enough for me to be able to enjoy it is not going to work for me.  Each person's body chemistry reacts differently with a fragrance so I would highly recommend you get a spray of this at a perfume counter and wear the scent for a few hours before you decide whether or not to purchase it.

Several days later I decided to try again, only this time I wouldn't spray it on myself.  I just wanted to study the scent so I folded a facial tissue into a small square and sprayed that.  Over three days later I can still smell the perfume on that folded tissue.  My office smells like REVEAL parfum.

The design of the container looks wonderful.  Unfortunately, getting the top off is something of a struggle and then holding the bottle in order to push the atomizer down is not easily done. It looks lovely sitting on my dressing table, though.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_title: Wanted to like this, but cannot
review_text:
I wanted to like this, I really did.  The description sounded intriguing, and I love scents with pepper and sandalwood as notes.  The bottle is interestingly shaped, and holds a generous amount of scent.

I open the package, remove the rounded square bottle, take off the cap and spray lightly in the air, walking through the mist.  I smell nothing but generic CK scent-vaguely artificial and synthetic.  A few minutes later I begin to get a headache.  I try again the next day, and the same thing happens.  It lingers on clothing and the skin, lasting through a shower, or several days in the closet (some spray got on a sweater).  I let my daughter try it, and thank goodness she went to school shortly after, as even on someone else it was triggering a headache.

I am glad that so many people like this scent, it just is not for me.  I cannot give it to my daughter to use, unless I want to move out of my house.  I will dispose of this as soon as I am able.

review_text: When my wife first applied this, we both thought is was far too string.  However, after a few minutes it seemed to settle down and really is an interesting scent. product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_text: This perfume, from bottle to scent, is very attractive both to wearer and to people admiring it. That is saying a lot about it, because I am not a fan of the majority of scents out there. The bottle has an simple design that is both elegant and colorful, with the upper half's metallic gold offsetting the bottom's glass-and-perfume display. It looks very attractive under good lighting, adding something to countertops while accenting modern amenities. The bottom is also weighted well so it sits upright with ease and I do not worry about it getting cracked by the occasional "oopsy." As for the smell, I like the way "woods" or "warm woods" seems to capture it. It has a springtime scent that is a bit floral without being too flowery and goes on light, does not overpower ,and stays for a while. I like the way this compliments people at work or going out, too, and think this works as an everyday scent.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum

My daughter's review; Lovely scent! I think the "warm woods" describes it best for me. Scent, like taste, is subjective so although I enjoyed the scent my mother said "it smells like man" haha. I think it cooould smell like man if it was worn on a man but I think other human beings accept this as a feminine scent when I wear it. product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_title: A solar Oriental, enigmatic - starts salty then turns musky. Love it.
review_text:
The bottle is so beautiful, that I was drawn to it the first time I saw it at a store. However, I realized it's not a great design for everyday use, but still pretty.

Calvin Klein has managed to churn so many successful perfumes that they made them smell generic. I want to hate them as they're so popular but I can't find anything to hate about most of them! Everyone wears a Calvin Klein perfume at one point. Obsession was an obsession when I was a teenager, and Eternity, One, and Euphoria are very pleasant fragrances from the same house. And I can name so many others I've used in the past. I thought Reveal would be another Euphoria Lite, but it's really not.

I would classify Reveal as a Fall/Winter perfume for the Day melding into evening. This scent is deceptively unassuming at first but grows on you as you wear it and then, you're hooked. I would still wear it in the Summer but at or after sunset rather than in the day time.

The perfume is called a solar oriental, designed to be like a second skin almost. When the sun is out the skin smells of salt and as the light fades the skin takes on a sandalwoody and musky tone. This perfume mimics that natural scent of skin. Reveal is an apt name as the perfume tends to evolve slowly over time but is never overpowering.

The top notes are raw salt, pink pepper, white pepper, and black pepper, revealing a salty earthiness and spiciness. At first whiff, it almost smells like a male fragrance as it is more salty and subtly spicy and woodsy than floral.

The middle notes are Orris and Ambergris. Ambergris used to be thought of as sperm whale vomit but now it is known to be whale excrement. The whales imbibe the sea flavor and release them as highly prized ambergris - it is said to release pheromones and have aphrodisiac properties and makes perfumes longer lasting. Orris root has a similar fixative property.

The base notes are sandalwood, cashmeran, vetiver and musk. All very warm and sensual notes that make the dry down smell like a second skin but so much more pleasing.

This is an expertly crafted fragrance with less drama and fanfare like some others, but still sensual and feels closer to a natural scent. I cannot wear many heavy vanilla and flowery perfumes close to my skin as they give me a headache, but I was able to spray Reveal on pulse points and it smelled great, wafting gently rather than cloying and sweet.

It is fairly long lasting due to the presence of musk and sandalwood but for me that is just 3-4 hours, and the sillage is moderate. That's why I will use it as a day or early evening perfume rather than late night.

There are some perfumes you simply can't sniff from the bottle, you have to try them on your skin and sniff at it over a few hours to understand its true colors. Reveal is that type of a perfume and it has the potential to become a favorite.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_title: This Spicy -  but Short-lived - Scent Crosses Gender Lines
review_text:
Calvin Klein Reveal has a scent much like CK One Eau de toilette: spicy overtones with no herb elements and no florals.  As such, it's rather unisex and quite attractive.

But it is not long-lasting, thus 4/5 stars.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_title: Attractive Pillowy Bottle And A Pretty and Unique Fragrance That Reveals Its Nuances When Applied  Lightly
review_text: I love the presentation- The bottle looks like a pretty, soft, elegant pillow. While at first I wasn't jumping for joy over the fragrance, as it has faded some over time I have a completely different opinion. While perfume smells different on everyone, on me the nuances in Reveal emerge more and smell better with a light application and after it's had an hour or so to fade.  When first sprayed, Reveal smelled very sweet and powdery with a woodsy or musky scent on me, not my favorite combo. But as some time passed, I could smell the lightly sweet (not spicy) scent of peppercorns with a hint of floral, powder and what I think is sandalwood, and it's really pretty and not overpowering like it was when first applied. I don't smell sea salt, but the fragrance is complex as it mixes a variety of scents that might not normally be combined and doesn't fall into a precise category, such as floral, musk, spice, etc. The longer I wear it and it fades some, the more the nuances of the fragrance come through and the more I like it. I think it's pretty and recommend it, but definitely a lighter application is better as I think the nuances of the fragrance are "revealed" more when not applied too heavily.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_text: My wife had not heard of this perfume before, so she didn't know what to expect; trying it out was sort of a gamble.  In a word, she was pleasantly surprised (I was too!).  She really likes it because it is sweet (but not too sweet like a teenage girl's perfume) and flowery (but not too flowery like perfume for an older woman).  She says it's not overpowering, but is easy to smell (sort of a nice "light" scent if that makes sense).  Anyway, she's glad she got it (so am I!) and she recommends it (so do I!).

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_text: Calvin Klein has done it again. REVEAL is perfect. I absolutely love it. Somehow the combination of pink peppercorns, salt(!), floral, and then woodsy is just perfect. This scent is totally unique and totally captivating. It is definitely a scent that will appeal to the young, as well as the young at heart. It is great for daytime as well as evening wear. I appreciate that it is long lasting, and the unique design of the bottle captures the essence of the perfume perfectly! REVEAL is a scent for a woman that any man will definitely appreciate. Enjoy!

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_title: Pleasant smell that stays all day.
review_text:
I ordered this perfume not sure if it was for a man or a woman based on the description.  Im happy to say, it is a womans perfume so I got lucky since that was what I was hoping for.

I realize liking or disliking a smell is a very personal thing, but I really like this.  It is kind of a combination of sweet, light floral, and musk.  Now, let me say, usually as soon as I see the word musk I head the other direction, but combined with the other scents, it is very pleasant.

This perfume has staying power too.  I squirt one squirt on my shirt in the morning and it is still very much there when I take the shirt off to go to bed.  Honestly, this probably has more staying power than any perfume Ive ever owned.  I think this might be a perfume that would be easy to overdo just because the scent doesnt dissipate much at all throughout the day.
Overall, Im very pleased with the product and would most definitely recommend it.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_title: A very different sort of fragrence
review_text:
To give this a bit of perspective, my favorite scents are all the sweet ones.  Channel #5 is a great favorite.  If you love that, you won't love this.  If you think that's too flowery, too girly, not right for today's woman, you may well adore this.

It's not at all like a normal perfume.  The initial impact, when it as its strongest, smells like vomit.  It's horrible.  After a few minutes that fades and you get a kind of spicy musk, almost like a feminine variation on a man's cologne.  Then you get the more subtle layers of sandlewood and spice.  It is a very sophisticated, very different scent.  It takes a bit to get used to.  I would not debut this at an important event.  Try it first, because it is not for everyone.  And definitely give it time to settle down before going out in public with it.

I would give it five stars but for the first few minutes after putting it on.  I know perfumes are always a bit overwhelming initially, but this was far worse than I've ever experienced before.

product_title: Calvin Klein REVEAL Eau de Parfum
review_text:
This is NOT the usual Calvin Klein fragrance.  In fact, this fragrance is downright different from pretty much all fragrance on the market.  It has a very salty and peppery scent - salty as in sea salt to my nose - that briny ocean scent. Then there is a very big cashmeran wood & sandalwood that lasts the entire way thru.  There is also a powdery/musk undertone but it is not too strong.

I really did not like this the first time I tried it - that sea salt was funky in a bad way to my nose.  I tried it again after I smelled it in the air on someone else - it smelled good; I recognized it immediately & once I got home I sprayed again.  It was better but I don't think this is really my kind of scent.  But I have a large sample, so will try again....maybe it will grow on me. :)  I tend to like more white flower scents but I also like to explore & try new things.

Sillage is arm length & beyond so go easy with the spray.  This lasts about 8 hours on my skin.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray
review_text:
I'm not an overly experienced scent wearer. I wore different stuff in the 80s (Drakkar, Givenchy, the original Fahrenheit, even Poisson (it was a new wave thing...don't ask why...)), but during the 90s and new millenium I just couldn't be bothered, so I'm waaay out of the loop here. Sandalwood essential oils and shaving soap, Pinaud Clubman aftershave, that aging (beautifully, by the way) bottle of classic Polo, these were the extent of how I might smell on any given day, if I could be bothered. I grabbed a bottle of this on the recommendation of a few sites. I wanted a classic yet modern scent that might be talked about in a GQ forum, but not a scent raved about on some pop site, dedicated to kids getting laid (sorry). I can't bring myself to wear anything with a rapper's name on it, or the stuff they push at Macy's (ie. Play..."Oh, Justin Timberlake is on the advert"...Well, I run screaming from that image, regardless of the whiff the stuff gives off.)

So I tested the Artisan, and immediately loved it. I was wandering the Barnes and Noble's wondering: should I go back to buy this? No one ever commented on it. Sometimes I smelled it, sometimes I didn't (and this is still true). I felt haunted like I was waiting for an evening rain storm to pass, here in the Northwest, and she hadn't gotten here yet, and the Spring blossoms are falling, filling the air with the ingredients for a nostalgia moment for some future recall. So this stuff caught my attention. I'm glad I didn't wait longer before going back to buy it. It does, as has been noted, seem to fade to gone in an hour or two. Had I realized that, I might have decided against it.

To whit: it doesn't last long, yet it does. I noticed it smelling better, lasting longer and feeling more present after several days of wearing it, because, I think, but don't know or understand how, the cologne in the straw at packaging was used up, and fresher stuff going out of the pump seemed to stay with me more. Is this a cologne phenom I am unaware of? I guess I'd say to the people who don't like it cuz it fades too fast to use it till they've replenished the straw inside. Maybe you'll like it better. My son texted me from his school to say a girl thought he had a nice "vanilla" scent hours after spritzing the Artisan (there's no vanilla in this, so I don't know which note he was getting, but it's cool like that). The next day, I felt my spritzes started to last better.

Maybe, also, this cologne is designed to be an answer to the cloying Axe sprays and Dude colognes, the ones that reeeek!!! of sweat. It's like having your still hunky grandfather telling you to ditch the (insert kid cologne here) and use Artisan. I think Brad Pitt would wear this if he were making"Benjamin Buttons II: Old Again" and he was riding his retro Indian into the sunrise. I think it's a softer take on classic man-scents. In a category like Acqua di Parma in that it's manly, yet reveals a complex, feminine side. I feel like I need to soap-shave and grab my ooolllddd Woolworth sweater that smells like the closet in order to be ready for the subtlety and maturity of this cologne. It's supposed to fade to nostalgia quick. It's for you in brief bits (no matter how much you spray, sorry  4 spritzes still faded, so leave it at two, I think, and maybe carry a girly atomizer to refresh if she calls you up, but you may not need it. It's still there, you can barely tell); it's for that special someone who gets close enough to whisper in your ear. They'll like it, I think, so who cares if your bros didn't notice!

This is good for second dates, Manly men who want to cast themselves in a softer light, gay men who want a masculine smell, women who want to confuse people a little. In short, I think it's great, possibly unisex, and I can't wait to see how the bottle smells in five years. I bet that's an important secret to this cologne, but I don't know enough.

This stuff is pure gold. On the spectrum, it's got an overall aquatic feel to it, and the dry-down is fantastic. Supple enough to wear all day (though it shines the best during the day), but strong enough to stand out. The scent has a voice, but nothing about it is overpowering. This scent says something and makes itself known. The balance of the ginger, citrus and georgywood is superb and carry much of the heart of the scent, while the notes of thyme, belambe and lavadin are on the upswing and provide the suppleness that allows this scent to carry you through the day.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Eau de Toilette Spray
review_text:
Cologne's different on everyone, so please take my experience with a grain of salt.

  To me, Artisan starts off with a kick of citrus to your face; it feels like someone ripping open a box of mandarin oranges and freshly-crushed thyme right underneath your nose upon first application.  It's juicy, and strong.

  After a few minutes, Artisan evens out with a pleasing floral note (orange blossoms, as I'm told), and you catch hints of aromatic wood and sweet musk.  Sadly, this fades away within an hour or two, and the cologne no longer projects.  If you move in close, you'll detect a feint whiff of what it once was (it smells as if someone lightly dabbed orange peel and vanilla on your skin).

  At $78 retail for the 4.2 oz bottle (I purchased Artisan from a department store), this kills Artisan as a likable product for me.  As other users have alluded, you're paying to get teased.  To find the silver lining, I'd recommend Artisan for short term use, in occasions such as walks on the beach, coffee dates, a trip to the store, etc.  To note, I've also had better longevity with Artisan in warmer climates.

  All in all, if the makers manage to extend the longevity and projection of Artisan, I'd be a lifetime customer.  As is, however, I'm sticking with another cologne as my primary, and will toss my bottle of Artisan out, along with any attachment to it, as soon as occasion allows for it to run out.

review_text:
I consider myself a bit of a fragrance snob, and I was pleasantly surprised by this scent. Frequently, I find that the chemical compounds used to mimic white florals in fragrance are irritating, which is a telltale sign of a poor quality. Thankfully, I don't get irritation from this scent. In fact, I quite like it. It is neutral enough to wear to the office but unique enough to be recognized.

Although it appears to be marketed to women, I think a fragrance-daring gent could easily pull this off. The top citrus notes and middle floral notes are quite fleeting in my opinion. Not really a true floral scent, in my opinion, and on the order of D&G Light Blue but better.

review_text:
I'm super picky when it comes to floral perfumes, but this one? Hits it out of the park. Cote d'Azur is a deliciously beachy floral with strong hints of citrus and a really lovely, rich base of sandalwood and amber.

At first spritz, when the perfume is still wet, citrus is the strongest note; it smells like fresh lemon and orange peel. Immediately upon drydown, the florals take over. I mostly smell jasmine and tuberose. Underneath, though, is that nice, warm base of sandalwood and amber. The base isn't too strong, though it gets stronger the longer the perfume sits on my skin.

Throw is low to medium; my very scent sensitive husband just caught a light whiff of it as I walked past him. It's more of a private perfume rather than a perfume that lets everyone in the room know about it. On my skin, it lasted fairly well, though it did fade after a few hours. Applying the perfume over lotion helps with its staying power, though.

Overall, this is a gorgeous floral and one I plan on wearing all summer.
