product_title: ORIBE Cote d'Azur Eau de Parfum, 1.7 fl. oz.
review_text:
This sample came to me in my Janurary Birchbox.  Now I am not really one that goes all out with perfumes.  I am more or less kinda a body spray kinda girl.  I have always found perfumes to smell more grandma like and don't really offer the lighted scent that I prefer.

Needless to say I was very hesitant to pull the cap off this little tube and take a whiff.  However, when I did, I was surprised at the light and fresh scent!

Since I do share the monthly suscription boxes with my two teenage daughters, I offered them a whiff.  Both girls declined, and stated it was too much for them.  So of course I gladly excepted ownership of this particular sample.

The following morning, after I took my morning shower, rather than using my choice of body spray from Bath & Body Works, I opted to apply this parfum.  I put a slight dab under the jaw line and on my wrists and gave myself a small little sniff on the wrist.  Again, I received the light and fresh fragrence that I experienced right out of the bottle.

I went about my morning chores about the home.  You know the routine, unloading the dishwasher and reloading it (have three teenagers in the house I am constantly doing dishes in the morning! For some reason they think they need to eat all night long! Oh, and we will not discuss how many cups are used on a daily basis!).  I started my daily laundry, swept up the floor, checked my Elite Deals and headed out to the barn for the morning feeding.

While outside, feeding the goats, chickens and rabbits I decided to take a bit to do a bit of cleaning up.  Animals can be quite messy!  I spent about an hour or so cleaning out some rabbit cages and mucking the goat's stall.  Leave it to me to take a shower first thing in the morning to freshen up and on a whim decide to muck out stalls and get filthy!

Now, even though it was about 25 degrees outside, I worked up quite a good sweat while cleaning up.  And I came back in the house planning on taking yet a second shower!  My hubby who is currently working a closing shift was up and about at that time doing his morning/afternoon prework ritual.  I had gone about and done a few more things around the house deciding to wait to reshower until after he has gone to work.  He had come up to me while I was taking a minute to rest, for his morning snuggle.  Gave me a kiss on the cheek and said, "hmm, you smell nice."

I have to admit I did give him a perplexed look, as I had just cleaned the barn!  I knew I most likely smelled like a combination of sweat, rabbits and goats.  How can that smell nice?  After he had walked away, I had taken a sniff of the wrists and sure enough I could still smell the parfum I applied right after my shower!  I was surprised that this scent lasted over the sweating from working in the barn, and still could be detected over what I felt, was the over powering scent of goat and rabbit that I assumed I smelled like after cleaning!  Needless to say, I was a bit impressed!

Now, as I have stated in the begining, I am not a big Perfume type of gal.  But I am impressed with this one.  To purcahse this scent in a large bottle is about $95.00, plus your shipping costs.  Will I purchase this after my sample runs out?  I honestly do not see paying that much for a scent, but I am frugal in that way.  Therefore I will use my sample sparingly, on special occasions (Not for mucking the parn!)  Perhaps on date night since the hubby likes it so much!

However, for those who do enjoy perfums with a light and fresh scent, I would highly reccomend this one!  The scent is long lasting and stays with you, even if you think you smell like a barn!

review_title: Imagine a forest and an orange grove, at the ocean
review_text:
First I had to look up "Guaiac Wood," as this is apparently the "top note" in this fragrance.

Apparently, this is is a small tree, also known as guayacan, whose wood has been used for centuries by Native Americans in treating various ailments. Apparently, it adds a "smokey note" and has "phenolic notes."

What "phenolic notes" means, I had no idea. Phenols are found naturally in foods (apples, bananas, oranges, cocoa), but they are also byproducts of fires and other combustions (burning tobacco, etc.). Some phenols are endocrine disruptors; some aren't.  This site can explain all the terms used in the world of fragrance:

http://perfumeshrine.blogspot.com/2012/02/definition-terpenic-phenolic.html

Now, on to what I do know -- that is, my very subjective reaction to the scent.

I wouldn't know exactly which citrus describes the top note -- lemon, lime, grapefruit, keffir lime, or bits of all four, with a bit of licorice thrown in. But it strikes me as definitely citrusy as the "top note" with grassy mid notes and smokey/woody bottom notes. Somewhere there is enough "sea note" to remind me of Acqua di Gio.

It's a nice solid container -- a navy-blue glass cube, with the side and back panels overlaid with red, white, and blackwith a spray. (I think I'd prefer a non-spray; easier to control.)

Anyway, for the last 30 years or so, I've been unable to tolerate commercial fragrances. Even the "top quality." I get sneezy, my throat closes, eyes itch, etc.  With other types of allergies (such as to our biohazard of a pine tree) somewhat resolved in recent years, I thought I could give the green light to my husband to again try wearing a bit of cologne without making me sick.  (Some types of fragrances gave him headaches, too, and no one wears cologne where he works, in a science lab, so it's not like going without has been a big imposition.)

So, I sprayed a bit of this LIVE fragrance on my shirt, as a test. I love the scent; it's very fresh and evocative of the outdoorsif a forest and citrus grove were situated at the ocean.

I sprayed it yesterday, and the scent is still in evidence this morning. So, there is "staying power."

Unfortunately, it wasn't long before I started feeling the physical effects. Not rancorous sneezing or eye-watering but more subtle nose stuffiness and "tight" throat. Not everyone will have this reaction, so it's not fair to downgrade the cologne for that. Still, I wonder why I largely don't have this reaction to good essential oils but I do to commercial fragrances.

product_title: Lacoste L!VE Gift-Wrapped Eau de Toilette for Men, 3.3 fl. oz.
review_text:
Bit on the musky side for my liking.

Full disclosure: I have an unnatural love for Acqua di Gio. Its citrusy notes make me so happy. I love sandalwood, jasmine, and orange. A bit of spicy fragrance is cool too. It's why I've loved Gio for so long. When I saw that this fragrance is in the citrusy side, I was happy to give it a shot. Also, bear in mind that I don't wear fragrance every day, because I enjoy cooking, and you don't want anything to interfere with the smell of the food.

According to the marketing notes for L!ve, it's meant to hit you with lime at the forefront, and then bring out green notes of leaves in the background. That's fine by me. Guess what I didn't get? Lime. Leaves. What I did get is this overwhelming musky smell, which I dislike. Axe body spray grosses me out. I hate the stuff, and damn near every teenage boy I know bathes in the stuff.

L!ve has a strong musk to it. The musk overpowers the citrus, the leaves, and the liquorice that was promised. That said! It does have a sweetness to the edges of the scent which is rather nice. There's also a ground note of earthiness rather than freshness. Why is this good? It covers the smell of sweat rather handily. Other fragrances, that tend towards the lighter, more airy side tend to clash with the natural scent of the body, and will be jarring. If you're one of those types that sweats a lot, L!ve is your jam. It's got serious staying power. One spray (AND NO MORE) is enough to last throughout the work day, and leave a little bit of lingering fragrance at the end of the day. Don't do more than one spray, or you'll be consumed by the scent. It's better to have it be subtle than something that people can smell before you show up.

Bear in mind that this is eau de toilette, which means that it's not going to be as strong as an eau de parfum. Generally, it'd mean that you'd need to put more on to get the effect. Not the case here. The fragrance is strong, and has plenty of staying power.

Why did I not rate this lower? Because it does grow on you over time. Throughout the day, I noticed that it mellowed out from the harsh muskiness that I got when I first put it on. And, as a product goes, it's not a bad product. It just doesn't live up to the promises it makes.

Coming in at 100ML, it's technically airline compliant, however fitting it into a single quart bag with other items is not going to be easy.  It's dimensions are 2.5" in a perfect square with the sprayer about an inch tall from the center top consists of a very thick and heavy glass.  It's a little awkward to hold in your hand and spray effectively and if the gentlemen has smaller hands, it may require two hands to spray straight, but it has a simple classic look to it.  If you're looking for something to travel easily with, this is not the best option.  Other than that, it's a great scent I would highly recommend for men.

review_title: I don't even like cologne, but I LOVE this stuff!!!
review_text:
For a guy who doesn't wear cologne, I was utterly shocked at how much I loved this one.
-
See, I used to wear Agua Lavanda by Puig.  It was Frank Sinatra's favorite cologne.  Unfortunately, they stopped making it.  Or at least, I can't find it online, and believe me, I know where to look!  I've been looking for years for a replacement.  But there's so much terrible garbage out there - I simply hate most colognes.  Drakkar Noir, Polo, oh man kill me now those are all so horrible!!!
-
But enter Lacoste L!VE.  I had ZERO hopes for this stuff.  1) I've never liked the Lacoste clothes.  I remember as a kid all the preppy guys wore the polo shirts with the little crocodile on them.  My family was too poor to afford name-brand stuff, so I was teased for that.  2) I hate most colognes.  They all seem so overwhelming it's just unbearable.
-
This might be my favorite cologne, ever.  It's a wonderfully light and refreshing scent.  Citrusy / little woodsy with a hint of musk - it's truly the ideal cologne for a man.  I love it!  It's amazing for me and I can't recommend it enough!
-
The bottle is pretty cool.  It's a spray, which I'm not a fan of - I'm old school - I like to splash it on.  But it's not too much when you spray so it's OK.  It does fine by me!  The bottle itself is a chunky cube, with these white inserts on each side.  Different enough to stand out amongst your bathroom garbage and say "hey, look at me - I ROCK".
-
Get this stuff.  Smell good, and be happy.

product_title: Lacoste L!VE Gift-Wrapped Eau de Toilette for Men, 3.3 fl. oz.
review_title: LaCoste LIVE - it smacks of class
review_text:
LaCoste LIVE eau de toilette for men is made in the United Kingdom. It arrives in a unique blue square bottle and smacks of class  packaged to serve as a gift. It is not very strong and can pass for an expensive aftershave.

It is fine with me that cologne begins firmly but fades as the day progresses. That way it does not repel those who dislike them all together. This fragrance will do just that. It invites a smile from others as I walk by.

product_title: Lacoste L!VE Gift-Wrapped Eau de Toilette for Men, 3.3 fl. oz.
review_text:
This is a very nice clean, masculine fragrance. Despite being female, I've long preferred male or unisex fragrances because those marketed to females are often too sweet and flowery.

This one reminds me of Benetton's Colors divided by Axe. Axe is still my favorite, but this is one that I don't mind using. It's a little strong at first, but becomes more subtle as the day goes on.

As someone who appreciates good design, I also like the bottle's design. I'm not in love with the red, white, and blue color scheme (would have preferred earth colors or monochrome), but the square bottle design is cool.

product_title: Lacoste L!VE Gift-Wrapped Eau de Toilette for Men, 3.3 fl. oz.
review_text:
This cutely packaged, square bottle cologne has a very after-shave scent quality. It's not revolutionary and will smell familiar to most men, without being overwhelming like so many of today's body sprays. It's soapy and spicy and I actually really liked it. It had sort of a retro Old Spice-Zest Clean scent to it that doesn't scream HE'S WEARING COLOGNE! Just light, cool and fresh and, to my nose anyway, altogether pleasant.

At two squirts in the morning, I liked that I could smell it on him if I was within hugging distance even at the end of the day, but not from across the room. Definitely something I'd be happy to have my husband wearing regularly. He said he liked it to, and actually got a few compliments throughout the day and I've noticed he's used it several times since. (And he's not someone who usually wears cologne outside of "special occasions.")

The high quality exterior packaging -- a square box with ribbon handles -- and the chunky, square bottle also make this imminently suitable for gift-giving; there's even a snow-covered mountain motif that could make it a really nice Christmas stocking stuffer.

review_text: I think I have found a new favorite summer cologne!  Its tough for me to find a good summer scent.  I don't like "fresh" scents as I don't feel like smelling like an air freshener.  I cannot carry off citrus or other fruity scents either.  Burberry Brit Rhythm Intense is spicy but also crisp and clean. review_title: First time I have smelled anything like this.  Smells better/lighter as time goes on.  Definitely manly.
review_text:
I admit, I can't figure this scent out. I kept trying to find what the smells make me think of, and I suppose light musk  white a hint of citrus is what resonates with me.  From what I have read on another website, this is how they describe the smell, "Top notes are basil, verbena, cardamom and juniper berries; middle notes are leather, patchouli and styrax; base notes are cedar, incense and tonka bean.".  I suppose that could be correct, it is unlike any scent my husband has and I am hoping he will like it.  Of course, I have to like it too, which I do, but I don't think I love it.  I imagine it will smell different when he wears it, so overall I feel  it is pleasant.  It is not a cloying, thick cloud of odoriferous scent.  I also find it interesting in comparing  how the eau de toilette smell is described, and to what  ingredients are in it, and they are: Alcohol Denat. (SD Alcohol 39-C), Water, Fragrance, Limonene, Linalool, Sutyl Metroxydienenzylmethane, Benzyl Salicylate, Coumarin, Alpha Isomethyl Ionone, Hexyl Cinnamal, BHT, Citral, Citronellol, Geraniol, CI 60730 (Ext. Voilet 2), CI 19140 (Yellow 5), CI 17230 (Red 33).

I had my oldest teenage daughter smell it and she didn't really know how to describe it either, but she found it like-able also.  I have a bottle of the essential oil of patchouli, so I compared it to that, and I can see a slight similarity, but thankfully the Burberry smells better than plain patchouli. And for the price, it better.  My other daughter could still smell the cologne a few hours after I spray tested it and she said it was "okay".  Kids these days!

In all this is a unique smell for me, and will round out his collection of colognes.  The bottle is quite fancy and manly too.

review_title: Pedestrian scent with the well to do mans pricetag.  If you're considering it, make sure you try it first.
review_text:
Maybe this doesn't mix well with my skin chemistry, I tried it on hand, cheek, neck and chest, with poor results.  I was surprised with the description which is smoky leather, I envisioned cowboys at a camp fire.  I didn't get that out of it, the first was mostly a rubbing alcohol smell then a strong hint of citrus, then sort of a musk.  The musk was not bad, but not enough to pay 80 buck for even a bottle this large.  Stick with the cheaper brands, this is a pedestrian scent with a CEO's price.

The bottle is nice and the sprayer top does a nice job spraying it on, but I think you can get a bottle of something as good for in the 10-15 dollar neighborhood.  Maybe its me or men in general, having the opportunity to try these was fine, but I could never see me spending this kind of money unless it were something special.  I reviewed a Calvin Klein fragrance recently that I could almost say that about, but it either worked better with my chemistry or it was just better period.  I can't recommend this, but if you think you'd like a citrus musk type scent, Try it out at a high end mall store where they might display that, if you can honestly say you like it, and you don't mind dropping eighty bucks on mens scents, go for it.

review_title: Way to intensely strong for me.
review_text: I wanted to like this cologne, but it's way too intense for me. No pun intended. It is not one of those scents where you can just apply it very sparingly and be fine. It is a knock you out from across the room strength intensity. Not good. The scent itself is not bad, it could be pleasant if it were only 1/4 as strong. Thank goodness I sprayed a testing spritz into the box it came in, rather than on myself. This is literally unwearable in my opinion. I know colognes are a very personal preferrence so I'll list several that I use which might be of help to you in determining whether this scent is for you. Regardless, please go try it in a store before making a "blind" purchase. Colognes I enjoy are: Euphoria and Encounter by Calvin Klein, Blue by Marc Ecko, Gio by Georgio Armani, All American Stetson, and Voyage by Nautica.

review_text: To me, this scent is tart and a little fruity, kind of like I remember fresh figs tasting, but it also has a clean edge so it's more sophisticated than some body spray you'd find at the mall. When it dries on my skin it takes on a deeper note, a bit like clover or something slightly noir, which I love. It is strong though--in my opinion a little overpowering, so I think I would prefer the lighter Eau de Toilette version (Eau de Parfum is always stronger). The rollerball bottle has its benefits and drawbacks. On one hand, it can be safely carried in a purse without the threat of the cap coming off and the perfume spilling. The cap screws on tight and the ball holds the fluid in. But, because the ball rolls through the perfume onto your skin, over time it picks up debris that floats in the bottle and can't be removed. Little tiny bits of dead skin, I think. So if that disgusts you I'd just get a traditional spray bottle.

product_title: Juicy Couture Hollywood Royal Eau de Toilette
review_text:
I've tried a few Juicy perfumes now and I've generally liked them.  This one is no exception!

It is definitely fruity at first (the top notes are listed elsewhere as apple, pear, and pomelo), but that mellows out later on.  After a few hours, I am left mostly noticing a bit of musk and vanilla (two of the base notes).  Since my favorite fragrances are musky, I'm happy with this.  (The middle notes are several different florals.  I think they blend well with everything else but aren't super noticeable with my body chemistry.)  I have to say, it's rare that I like a perfume at all points in time, but I like the fruitiness at first and I also like the musky/vanilla scent later.  It's also rare for a fragrance description to match exactly what happens with my body chemistry, but here it does!

The scent lasts about half a day but then needs to be reapplied.  This is about average performance, for me, for similar types of products.

Please note: Check seller feedback carefully before making a purchase, because large bottles of designer fragrance are sometimes counterfeited.  (Good seller feedback is an indication that people are happy with the seller, and therefore also an indication that the product you receive is likely to be genuine.)  Also note that this is a flammable liquid and can only be shipped ground, so it will take longer to arrive and returns will probably not be accepted.  Please plan your orders accordingly.

In the end, I'm very happy with this fragrance and will definitely buy it again soon.

product_title: BURBERRY Brit Splash Eau De Toilette, 3.3 Fl. oz.
review_text:
I have an immense collection of fragrances, with a particular interest in sporty scents such as Lacoste Essential and Nautica Voyage, and I've been very pleased with Burberry Brit Splash for the past week or so.  It's a nice, watery, summer, fresh smell that doesn't scream frat boy or Axe cheap.  It's a fine blend of scents that also doesn't overpower anyone within nasal range as many fragrances, such as anything by Ed Hardy or Axe, wreak of cheap ingredients and overpowering musk that can only be described as machismo.

I am very satisfied with how Burberry Brit Splash smelled on me and the pleasant reactions of those around me and will continue to wear it on the appropriate occasions.

product_title: BURBERRY Brit Splash Eau De Toilette, 3.3 Fl. oz.
review_text: If you're looking for a light, clean scent, Burberry is definitely a must try. The bottle is very easy to look at, nice design with the spray atomizer easy to use. Just a small amount lasts for hours.  It has a woodsy, vanilla, clean scent (to me) but I'm sure it will smell a bit different on anyone as it works with your own body.  My son wore it to work and had many, many people tell him how good he smelled.  Not his normal scent but one he would definitely purchase in the future.

product_title: BURBERRY Brit Splash Eau De Toilette, 3.3 Fl. oz.
review_title: Fresh, pleasing, not overpowering scent, intended for guys who are tired of little boy fruit bombs
review_text: I love how fragrances are sometimes described.  This is described as "blend of greens, nutmeg and tonka bean."  I don't even know what a tonka bean is, so I have no idea.  To my nose, I pick up notes of fresh rain and herbs.  And these notes are great.  I love this scent.  If you're a guy who gets tired of overpowering, fruit-heavy scents which are aimed at college kids, then this is definitely a man's fragrance to consider.  At the time that I write this, no price is available for the bottle I received for review (3.3 fl. oz.), so I can't honestly address whether or not this represents a good value.  It is definitely a quality product.

review_title: It's great for both day and night
review_text: Got this for my husband who is really picky about his fragrance. He loves Polo Blue by Ralph Lauren for Men, Eau De Toilette Natural Spray and is really unwilling to try anything else. With his birthday coming up I figured I'd get him something that he can change up and it was a hit. He loves the light not overpowering scent and so do I. It's great for both day and night. If the man in your life like the stronger stuff then you might want to get something different. This is definitely not your Axe deodorant spray but for a real man's man.

product_title: BURBERRY Brit Splash Eau De Toilette, 3.3 Fl. oz.
review_title: light, pleasant, intimate scent that is not overpowering
review_text:
It is always difficult to review colognes and aftershaves as scent is a very subjective thing, and trying to describe it with words is like trying to describe a color.  What I can say about this Burberry Brit Splash is it has a very pleasant, light scent that is not overpowering like so many fragrances people often wear these days.  I agree with another reviewer who referred to it as clean-smelling, but this is not the kind of scent you might find on bath soap or deodorant.  It is much more refined than that. This one is intimate and intended to be smelled by someone nearby.  It is the ideal scent for a man to wear while out on the town with his favorite lady and for more romantic moments.  My wife seemed to really like the scent after I sprayed some on.

There was no price listed for this product at the time I received it for review, so I cannot comment about cost and value.  What I can say is the bottle I received was quite generous in size (almost 14 ounces), much larger than I expected, and should last a very long time.  It has an atomizer on the top of he bottle, which allows for very light application.  The bottle is attractive and looks just fine sitting on the edge of my sink.

She generally only likes certain men's cologne products, like CK One, but she really likes the Burberry.  It actually caught me by surprise as she kept taking about how much she likes how it smells.  The Burberry would make a great gift as it comes in nice box and the bottle is nice as well.  I don't like the spray cap and find it hard to take off at times.  Outside of the spray cap the bottle looks good and presents itself well.  I would buy the Burberry again, and I'm sure my wife will make me buy it over other products.  I would even consider giving it as a gift to my dad.

review_text:
I love the way this smells on my husband!  It does have a fresh clean scent that's perfect for daytime wear, but there's also an undertone of something almost musky about it.  It's actually pretty sensual, but maybe it's because it's my man wearing it.  Burberry is all about the classics and this fragrance delivers that on all levels.

At the time of writing this review, there was no volume or size information available on the page.  For reference, this is a review for the 100 ml (3.3 fl oz) bottle.  The packaging is well designed and the bottle is very attractive (better in person).  This would make a great gift.

review_text:

She said she noticed a soapy, clean scent but thought it was a new deodorant. Not exactly what I was going for with this cologne.

review_title: Not to my liking, but YMMV.  Fragrance is a very personal thing.
review_text:
I received this in exchange for my honest review.  In order to assess the value of a review for your own personal buying decision, I think it's important to understand the preferences of the reviewer.  I adore scent.  I favor somewhat pungent natural fragrances with strong notes of rose, cumin, amber, but also some soliflores.  My own personal fragrances tend to come from places like Andy Tauer (Une Rose Chypree), LeLabo (Rose31) and Annick Goutal (Rose Absolue, Eau de Charlotte).  Formy husband I like Serge Lutens Chergui.  So, if you do not share my tastes, what I have to say about Burberry Brit will not be relevant to you.

I found this to be a  generic modern chemical ozonic  rather sweet fragrance, not very easily distinguishable from many that you can sample at Sephora.  To my nose it has more in common with the scent of dryer sheets than the kind of fragrance I am drawn to.  Very little silage, but it is quite long lasting on the skin.  Fragrance is a very personal thing.  For me personally it is not a match.  Neither on me nor my husband.  Your mileage may vary, as they say.

That being said, I suggest you take a fairly decent amount of time to test this on yourself before buying (or buying any perfume).  I like to go to big department stores that have testers of virtually everything they sell, spray a fragrance on both arms, and walk around the store a bit.  I sniff a few times during the stroll to see if the scent is changing on me.  Amazing how what initially smells heavenly can within 20 minutes turn into a real stinker of a perfume (and vice versa).

So far, I seem to get along well with all Camuto products.

review_title: Deep Earthy Scent with a Sweet Edge
review_text:
First things first: A little goes a long way with this perfume. A single spritz, in most cases, will be more than enough to get through an entire evening. From the description, I did expect the scent to be much lighter and more floral, but the initial scent notes I picked up were (strong and earthy) sandalwood and a cloying powdery jasmine.

Based solely on that initial spray, I'd peg this as an evening scent due to its heaviness. After about an hour, the sandalwood mellowed considerably leaving behind softer floral notes, especially the powdery jasmine and bergamot. And after about six hours, most of the heavier notes have all but disappeared leaving behind something much lighter, and flirty. If you put it on early enough, this could even be a day to day fragrance.

My typical perfumes are Very Irresistible by Givenchy, J'Adore by Christian Dior, and Forever by Alfred Sung (an oldie, but a goodie) just to give an idea--this was quite heavy in comparison to them--but for those who like heavier perfumes with a soft edge, this would do the trick. There is no hint of fruit, though the floral notes do lend it some sweetness.

Although the box could use a little work (the bottle swims around in it), the bottle itself is quite lovely to look at. The cap comes off easily and the nozzle is easy to locate--in other words, this bottle is thoughtfully designed, beautiful and functional.

Clothing designer Jose Natori has created a new fragrance called Josie. I am reviewing the 3.4oz  Eau de Parfum spray. The spray dispenser is appealing with its black and white geometric pattern and red highlights. The atomizer produces a fine but generous spray.

While this fragrance is advertised as a sensual floral scent, I thought it more of a musky scent. After 30 minutes or so, I smelled my wrist again and some of the musky scent that was initially present had dissipated, so it began to smell more floral, but the underlying musky scent remained. At first, I wondered if this was a unisex or mens cologne due to the musk.

Aside from Asian Pear in this fragrance, there is also Bergamot. I looked up Bergamot and was surprised to discover that it is derived from the Bergamot orange peel and is an ingredient in Earl Gray tea. Since designer Jose Natori is originally from the Philippines, it is fitting that her trademark scent contains the essence of the national flower of the Philippines, the Sampaguita (a.k.a. the Arabian jasmine). Freesia and Wild Orchid are also in this cologne.

I usually wear Marc Jacobs Daisy and Daisy Dream. I tend to prefer sweeter, flowery scents and I was not wild about this fragrance. My daughter, however, tried it and loved the scent. She wears a mens scented deodorant since the smell is appealing to her, so she selects fragrances that appeal to her senses rather than wearing ones that are touted to appeal to the opposite sex. She mentioned that the initial, primary musky scent was appealing to her.

product_title: Josie By Josie Natori Eau de Parfum
review_text:
I try not to give out 5 star ratings very often because I feel an item needs to be superlative to reach that level.  When I do give 5 stars I try not to be terribly effusive in my praise.  Well, how can I ever follow my own rule when it comes to this product?

I absolutely LOVE this fragrance.  This is going to become my signature perfume and that is coming from someone who is so picky about perfumes that I've often gone years without wearing even a sniff of one.

First:  presentation --- This product arrived in a black and white box which matches the picture of the container you see on the product page.  When opened, you see solid red fold-down flaps and under the box lid is a white space with a stylized red flower.  When you remove the container from the box it is heavy.  Heavy because it is a glass container approximately 5 1/2" x 1 3/4" etched with deep grooves cut into the patterned side of the glass to allow a hint of red to show through.  The black and white design is on two sides and the top and bottom, the other two sides are clear so you can see the spray mechanism which is a textured, see-through, red cylinder.  The clear tube carrying the perfume is inside this cylinder.  The perfume liquid is clear.  The lid lifts off to gain access to the red metallic spray mechanism.  The size fits my hand well for ease in spraying.  All of this is fascinating to look at and most attractive.

Second:  scent --- I'm a floral kind of girl so this fragrance is right up my alley.  When I first apply it I get a nice strong citrus scent.  As the moisture is absorbed into my skin and mixes with my personal body chemistry the light, soft, powdery, sweet, floral scents come to the surface and the citrus fades a little into the background.  I'm no expert in perfume formulation, I just know which scents I want to be around long term and this is IT.

review_title: Delightful floral that grows on you
review_text:
I must admit that when I first received this and put it on, I was almost nauseated with how strong and overpowering the fragrance was. After a couple of weeks of wearing it everyday, however, I think I have to say that it has grown on me. I understand that every perfume reacts with the individual's own body chemistry and subtly or completely changes the notes in the scent, and I was totally surprised to find that I actually like this perfume quite a bit. Normally I wear only one perfume -- Ames Soeurs by Joya -- so I thought I'd branch out a bit and try something new just to change things up. When I first put this on I felt that the smell was more suited to what I term "old lady" gag. But after the scent dries and absorbed into my skin, it changed to a very pleasant aroma (at least to me). I find it very floral with a bit of a woodsy note and definitely this is a perfume that you find where a little goes a long way. Two spritzes with the pump at the neckline and done is enough and it lasts for quite awhile.
As a side note -- the lingering smell on my clothes is very pleasant because as it evaporates into its essence, the residual is quite a nice scent.

The packaging is very trendy and the perfume comes in glass with a plastic pull off top. The black, white and red accents are striking and sort of belie that this is definitely not so much a "fresh" scent as a heavier toned floral. Great for evenings out, or nights in. As with all fragrances, I suggest anyone who is interested try a sample over a period of time to see how your body chemistry reacts and changes the scent and to see if it suits you. The product description details the essences used to make the perfume.

As previously stated, although I initially wasn't too crazy about this perfume, I actually ended up liking it a lot and am glad I have it!

review_title: Beautiful Floral, Woodsy Scent that is Light, yet Lingers
review_text: This is a new fragrance from renown designer Josie Natori. Josie is an invigorating, fresh scent that lingers. It has a floral, slightly woodsy scent that lingers, but isn't too strong. As a perfume lover, my tastes run to many of the classic fragrances like Estee Lauder and Channel No 5. Josie ranks up with the classics. It's not too light, very feminine, yet strong enough to make an impression and last the day. Friends and coworkers all remarked on how they loved the fragrance. Josie is packaged in a large, box with black and white blocked designs. This is a large 3.4 ounce bottle of eau de parfum. I prefer the parfum over eau de toilette, as the scent is stronger and not watered down. The bottle itself has 5 bands of the blocked design over two sides of the bottle with Josie's name on a red band in the front. It looks exactly like the photo. The sides are clear so you can check the volume and the atomizer is red. This is nice, sturdy bottle that is heavier than a normal bottle. The packaging and bottle also got rave reviews from my friends and coworkers. The atomizer sprays easily. This is now a new favorite fragrance for me. An excellent new entry from Josie Natori.

review_title: Josie is a nice scent, but use small amount.
review_text: I like Josie Eau do Parfum.  The scent is nice, though a tad too strong for me.  After spritzing a very small amount behind my ears and cleavage, then crossing my wrists over cleavage, rubbing wrists together, I approached my husband to get his opinion.  He did not care for it.  Well, he won't be wearing it anyway!  LOL  (He prefers a much lighter floral fragrance on me, such as L' Air du Temps.)  Josie's fragrance is made up of a jasmine (sampaguito - national flower of Philippines), Asian pear, bergamot (also found in my favorite Earl Grey tea), freesia, and orchid, plus the usual other ingredients that are there to stabilize and keep it fresh.  This is a perfume that seems to be more for evening wear, than morning and during the day.  It's been about 5 hours since I applied it, and I can still catch a whiff on my wrists.  Rather pleasant, I think...so I would say let it linger a while before going out.  It is referred to, as being a vibrant mix of being confident, sexy, and delivering a spirited energy.  I guess I'm just a little to quiet and mellow, so I'll wear it occasionally with caution.

product_title: Josie By Josie Natori Eau de Parfum
review_text:
I don't wear a lot of perfume these days, but I really, really like this one.  I'm in my late 30's, not fussy, and I think this is just perfect, and I keep smelling my wrist as I write this review.

I realize how silly it sounds to describe a perfume like this, but this reminds me of my childhood when I marveled at the perfumes on magazine pages.  That's mostly because  it's just very classic and familiar - and will remind you of a dozen other perfumes that you can't quite place.

This is definitely not a teen perfume (which, I think tend to be fairly shallow and heavy on citrus).  It's too rich and Musky.  That's not too say it's not youthful -  because it's got enough sweet floral to keep it from feeling musty or old.

product_title: Josie By Josie Natori Eau de Parfum
review_title: I quite like it, but think there will be lovers and haters of this fragrance, not too many who can take it or leave it.
review_text:
Overall, I like this eau de parfum, but am definitely not in the "love it" category.

There are many scents happening at the same time, which may appeal to some, and to which others may be adverse. It is not a light fragrance, and that said, my 17 year old daughter doesn't like it. As difficult as it is to describe a fragrance in words, especially given that it's all totally subjective, I would say that this fragrance is probaly one of those that women will immediately like or dislike as it's not one of those "beat around the bush" scents that you need to contemplate. It's definitely got musk, citrus, floral and tea notes happening, and I would honestly say that it's not a strong feminine fragrance (but does have a sweet finish) and has "shades" of more masculine scents. Like I said, a lot of different scents happening all at once, and a little goes a long way.

I do like it, but don't know if I'd actually pick it up and buy it for myself, as I have other fragrances that I really adore, and to add the fact that it's not a very inexpensive perfume. The bottle itself is unique, but very heavy and bulky.

product_title: Josie By Josie Natori Eau de Parfum
review_text:
I have not had much luck recently with commercial fragrances, as they all tend to smell the same with my body chemistry, sort of chemical like and cheap.  Since I tend to gravitate toward woodsy or floral type scents, I thought maybe a fragrance that claims to have a more fruit based scent (Asian pear in this case) would be different.  I was wrong.

Josie smells fine in the bottle, but when I apply to myself, I first get a strong alcohol smell-like I had spilled rubbing alcohol in the room.  Then the alcohol smell goes away, and I am left with a scent that is hard to describe.  It is not Asian pear, nor is it citrus, but more of a can of tropical fruit salad smell.  This fades quickly and is followed by a floral scent, like freesia and hyacinth mixed with Ivory soap.  On my skin, it smells absolutely nothing like the matching body lotion did-which is a good thing.

Not a terrible scent, and it did not give me a headache like Reveal by Calvin Klein, but it is not for me.  It does smell better on my clothing, curtains, and as an air freshener than it does on me.  It does not even smell nice on my daughter, on whom the body lotion smells wonderful.  Guess I will have to stick with perfume oils.

review_text:
It is difficult to review a fragrance when my claims cant be measured or substantiated by anything solid. The only real claim that can be made is how it smells and how long it will smell like that for.

In this review I will be comparing it to my other Calvin Klein product Aqua.

I have been using the Aqua product for about 6 months and before that I used Polo Black for about 2 years.

Reveal is a lighter fragrance than both Aqua and Black, which I like, and along with that, it is not in the least overpowering.

In relation to the product description, stating that it has a captivating, salty, oriental scent with identity is something I can neither confirm nor deny. In addition, I am in no position to comment with any authority about the content if its top, mid or base notes. I imagine that like me, the average consumer would also only be able to talk in broad terms about the cumulative effects of the ingredients.

What I can say is this:

It smells great - light but not feminine.

It is packaged in a very attractive bottle which comes in a stylish box.

My wife really likes it.

The only negative is that it appears to lose its strength quite fast compared to Aqua and Black.

All in all, I recommend this as a good buy,

review_title: A pleasant initial vanilla and almond scent, but overpoweringly sweet and strong!
review_text: Years ago my cologne of choice was a Calvin Klein creation called CK One. That scent was light clean  and citrusy, the type that I still prefer though my current go to choices have been Issey Miyake L'eau D'issei and Fierce by Abercrombie and Fitch. (Mentioned to establish a baseline of personal preference.) Those both qualify for the suggested correct strength of a scent also, of being barely detectable until someone has leaned into your personal space. I was anxious to see what the people at Klein had released with this new Reveal. Love the container which has clean lines and suggests something simple but elegant inside. The first spray revealed a scent that had strong overtones, at least to my nose, of Vanilla beans and a hint of Almonds; both very pleasant. It takes a few minutes for any scent to mix with your individual body chemistry and skin oils and any initial alcohol to evaporate before it settles down to it's real character. Allowing that time left still very strong scent of vanilla and perhaps talcum powder, but very, very sweet. Almost overpoweringly so. In fact it caused me to react by repeated sneezing. Something I've never experienced with any product before. You want a scent to linger so it lasts throughout your day, but this scent was so strong I found myself with a headache and actually needed to wash it off!  Imagining, perhaps, something else in the environment had caused the reaction, I applied it again the next day, but the reaction was the same. The scent was so overpowering that I felt the need to apologize to anyone near me, and hoped I wasn't giving off the impression of those people we all know who seem to take a bath in their perfume or cologne. (My elderly third grade teacher comes to mind, though was forgiven after my parents explained that elderly folks sometimes have their sense of smell diminished so put on copious amounts of a scent until they can detect it!) To be clear, I like the scent and tones, but if the volume could be dialed back considerably. I even tried spraying it on my fingers to just then dab a bit on my neck, but it still has boom box volume. Sorry Calvin, you still have all my boxer and blue jean dollars, but until the scent is toned down in another incarnation, I can't use Reveal. I suggest, as with any scent, a person test it at your department store of choice or at a duty free shop between flights to see if the scent and powerful strength is to your liking. As with all things, scent and strength are relative to our individual taste and perception. But the screaming volume and cotton candy sweetness that lingers unfortunately make it unusable for me.

product_title: Calvin Klein Reveal Eau de Toilette for Men, 1.7 fl. oz.
review_text:
I've never been the kind of guy that wears cologne every day of the week.  I shower, throw on some deodorant, and maybe, just maybe, I make a quick pass with a body spray to start off my day.  My work often finds me covered in sweat, and only the strongest deodorants can handle my funk by the end of the day.

However, Calvin Klein's Reveal might just change my mind.  I've been wearing it daily for over a week now, and I can honestly say that not only does it smell great when I first spray it on my body, it remains great smelling (but not overbearing) for at least twelve hours.  That includes a lot of sweaty time as the day rolls along.

The scent is very subtle, but it is definitely a wonderful scent.  I definitely notice the ginger in the cologne, and I also catch a hint of musk as the hours pass.  That might just be due to my body's chemistry, as it's well known that colognes and perfumes react and smell differently on different body types.

I'll often catch myself smelling my arm just to get a whiff of Reveal.  I've also noticed that my wife, close female friends, and complete strangers linger closer to me.  I know that my looks aren't what's drawing them in, so I can only assume that it's my cologne.  Also, I've received a few compliments about the cologne as well.

In short, if you want to smell good, buy this stuff.

product_title: Calvin Klein Reveal Eau de Toilette for Men, 1.7 fl. oz.
review_title: Clashed with body chemistry creating unexpected result
review_text:
"Sensual. Vibrant. Captivating." That's what the advertisement is selling, but I have to be honest, upon my first sniff I had to check and make sure it was indeed a men's fragrance. Perhaps it was the floral overtones that caught my attention, or the way it reminded me of cotton candy the longer I lingered over my husband's neck where he'd sprayed it, but this scent wasn't what I'd expected when I read the those three little words.

The scent is musky with a hint of spice, but sweet. I'd say it would be perfect for a tween, teen or twenty-something, but might be a little too soft for older gents. It's a youthful scent that while not off-putting; it's clean and fresh, isn't particularly sexy to my olfactories. Obviously scent is a subjective thing though, and while it may not be my cup of tea.

My husband initially liked the scent, but said over the course of a few hours of wearing it he began to find the scent off putting. He said it smelled like 'food' to him. I asked him to describe the 'food' in question and he said he couldn't. I asked him if he'd dribbled some food on his shirt.  Rolling his eyes he assured me it was the 'Reveal'.  We decided that for us - this scent was not good.

Fragrances work differently with each person's body chemistry to produce unique scents - that's why there are so many!  I give this 3 out of 5 stars (on the Amazon rating scale that's 'It's OK'...) based upon the experience my husband and I have had with this scent.  It's not bad, but it's definitely not for either of us. However by looking at other reviews I guess our experience puts us in the minority.  Take this into account before buying this product.

My advice regarding purchasing ANY scent  you've not yet tried: Go to a local department store that carries it to spray some on and wander around for a few hours first. I think that's the only true way to know if a fragrance is for you.

'Sweet. Clean. Unpredictable.'  These would be the three words I'd use to describe 'Reveal' after experiencing it first hand. Test drive before you buy. If you try it out, you'll have the best chance at enjoying it and not being disappointed... or hungry.

product_title: Calvin Klein Reveal Eau de Toilette for Men, 1.7 fl. oz.
review_text:
The packaging for the box and the cologne are both minimal and sleek. The box wouldn't grab your attention with its muted color palette and thin font but all cologne and perfume designs are put into the bottle.

The Calvin Klein Reveal bottle feels good in your hand - no sharp edges, continuous oval curve around the side and all corners and the bottom are rounded. Color-wise, everything is clear to gray, with the cap being a reflective chrome. The cap is snug and a good balance of having a secure fit and not being too hard to remove. When you remove the cap, you realize that the cap is over half the packaging, which seems a bit unnecessary.

One spray packs a powerful scent but it quickly mellows out as it melts into your skin, so I would say you don't need to spray much. There is something alluring about the scent. It has a subtle sweetness and no strong musk or wood notes. The description says the fragrance includes a mix of crystallized ginger, salt, and vetiver (bunchgrass native to India). Knowing that, I do notice that is a lingering sting in the back of my nose probably from the ginger. I will definitely mix this into my repertoire, as the scent notes are what I usually like. For reference, my favorite fragrances are Hei by Alfred Sung, and Acqua di Gio by Giorgio Armani.

review_title: Nothing new, too expensive, and no justification for it
review_text:
I want to place my sensibilities. I am a mid-30s professional man who enjoys a nice wardrobe - nice way to wallpaper the walls of the maze we run through in the rat race, I suppose. Anyway, I'm not a professional by any stretch of the imagination, but I'm also not an amateur. I have an embarrassing number of fragrances in my wardrobe, numbering in "several hundreds" although I haven't counted recently - somewhere north of 500 by my best estimation. I enjoy whatever smells great, without being snobby. I enjoy a $15 bottle of a nice synthetic like Fujiyama as well as a $300 bottle of Amouage (and I have all of them, all the Maitre Parfumeur et Gantier, several Le Labo, all of the Montales, all of the Creeds, all of the L'Artisan Parfumeurs, a variety of ouds, attars, and other pricey niche frags). I love a pleasant, silky floral that everyone can enjoy every bit as much as a complex, challenging and dense high-end fragrance that the layperson may find impossible to appreciate. My top-25 (alphabetical, not rank-order):

Amouage Lyric
Creed Green Irish Tweed
Creed Erolfa
Czech & Speake No 88
Dunhill Dunhill Man
Ferrari Light Essence
Ferrari  Uomo
Franck Olivier Black Touch
Franck Olivier Sunrise
Issey Miyake Issey Miyake pour Homme
Kenzo Kenzo Pour Homme
L'Artisan Parfumeur Passage d'Enfer
L'Artisan Parfumeur Timbuktu
L'Artisan Parfumeur Dzongkha
Le Labo Rose 31
Le Labo Oud 27
Maitre Parfumeur et Gantier Route du Vetiver
Maitre Parfumeur et Gantier Baime
Maitre Parfumeur et Gantier Jardin du Nil
Montale Aoud Forest
Montale Aoud Safran
Montale Black Aoud
Montale Aoud Lime
Polo Double Black
Success de Paris Fujiyama pour Homme

I love pleasant rich florals, aouds, fougeres, orientals. But I have eclectic taste in fragrances. The only type I really don't like are medicinal, artificial "wood" fragrances, the acerbic common "man" smell of the 70s office place. "Old Man" smells, like Halston, Old Spice. And, cloying, sticky-sweet catastrophes like Karen Low Xchange. A lot of background to say, "I like everything except sour-artificial-woody medicinal old man smell, or super-sappy-sweet teenage boy smell".

Now, this one - the sample in a magazine smelled pretty decent. Nice, a bit sweet but mellowed out to a sort of mildly sweet cedar and iris fragrance. I thought it smelled a little sweet but pleasant. Maybe a good attempt at a fruity drink sitting on a Caribbean beach, fragrant flowers in the air, warm sun. I bought a bottle for retail price from Macy's.

First application, I scrunched my nose. I thought - I have this one. I have three or four copies of this already. Dunhill Fresh, Dunhill Pure, Montblanc Starwalker, and a few others - same thing, in a different bottle. Applied with a full spray, it simply provides a thick cloying note. On skin it dries down and disappears. On fabric, it dries down but the sappy sweetness never goes away. I gave my wife a sniff (we always check out each others' new fragrances). She scrunches her nose, thinks, and says, it smells generic. Don't you already have that? It smells like any sweet man's fragrance. It's just... nothing special.

She summed it up well. This isn't a special fragrance. It isn't new. It's a mass-manufactured fragrance that has been around for years, probably mixed by Coty, that has shown up in bottles as humble as a $6 Adidas fragrance (I kid you not) - bottled with a nice bottle, wrapped in neat bright-orange leather, with a bright silver emblem.

I bought all of the Adidas fragrances. If anyone cares, comment here and I'll get the comment in my email. I'll rustle through all of the Adidas frags and find the closest one.

This isn't a "scrubber". I'll probably wear it as an inoffensive around-the-house fragrance, something to spray on and freshen up during yard work or car work, or perhaps as a shower fragrance. But for the price, no. Don't bother. It's not the worst, but it's absolutely, unequivocally not worth the price. In this price range you're getting dangerously close to Creed, MpG, L'Artisan Parfumeur, etc. - unfortunately, 70% of the price of this bottle goes to the bottle itself and the carefully construed advertising campaign with samples in mens magazines with dried-down samples nested in glue that emphatically underrepresents the synthetic cloying nature of the top and mid notes. At this point, after 30 minute, the fragrance on my skin is gone, and on fabric, it's still there, but smells almost like pineapple - maybe a spritz of pina colada mix from the grocery store - an embarrassing shadow of something in the same vein, but well done, like Franck Olivier Sun Java White - which incidentally costs well less than half as much.

Enjoy the good ones!

--------------------------------------

Revising down to 1 star. After wearing for a few days I can confirm that this has near zero longevity even when applied liberally (10+ sprays) in a dense pattern on fabric. That should give it the best staying power possible. The sillage is down to nothing in less than an hour. I strongly recommend avoiding this.

Solare - High School Freshmen boy scent.
Homme - 20's adulthood scent.
Vince Camuto - Mature, sexy scent.

We both agree it has a very sweet smell that has strong hints of vanilla (despite the fact that nowhere is vanilla mentioned in the product description) with a bit of peach and cotton candy in the mix.  Others have described it as light, but my wife said it is a strong fragrance in her opinion, and it lasts.  I actually like it better than my wife even - she enjoys it but I think the sweet aroma is extremely pleasing and it isn't floral at all (I don't care for floral perfumes and thankfully neither does the Mrs). review_title: Juicy Couture I am Juicy couture Eau de Parfum
review_text:
Reviewing scents is not an easy endeavor.  Everyone is different when it comes to what scents they like or don't like.  I have always been very particular about scents and never wore perfume until fairly recently.  There are a few scents which I absolutely love, some I like and some that send me running in the other direction.  The "Juicy Couture I am Juicy couture Eau de Parfum" (wow!) is a scent I like.  I'm glad it isn't very strong and I have been able to wear it for several hours without wanting to wash it off.  It has a light, sweet-like fruity scent that is not overpowering.  Granted, I didn't douse myself in it, but gave the inside of my arms a light squirt each.

The bottle is pretty cool - almost garish but I like it.

product_title: Juicy Couture I Am Juicy Couture, 1.7 fl. Oz., perfume for women
review_text:
This is a popular product and I was glad for the opportunity to try it.  Beautiful bottle (1.7oz/50ml) with pump mist.  Very nice packaging.  Made in USA.  But, I was disappointed in the scent.  My wife likes it better than I do, but my findings . . .

Flowery (but not roses, perhaps the gardenia influence), sweet (candy-like),  fruity (citrus).  Not offensive, if worn lightly, but definitely not a fragrance that I would consider a "signature" scent or something that makes me want to get closer to it.  Certainly feminine, but it's more like what I would consider an "old lady " perfume (or, conversely, for a pre-teen girl to use on her Barbies).  A couple of other reviewers commented that it smells like baby powder.  I didn't find that at all at first, but maybe over time it finally settled in to a little baby powder-ish influence.  I think it would be more accurate to say that it settled into scent resembling my favorite gum . . . which solves the riddle of the curious name of this perfume.

Sorry, I really wanted to give this a more positive review, but it's just not for me.

product_title: Juicy Couture I Am Juicy Couture, 1.7 fl. Oz., perfume for women
review_text:
I really like this fragrance, probably one of my favorites in the Juicy product line. I have 4 so far (Juicy Couture, Viva La Juicy, Viva La Juicy Noir and this new one, I Am Juicy Couture).  This new one smells a lot like the original Juicy Couture but with a heady bouquet of summer flowers and summer fruit (peaches,  I think).  While I liked the original, I like this one even more.  It just reminds me of Spring & Summer, outdoors in the warm fresh air when everything is blooming.  It's a much softer scent than Viva La Juicy, which seemed to have bright berry notes (reminded me of raspberries) and smelled a little sharper when first applied.

While I really like this perfume,  it may smell totally different on you.  I would suggest smelling a sample before taking the plunge.  After all, this isn't a cheap bottle of drugstore colonge.

product_title: Calvin Klein Eternity Now Eau de Parfum Spray
review_title: Strong formulation of a somewhat mysterious and layered perfume
review_text:
Naturally the only way to tell if you like a perfume is to test it.  My review can't tell you whether the scent works for you.  BUT I can tell you a few things that aren't apparent after a quick department-store sniff.

First, this is a strong and long-lasting scent.  Use less than you think you need, and expect there to be some lingering detectable scent at the end of the day if you put it on in the morning...or in the morning if you put it on in the evening.  To my mind this is not a daytime scent, though you may disagree.

Second, the scent is REALLY strong in the first few minutes.  Don't judge until it has had a little while to settle down.

Third, the bottle is really nice - simple and elegant, and looks pretty on the dresser or vanity table.

Fourth, I have no idea what "Eternity Now" means, or even what marketing message it is supposed to convey.  But that doesn't matter, as long as you like the scent.  And I do.  It is a mix of more elements than usually go into a perfume, with no dominant note.

Oh well, I did try to convey something of the scent in words.  In any case, if you know you like this perfume, I can assure you that the bottle holds no bad surprises, as long as you are sparing with your application.

If you like Calvin Kline scents - I think you'll also like this one.  Amazon also offers a better price than most department stores.

The 4 star rating rather than the 5 is simply due to comparison to my all-time favorite scent which is no longer on the market (Fendi).  Whereas I really like Eternity Now, it hasn't surpassed by favorite perfume and for that reason I view it as a 4 star - still a wonderful scent but not my all-time favorite.

review_title: Not for me - too much Neroli overwhelms the lychee and peach blossoms brightness
review_text:
I received this at no cost from Amazon Vine in exchange for a fair and unbiased review.

I loved the original Eternity, so thought I would try this version. It is nice and has a touch of the original scent, but it has a little too much Neroli to make it a perfume I would buy. It takes a lovely, bright, fragrance and almost deadens it with the Neroli; almost makes it a "cloying" scent. For some, that would make this a product for them, but I prefer brighter fragrances with a soft finish. You can definitely smell the different facets from the lychee/peach blossoms to the ambrox/musk. Sadly, the Neroli takes over at the finish.
