review_text:
Warning: This is a ONE SPRITZ perfume!  A very powerful scent, don't overdo it!

When worn with only one spritz, it is an uplifting and flowery scent perfect for spring.  Its absolutely lovely, the smell is delicious and rosy.  I have the body wash, and loved the smell so much I wanted the perfume to continue to enjoy it throughout the day.  It clings to your skin more than your clothes, which is nice, because I can rewear a sweater without having to wash it if I want to wear a different perfume.  It also means you can continue to enjoy the smell through multiple wardrobe changes.

The first day I wore it I did two spritzes and that was WAY TOO MUCH.  I was sneezing over and over, and was feeling sickly being trapped in the car with myself.  I received it as a gift from an aunt who bought it from our local L'Occitane retail store, and they sprayed the tissue paper in the gift bag.  It was really overwhelming, one of my cousins was really displeased with the overpowering smell.

So ladies, use this lovely smell wisely!  One spritz will do.

review_title: Regular Burberry Baby Touch (with alcohol) vs. Alcohol free
review_text:
Dear Amazon,

I don't know if you're aware, but Amazon has some misinformation regarding this product. The reviews from customers clearly say they were sold the 'alcohol free' version of this product, yet the photo Amazon displays here is of the normal (with alcohol) product.  As was stated by the review from T. Cobain: "Got this as a gift when my son was born, and honestly, since it was alcohol free I sprayed it on his clothes some days. OH! How people LOVED to hold my baby. He smells so heavenly! ..."

The alcohol-free version is green tinted liquid and clearly is noted on the front of the bottle as alcohol free (sans alcohol). The photo Amazon displays is the purple tinted liquid, which is the normal, alcohol containing version.

I have had more issues with this product and returns/exchanges for this very reason of companies displaying a version of baby touch that they are not actually selling, and I ask that you please look into this and make it right.

Purple tinted= normal Baby Touch, 'with alcohol' version, and Green tinted= 'alcohol free' version (Please look up on the internet the alcohol free version to see the difference in the color of the liquid and the extra line of typing on the front of the bottle that indicates it is 'alcohol free').

Thank you~

review_text: I have been using this brand for about 2-3 years.  I absolutely LOVE this perfume and I have received many, many, many compliments on it. It is not in the duty free in France or Amsterdam.  Typical price I pay (1-2 years ago) is $230. I was very surprised to find it on here and searched on a whim.  I don't want to buy a new bottle, I fear when they sit too long they go bad.  Too much money to waste on a spare but it is such a lovely scent.  And unique, like I said, hard to find. product_title: Jean Patou Joy Forever Eau de Toilette Spray
review_text:
Jean Patou Joy Forever is a beautiful fragrance.  I feel like I've got my own personal bouquet of flowers on my wrists.

Top notes: bergamot, mandarin, galbanum
Mid notes:  jasmine, rose, orris, marigold, orange flower and peach
Base notes: cedarwood, sandalwood, white musk, amber

For me, the base notes are so subtle that go unnoticed.  The scent is a true mixed floral.  I have a difficult time picking out the individual notes, but they blend together to create a gorgeous bouquet.

I am drawn to florals, but I typically like a quieter fragrance.  Joy Forever comes on strong and lasts a very long time, but it's quite pretty and I'm growing used to the power.

This is a classic, romantic fragrance that I could see myself wearing any time and for many years to come.  For some reason that I can't pinpoint, I really find this scent comforting.

review_text:
I have been looking around for a while, trying to find a replacement cologne to my favorite one that was discontinued (only sold by Gordmans). I was a little hesitant to pull the trigger on buying Arrogant because of the price, but now that I have it I will be a customer for LIFE! This cologne is simply amazing! It comes in spiffy looking box. I'm not really good at describing smells, but it is simply awesome. I really can't see anyone being disappointed using this fragrance.

One more thing...buying fragrances online is kinda dicey for a number of reasons: 1) how can you smell a sample and know if you're going to like it? This leaves one to sift through legitimate reviews to find out if it is well accepted (And there are a lot of fake reviews out there so do your research) 2) A lot of third-party vendors push knock-offs of the real fragrances--greatly increasing their profit margin and destroying customer trust. My advice is to only buy from vendors you know--or simply buy this through Amazon--it'll say "ships from and sold by Amazon.com." This way you know you're not getting a knock-off.

product_title: AMOUAGE Journey Man's Eau de Parfum Spray, 3.4 Fl Oz
review_text:
After spending $50 on two carded samples, wearing Journey Man for six times, during two weeks, I can conclude the following:

Opens w an acute boozy cognac note, a la bois d'ombrie, to be immediately tamed by a short lived but cloyingly sweet rich tobacco that is overtaken by a benzoin/tonka/pepper/fruit (kind of lichi?) accord that lingers on and on...throughout...

Although I tried, numerous times, to negotiate w this sweet accord to relax, and let mr. frank incense, cardamom, lezr, play their solos, or combined...in vain!

The base is also on synthetic sweet wood (probably ebony?), nothing special: faint undertones of rien de rien incense!

If you tilt toward the majesty of Epic or the smokiness of Interlude, forget this one!

However, if you are looking for a sweeter version of Jubilation 25, then look no more for Journey Man will satisfy all your sweet olfactory desires; this eau de parfum is 100% western, wout any oriental tendency!

By all means, Journey Man has the Amouage rich quality ingredients but not the Sultanate Oman Arab Signature (i.e.,intended to Western consumers...).

review_title: Good Design and Packaging, So-So Smell Over Time
review_text:
I know fragrances are very personal, and granted, I did not try this at the store before receiving a bottle for review, so take this review with a grain of salt. Also, I'm female, and got this for my husband to try. In every way, the beautiful packaging, sleek and modern looking bottle and amazingly micro-mist type pump action from the dispenser for this Jimmy Choo Man are straight 5s for presentation and utility. The heavy weight and leatherette banding of the top cap is also a nice touch, as is the metal accent shoulders. I love the way this bottle looks, feels and pumps.  That said, I am not a big fan of the scent, and neither is my husband, who I sprayed this on.

The scent from the bottle is at first quite pleasant, with a sharper woodsy note at the front and reminds me of how some higher end hotel toiletries are scented. Over time, however, the under-notes are more reminiscent of how women's magazines smell when they have a lot of scratch and sniff perfume scents in them- the blend is not unpleasant, but more feminine and generic. The smell on my husband starts to blend w his chemistry to become somewhat "powdery"  vs. crisp, and takes on a stronger mono-scent that's just smells like a boring perfume over time, which is really unfortunate.  I wanted to like this scent, and I do when I open the bottle. On my husband, tho, and over time, the stronger woodsy scent gives way to a powdery generic fragrance I don't particularly love.

review_title: Excellent gift for women of any age group
review_text:
My BURBERRY is an elegant perfume that is runway-inspired and features notes of sweet pea, bergamot, golden quince, freesia, patchouli, rain-tipped damask, and centifolia roses.  Normally, I find perfumes that have strong fragrances like bergamot, patchouli, and geranium to smell aged and not altogether youthful. However, what makes this perfume unique is that it smells like spring. It is bouncy, fun, yet remains sophisticated. I like the fragrance does not overpower me. The perfume is said to represent a London garden after a rain and I think it does that completely.
  My Burberry smells like wet flowers in the sun and it is a treat. It smells youthful and light and I think this perfume is perfect for women of any age and would make an excellent gift.  The perfume lasts for several hours with a light mist and lingers lightly on the clothing and skin once the scent has dissipated. This is a carefree and happy smelling perfume and an excellent choice.

review_title: This is a nice, feminine perfume
review_text:
It's hard to buy a perfume without testing it first, so try to test before purchase.  This Burberry fragrance is pleasantly feminine.  It is not sporty, not bright and light, and I don't think it would be a teenager's choice.  Maybe it's a bit too heavy?  It sure does last!  I found I like the fragrance better as it aged.  For instance, I sprayed it on my wrist, then put on a cardigan sweater.  Days later I could still catch a whiff of it on my sweater sleeve.

This eau de parfum is potent, and you will want to use it sparingly.  Which leads me to the observation that the spray bursts out of the nozzle in a wide and strong pattern.  I'm used to more delicate, shorter sprays.

The bottle is hefty and very impressive.  Comes in a pretty box for gifting.

review_text:
Depending on your generation, demographics and a few other factors wearing cologne is likely not as popular as it once was. Its certainly not more popular. For me it remains one of those things Ive never used daily. Im more apt to apply a dab before a special evening with a special person.

Most of the colognes Ive ever bought I still have, I think I bought the majority of them for how cool the bottles would look on my bathroom shelf and I cant say I don't choose which one to wear based more on the bottle color and shape than the fragrance inside of it.

It seems a little iffy to buy a fragrance through the mail without having the opportunity to sample it first so I must confess my primary reason for choosing this one was for the bottle. I figured it would be serendipity to discover its fragrance the first time I wore it.

How something smells is uniquely personal so Im sure you don't care what I think about what I smell like and I certainly don't care what you smell like. I will likely reach for whatever cologne catches my eye as I dash out the door all dressed up and ready to rock and roll so if you come with me youll be the first to know.

review_title: Very intriguing cologne.  A bit too strong for me, but accurate description from the manufacturer.  I like the lime notes.
review_text: This is a very interesting cologne.  The manufacturer has described it well as going on fresh and then turning a bit more intense.  I have had about four or five colognes that I have used often--Polo, Gucci, Emporio Armani black, and a few others.  So this more 'intense' cologne was an experiment of sorts.  At first, I really liked the way it smelled initially.  The lime notes are quite pleasant out of the bottle.  In fact, for the first few moments I could swear it was very similar to Emporio Armani (which I like a lot).  However, the lime fragrance dissipates very quickly.  And then one is left with the 'licorice' scent.  This is much stronger and a little bit (a very little bit) goes a long way (practically eight hours).  I am less inclined to like the cologne for this reason.  However, I am less inclined to strong cologne anyway.  The strongest one I like is the Gucci which smells a bit like fresh sawdust (a scent I happen to like as  I like woodworking).  All in all, I think that the description from the manufacturer is accurate, and the scent is powerful but not overpowering.  I think I will try to wear it in the late summer and early fall months, much as I would the Gucci.  It reminds me of a humid day in early September.

product_title: Lacoste L!VE Gift-Wrapped Eau de Toilette for Men, 3.3 fl. oz.
review_text:
I wasn't so sure about this product at first. I'm not a huge cologne wearer but I started with just a single spritz on the neck to see if it lasted, if I smelled it or if anybody else noticed it. None of those came to fruit so I upped the dosage to two and 1/2 or 3 and after doing this for a bit, I don't honestly care what anybody else thinks I smell like. I like what I smell like. Laoste L!VE has a nice even scent to it. It lasts a long time and it isn't obnoxious or overpowering. It's just a nice calm subtle smell to it. I've yet to have anybody comment on my cologne but I have noticed some squirrely eyes from some unsuspecting ladies wondering why they were so attracted to my awkward self.

Bottom line though, I'm more attracted to myself and that's where it starts. Nice easy-going product to fit my easy-going nature.

review_text:

The aroma blend is well composed with bottom (dark wood and spice) and high notes (citrus and grass) receiving equal prominence together in pitch perfect harmony.

Vessel presentation is equally impressive with the generous amount of fragrance (3.3 ounces) contained in a hefty and sturdy square glass bottle.

review_title: Sits between Brit Rhythm and London to me.
review_text: I like Brit Rhythm very much, and was running low on Burberry London, which is my go-to in colder months. I had come across Rhythm Intense in a magazine ad a while ago, but had a hard time finding it in stores. To me -- and cologne is so subjective -- Rhythm Intense is like a middle ground between Rhythm and London. There's the light / fresh aspects that make Rhythm interesting, but there's also the leathery pipe tobacco thing going. (If you've never smelled London, it's a lot like a spiced pipe tobacco.) Rhythm Intense is a bit trickier to wear, though. It gets overpowering very easily, and takes a while to lighten up. But unlike regular Rhythm, which tends to last for many hours, I find that Rhythm Intense seems to disappear after about 4 - 5 hours. I'd buy it again, for sure. But as a 9 - 5 kind of cologne in fall / winter, I think I'll probably stick with London and use this as more of a "going out" cologne.

review_title: Too strong with some strange undertones
review_text:
Obviously, colognes smell a little different on everyone, and this one will likely be one of those scents that you either love or hate, with very little mid ground.

The first (and main) thing that I have to mention is that it's really, really, really strong. I've used it a lot in the past month and found that even two sprays at close distance to my skin is way too much. When first sprayed on, it has an unfortunate chemical smell if you spray it straight on (my 4 year old daughter thought it was a permanent marker the first time I wore it), and after a couple tries I realized that all I needed was one spray into the air in front of me and a walk through it.

It's one of those colognes where a little is definitely worth a lot, and actually smells a lot better when spread thinner and more evenly. I prefer Burberry London straight up, but used sparingly this will be a decent occasional alternate.

review_text:

product_title: BURBERRY Brit Rhythm Eau de Toilette Intense for Him, 3 fl. oz.
review_title: Another Fine French-Made Men's Cologne from Burberry
review_text: This is a real French-made men's perfume or cologne ("eau de toilet" or "toilet water" does not translate well into English!). We'll start by saying that we were already fans of the English company, Burberry. In a marriage, your cologne and perfumes have to be a joint choice, as both the person wearing it, and the one who has to enjoy it on the other, must be in accord. In our case, either one has the veto over a new scent. Our very favorite is London Burberry, but the company has a couple of other men's fragrances we're not as fond of, so we really needed to check this out in person. (There's some sort of deep, musky note, in a couple of them that the female of the family cannot abide). We both agree, Burberry Brit Rhythm is a hit. That "deep note" is not present in this cologne. A couple of other reviewers found this scent too intense. Not our experience at all. Naturally, cologne is one of those very personal decisions, and one person's perfume will be another's poison. However, the man of the family, being someone who doesn't like to smell like a French woman of the street drifting by, is very particular not to wear overpowering scents. When you first apply Brit Rhythm Intense, the top note can be a little much. It's floral and strong. However, within 5 to 10 minutes, this fades into the masculine, pleasing middle and lower notes, and these are what last through the day or evening. We're no experts on how to blend fragrances, so the company's own write-up says it best (not on the Amazon page by the way, which is terse, but on Burberry's own site): "heart notes of black leather, patchouli and styrax resin and sensual base notes of cedar wood, incense and tonka bean." By the way, sometimes we've read reviews by men who say they spray on 4 or 5 "shots" of cologne -- that would be too intense! A discreet 1 or maybe 2 shots at most, at the base of the throat, is sufficient. (Of course, you would never apply this under your arms, as the effect could be overpowering. A neutral deodorant for that application -- and in our opinion, one without any aluminum in it which clogs pores, is a better idea. Then you don't have 2 totally different fragrances fighting each other). As you dig a bit deeper, you discover that different fragrances, even by the same company, can be unique. Often, each is created by a different designer. SO, having noted that cologne is a uniquely personal choice, the only way you're really going to know if you like this one blended with your own body chemistry, is to try it. By the way, the man of the family already owns and enjoys BURBERRY Brit Rhythm for Him Aftershave Balm, 5.0 fl. Oz.. Highly recommended!

product_title: Juicy Couture Hollywood Royal Eau de Toilette
review_text:
Hollywood Royal has that mystical combination of sweet and woodsy that makes my heart skip a beat when a woman wearing it walks by.  The lingering scent is not at all pungent or offensive, despite having some floral notes.  The "flowers" are the more modern sort, like white lillies smelled through a window rather than a potpurri satchel.

Why four stars?  The bottle looks like it is straight out of a kid's playset, with a plastic star cover perfect for Barbie's dream house.  I like the fun concept, but the execution might detract from using it as a gift.  Still, the scent is so good that I don't think it matters much.

It does not look nice in person, more of a child's fake perfume bottle for dress up. The bottle itself is glass and heavy, they should have just gone with an elaborate top and left the rest plain. The perfume is worth it, the bottle ruins it. If you can find the same scent in regular packaging, I'd suggest that over this.

review_text: Nice packaging on the box. Pull the bottle out and it looks elegant, but the stars that wrap around the bottle is like a collar and are plastic and they move, so it comes off a little cheap. The smell at first, you may want to shake it, but it has a strong alcohol odor. But spray on the skin and it has a different tone. product_title: Juicy Couture Hollywood Royal Eau de Toilette
review_text:
I feel like Goldilocks with the samples of Juicy Couture I've been given to try--one is too faint; one is too strong... This one has a very powerful, almost masculine, aftershave presence when first applied.  It does dry down to a lovely floral/herb cloud that lasts a very long time, but there's definitely a learning curve to how much to apply.  Less is certainly more!

When you get it right, Hollywood Royal is a wonderful fragrance--the kind you'll get compliments on!

review_title: Sporty, fresh fragrance that is not overpowering
review_text:
I absolutely LOVE Burberry Brit Splash, Eau de Toilette! It is a perfect blend of sporty and mature-ish scent and is not overpowering. You don't have to use much at all, and yet, the fragrance will last all day, even after a night of dancing and stuff. The best is my wife loves it (her new favorite, she said)....It is clean, fresh, and still subtle, and as my wife says, "sexy." Fragrances are so subjective, and often depend on skin type, etc. My skin is usually dry and not oily. I also find that I always need to let a cologne (or EdT) kind of settle in before I pass judgement because things change for me after just a few minutes.

This is a big bottle, and unlike some there Burberry products, this spray is easy to modulate so you don't get a huge spray. The only negative I can think of is that the cap is very tight a little difficult to remove, and because the bottle is so smooth, it sometimes feels like I might drop the bottle or fling something as I am pulling it off. Still, it looks nice. You see the Burberry design, but doesn't look stuffy.

product_title: BURBERRY Brit Splash Eau De Toilette, 3.3 Fl. oz.
review_title: Time for a Stiffener, Eh What!
review_text:
Reviewing a fragrance is of course a very subjective proposition.

So I will do my best to describe this scent and allow readers to form their own conclusions.

Burberry says this eau de toilette features a "blend of greens, nutmeg, and tonka bean," if that means anything to you.

I would say the predominant note is citrus.  To me, this smells like something between a gin and tonic with a healthy twist of lemon -- and some herbicide.

Brit Splash is nowhere near as off-putting as the dreadful Axe body spray that so many urban youths seem to immerse themselves in, but neither in my opinion does it come close to the lovely Crabtree & Evelyn Sienna cologne that has long been my own favorite.

I would describe this eau de toilette as "bracing."  And it keeps on bracing too.  One squirt on the left side of my neck, another on the right -- and I'm guessing I could attract fruit flies many hours after application.

The bottle is quite handsome, at any rate.  That counts for something!

So if you like citrus scents created by a prestigious brand and packaged in a decorous and heavy bottle, you might find a lot to like in this Burberry Brit Splash.

Myself, I think I'll stick with my cherished Crabtree & Evelyn Sienna cologne.

UPDATE: I applied more of this stuff before a night on the town a few days back -- this time, just one squirt under the chin instead of two under each cheek.  Again I concluded -- I don't very much like the smell of this ODT (eau de toilette).  I might keep the bottle, however...

product_title: Raw Spirit Luxury Eau de Parfum (Desert Blush, 1.0 fl oz)
review_text:
This was an interesting scent to try, as it can be smelled several times and different notes keep coming to the fore.

The initial spritz does smell strongly of alcohol.  Once that dissipate, that's when the spicy, very woodsy notes start to show up.  This is touted as being a unisex fragrance, but I would say that at this stage, the scent is fairly intensely masculine.  After some time has passed - usually a matter of a couple of hours or so - that woodsy smell starts to fade, and what remains is a slightly less intense floral aroma that retains a hint of the spiciness.  At this point, the scent becomes more feminine in nature.

The (changing) scent isn't bad, per se, at any time, but it is on the strong side; so much so that it tends to give me headaches, as I am someone who is generally sensitive to really strong fragrances.  This one turned out to be more intense than I expected.

Again (aside from the headaches), the fragrance isn't what I'd call bad, but I also can't say that this is one for which I'll be reaching with any kind of regularity.  Moreover, while it could appeal at different times to those looking for a masculine or feminine scent, I would caution users that the scent's change is pretty noticeable, so while those on the hunt for more manly scents might enjoy it initially, they might not be so pleased as the day wears on.  Similarly, those looking for a sophisticated, womanly scent (though not one that could ever be called girly or delicate) might not be overly happy with it when it's first used, but after waiting for some time, they could like the end product.

All in all, it's a difficult product to review, because it's something that could easily wind up appealing to different people at different times, given how it changes the longer it's worn.  It's strong, but not unpleasant, and I can definitely say that I've never smelled or encountered a fragrance quite like this before.  I can't say that I think it's worth the price for which it's being sold, but for all those who are in the market for a scent that's really different, you might like this.

review_text: Raw Spirit Eau de Parfum, Desert Blush comes in a nice bottle which is enclosed in a rose color sleeve enclosed in a white color cardboard box and the bottle sits inside in a crafted cutout exclusively for the protection of the bottle. After couple of minutes when the alcohol has dried out the smell starts to change and become primarily floral scent a mixture of sandalwood sweet flowers and feels fresh. IMHO the scent is overwhelming at first but slowly fades away to more fresh flowery smell. I have used Calvin Klein ETERNITY for Men and while this is an unisex product which is suitable for both men and women this one smells better than ETERNITY for men. This one needs to be applied in very small quantity and it does linger for more than 24 hrs after initial application and does smell nicer than ETERNITY when compared. The only quibble I have is the spray nozzle does seem little too basic black plastic when compared with rest of the product. This is a luxury scent product and has a very Rich sophisticated, floral scent! does smell nice. Four stars!

product_title: Raw Spirit Luxury Eau de Parfum (Desert Blush, 1.0 fl oz)
review_text:
Has a strong scent of alcohol when first sprayed, which within moments mellows to a woodsy scent. The smell is more complex than cedar.  It bears no resemblance to the smell of cedar-scented closet hangers.  My husband, who is allergic to cedar, did not sneeze when smelling this perfume.  Soon after that,  the floral undertones shine through, comingling with the woodsy smell.  I really like this scent, it is very unique and versatile, being both fresh and slightly musky and somewhat flowery but not overly sweet.  It's suitable for a day at the office, or a day spent outdoors, or even an evening out.  A lot of perfumes smell like they are made for either a teen girl or a grandmother, but this is a sophisticated yet sexy and down-to-earth blend.  Really a nice combination.  For reference, my other favorite perfume is  Katy Perry's Killer Queen. This perfume is described as being unisex, and I can see that.  It is not overly masculine or feminine.  One downside is that the scent does not last very long.

There is some controversy regarding the harvesting of sandalwood, including the wild harvested Australian sandalwood contained in this product.  If you are particularly interested in environmental issues, a bit of research is suggested.  The company, Nomad Two Worlds, was founded by famed photographer Russell James, with the goal of helping indigenous people through a self-supported company rather than a charity.  The company puts an emphasis on being socially and environmentally responsible and donates 10% of their profits to their charitable donation arm, also called Nomad Two Worlds, as well as an undisclosed amount of their proceeds to Australian indigenous agricultural projects, and are also aligned with the Clinton Global Initiative.  (This information about the company's background came from a 2013 Forbes article on Russell James, so may not be up to date.  The company's website contains no financials, including no references to what percentage of their profits are donated.)

This product is made in the USA. It is nicely packaged in a heavy off-white cardboard box with cutout insert for the bottle and the emblem in gold on the box cover.  The box has a rose-colored sleeve around it that is made of heavy paper.  The sleeve also has gold writing and emblem that looks like the label on the bottle.  The label on the bottle itself is made of thick, high-quality, glossy paper.  The lid and spray mechanism are black plastic.

product_title: Raw Spirit Luxury Eau de Parfum (Desert Blush, 1.0 fl oz)
review_title: Starts out very spicy with lots of cedar scent, but mellows to a unique floral fragrance
review_text:
When I spray this perfume on it has a very spicy scent.  You can really smell the cedar, sandalwood, and the musk base.  Especially the cedar.  It reminds me of camping in the deep, damp woods or the smell of freshly cut cedar planks.  Very out-doorsy.  In the first 30 minutes of spraying this perfume I could detect no hint of a floral tones, but after a while the spiciness starts to mellow and you get a hint of flowers.  After about 2 hours the spicy scent fades into the background and the floral tones become prominent.  And the floral tones are unique and interesting.  Like no flower I have ever smelled before.

So if you like spicy scents with just a hint of floral this is a unique and interesting option; but if you like a purely floral fragrance, this might not be the perfect choice.

product_title: Raw Spirit Luxury Eau de Parfum (Citadelle Luxury, 1.0 fl oz)
review_text:
I struggle to find scents I like. This one had me with one sniff.

It is a little woodsy with hints of lemon, but I was surprised that it was so delicate considering it was a unisex scent. I can actually see either my husband or I wearing it and both being able to pull it off, which is not common. It is not a delicate floral, if that is what you are looking for. Since I tend to like heavier, spicier scents, I was really pleased with this- it is woodsy, but not too strong. I don't usually wear perfume either, so a more subtle scent was appreciated. I got a lot of compliments, and I will definitely buy this again once I run out!

product_title: Raw Spirit Luxury Eau de Parfum (Citadelle Luxury, 1.0 fl oz)
review_title: Longest notes are green and grassy
review_text:
I have issues with some perfumes so am always on the lookout for one that I can wear.  I have learned that I have the most trouble with heavy floral perfumes so like to try unisex fragrances.

I was hoping that the bergamot would give this a more citrus-y smell but that note is fleeting at best.  I never really noticed any citrus at all.  I also thought the amberwood and musk would be more dominant but the scent that lasts the longest for me is the grassy scent of the vetiver.  If I had to describe this scent, it would be that it smells green and maybe a little herbal or grassy (but not like freshly mowed grass -- more herbal grass).

Because everyone's personal chemistry affects how scent will react and because words don't always convey smell very well, I would not buy this without finding someplace to get a trial size or to try it in person.

The bottle is classic and elegant looking and I thought the scent lasted a fair amount of time.  For me, I wish the citrus notes were more dominant.  It was OK but herbal/grassy isn't quite what I was looking for in a scent.  It is definitely not for someone looking for a girly flowery scent.  This might work well for guys who like to wear scent as well as women who want something different than the usual florals or citrus.

product_title: Raw Spirit Luxury Eau de Parfum (Citadelle Luxury, 1.0 fl oz)
review_title: deeply sensual scent for man or woman
review_text:
I love this earthy, grounding and deeply sensual perfume.  I've never had the pleasure to smell Vetiver, but LOVE Bergamot and Cedarwood, so I thought I would at least like the scent.  I was so happy when on first (tiny) spray, I instantly loved it.
I smell the musk quite a bit and yet to really smell the pear and nutmeg, but I'm not really a perfume connoisseur, so this would be typical for me.
I spray just a tiny bit on my stomach and it lasts all day for me. I definitely enjoy the scent come thru when I'm least expecting it.  It makes me smile and think of strength and resistance.  I can't explain it better than that.  I feel strong and able just a bit more when the scent hits my nose.
 I don't do well with very strong scents so this works best for me if I use just a tiny spray under my clothes as it is quite strong.  I highly recommend only using a small spray whether or not you can handle scents because it is highly concentrated and will make anyone's eyes water if wearing to much.
Overall, I think this is a quality product, magnificent scent and the fact that a portion of the proceeds help Haitian Agricultural projects make this a must purchase item for yourself and for your friends and lover.  Definitely a scent for either man or woman.

product_title: Raw Spirit Luxury Eau de Parfum (Citadelle Luxury, 1.0 fl oz)
review_title: Woodsy and exquisite, for me a powerful scent memory trigger
review_text:
This Citadelle by Raw Spirit is a wonderful scent unlike anything else I have tried in the past.  My first impression was that it was a light, powdery scent that was not in any way fruity or flowery (which is a good thing).  Beyond the initial hint of baby powder, there is a rich earthiness that I really enjoy.  It's hard to put the scent into words, but truly powerful smells often trigger sense memories and that is exactly what I experienced here.  It instantly and powerfully took me back to an Alaskan cruise I took nearly a decade ago, specifically the cool, woodsy scent I recall from the deck as we navigated a narrow channel surrounded by trees and water.  It may seem strange to recall a specific memory like that, but that is what instantly came to mind when I tried this out.  What a wonderful scent to rekindle that very pleasant memory from my past.  If you enjoy smelling things like a forest in the afternoon, fresh rainfall, and cool mist, this would be a scent you would likely enjoy.

Citadelle comes double boxed, and the tall thin bottle is beautifully simple and fragile.  I will treasure this one-fluid-ounce bottle and use it on special occasions.  It is listed as unisex, and I suppose that is true.  The initial light powdery scent, however, may strike some as effeminate though the more powerful and lingering woodsy/smoky scent lingers and it does have some masculinity to it.  Overall, I am thrilled with this and would easily recommend for those willing to make a special purchase for quality and - hopefully - some pleasant scent memories.

product_title: Raw Spirit Luxury Eau de Parfum (Citadelle Luxury, 1.0 fl oz)
review_text:
What a pleasant surprise...having had no idea whether this scent would work for me. I took a chance, and am so glad I did. This is the sort of scent I adore....with green & woodsy notes, rather than a face full of florals! I feel as if I'm in a forest after a light rain. Heaven!

The top note is certainly a bit fruity, sweet, and powdery. I also get grassy undertones. There's a distinct "greenness" that opens up this fragrance. It then settles into a smoky, spicy scent where the nutmeg is detectable as the sweetness fades. Citadelle then settles into it's primary basenote, a heady VETIVER dry down. That's where this fragrance really shines. The vetiver base lasts and lasts. Silage (longevity) for me is about 4 hours, which is very good for me....I find that most perfume doesn't last a long time on me unless it's cloying. But if you're looking for a scent that lasts all day, this isn't it. It's a LIGHT fragrance, very wearable for work, not heavy and does not "project".

One of my all time favorite perfumes is Sycomore by Chanel. It's very expensive, a scent I've saved only for special occasions. Citadelle reminds me of a lighter version of Sycomore, in many ways more wearable because it has less of a dark/heavy feeling about it. This is a scent that can be worn year round, rather than just saving it for Fall/Winter months. If you love Vetiver & tree/green smelling perfumes, you'll enjoy Citadelle. It's certainly more affordable than Chanel, or Encre Noir by Lalique and the lightness of it will win over those who feel that those scents are a bit too heavy and overbearing.

Unisex? Yes! My husband likes this scent very much. This fragrance is in no way too girly. No floral notes anywhere! But he'll have to get his own bottle....this one is MINE and I'm not giving it up. My new favorite is now Citadelle by Raw Spirit and I plan on wearing it often. Highly recommended for Vetiver lovers, you won't be disappointed. 5 stars.

review_text: I love the box, it has a sleeve that is sparkly greyish silver with gold writing and a gold symbol on it, then in a heavy white cardboard box with just the gold symbol  on it. product_title: Raw Spirit Eau de Parfum, Bijou Vert, 1 fl. oz.
review_title: Try it before you buy it, not for everyone
review_text:
First, I can definitely see why they list this perfume as a unisex version. Although I feel it leans masculine, it would be an appropriate scent and gift for both men and women. It comes nicely boxed in a 7" box that shimmers, a gold chandelier-like ink blot shape embossed in gold above the block text, "RAW SPIRIT", and the scent name "bijou - vert." It's attractively boxed.

The bottle inside is a simple one, about 4" tall and very square with a black cap and same ink blot style label. It is 1 fluid ounce filled with a complex fragrance. It is a musky, green, earthy scent. It's definitely bright! Not much floral there, no fruit except for a hint of grapefruit in those layers. It's spicy and woodsy. That said, I read another reviewer say it reminds them of a 70s Avon fragrance. OUCH! That's a low blow to Raw Spirit...if only there weren't some truth to it!

Yes, I have to agree, there is something a bit Avon grandma about this fragrance. There is even an aspect of it that reminds me of my Tinkerbell perfume from when I was a child in the 80s & 90s! So I already wasn't too big of a fan before I read that, although I definitely appreciate the craftsmanship of this fragrance. I can also see why it would REALLY appeal to a lot of people. I'm not a scent snob, just because I don't like it doesn't mean YOU won't. It's a pleasant enough scent, the longevity is decent, and complex enough to make it interesting. But it's not for me. Due to it's PRICE (!) too, I would definitely recommend testing this one out in person before purchasing.

If it helps the reader, my typical favorite scents in perfumes are: jasmine, vanilla, tobacco, musks, nutty scents, anise, and cedarwood.

product_title: Raw Spirit Eau de Parfum, Bijou Vert, 1 fl. oz.
review_text:
This scent starts out sharp and green -- vetiver is a major component -- but then warms to a spicy, peppery scent with undertones of exotic woods.  It's a pretty scent, but not a flowery one, both fresh and sophisticated.

The bottle is attractive and it comes in a really beautiful presentation box, so it will make a nice gift.

It's also a plus for me that part of the profit is devoted to supporting sustainable agriculture in Haiti, so you can feel positive about your choice whether it's a romantic present or an indulgence for yourself.

product_title: Raw Spirit Eau de Parfum, Bijou Vert, 1 fl. oz.
review_title: Raw Spirit Perfume - yes, it's one a man can share
review_text:
If this Raw Spirit fragrance bears any resemblance to the island of Haiti (as suggested in the product description) I should visit soon  I love it. And as has been stated famously about one particular product Raw Spirit may not be easy to describe but youll surely love it when you smell it.

About an hour before the start of the Super Bowl last evening I showered and stepped out for a quick trip to the supermarket (less than two blocks away) to pick up some of the usual stuff that go with watching the game. It was quite filled with shoppers. I sprayed on Raw and hoped someone would notice. Sure enough a couple was tempted to start a conversation that became an exuberant description of my smell. The lady guessed its a French product; her man said German.

I ordered Raw Spirit for my lady but I am going to keep it for myself. Its unisex after all.

product_title: Raw Spirit Eau de Parfum, Bijou Vert, 1 fl. oz.
review_text:
I love this.  So does my wife. Truly. 1.0 fl oz (30 ml) in an attractive heavy square glass bottle with a spray head.  Marketed as "unisex" and I easily agree.  Nicely presented in a 2 layer box with outer sleeve.  Now, the scent . . .

My very,very first impression was that it reminded me of the Asian after shaves my dad wore . . . Jade East, or Hai Karate (young people will not know those once popular names).  After settling in the scent mellowed and deepened.  Certainly a presence of citrus (contains grapefruit essence), but underlying fragrances of spices (contains black pepper) and woods (contains cedar wood and patchouli).  I put a little on my wrist, which I keep checking as I type this.  Just heavenly!  And the scent is not wearing off, implying use of high quality base oils.  This "Raw Spirit Bijou Vert (green jewel)" will join my short list of favorite perfume/colognes.

I already mentioned, "unisex".  Yes, that applies here.  I asked my wife to describe it - she replied, "Definitely not flowery, maybe some citrus".  I think I did well in my description above.  As a man, I'd be pleased to wear this on dressy occasions.  I may not get the chance, as my wife seems to have taken it over -- she just loves it.

A perfume/cologne is of course a matter of preference, but I would expect few disappointments here.

product_title: John Varvatos Artisan Acqua Eau de Toilette Spray, 1.3 fl. Oz. mens cologne
review_text:
Courtesy of the Amazon Vine program, I have received John Varvatos Acqua Eau de Toilette Spray, 1.3 fl. oz. review. I own a reasonable-sized collection (~ 30 bottles kept) and I own/have smelled numerous samples, including John Varvatos Artisan (my favorite of the house) and Vintage (a close second) and so I am a bit familiar with the image marketed by this house.

Despite the title quoted by Amazon, this is a flanker to Artisan and should be called Artisan Acqua. You can confirm that on John Varvatos' own website. The two, while similar, are definitely in different groups. Artisan Acqua is Aromatic Spicy, and Artisan itself is Citrus Aromatic. Essentially, think of the Artisan Acqua as that old style smell you expect when you leave a barber's shop, whereas Artisan smells like a bar of a high-end soap with some jasmine in it.

I am not going to repeat the top, middle, base notes since these are all for marketing only and does not really tell the reader much and anyone who is interested in this level of detail probably has an account on fragrantica or basenote already. :) For the newer folks, I would say that this really is the barber's shop smell; I mean that mildly-spicy soap that they use during and after shaving that gives you a small feeling of un-clean. Yes, it is that "we added smell to cover another smell". For my skin chemistry, it mixes very well and two sprays on the neck last 6 hours until I can no longer smell it. However, by hour 3 it is already a very faint skin smell. Silage is poor, which in my opinion is actually a good thing for this type of smell: I am not big into scent trail, and definitely not big in advertising a barber's shop smell behind my back. (The jasmine in Artisan is worth spreading though if only it is strong enough to leave a scent trail.)

Overall, I would say that this is worth sampling but not a buy for me. This is an authentic barber's shop smell, but I like something more interesting. For a starter, try Molinard Homme II for a cleaner, more floral but still very barber's shop smell.

As for the rating, I feel that the authenticity is worth upvoting. The ingredients seems decent and I and my colleagues have no major allergy after using it (unlike many recent tonka bean mess release). The price is on the high side for a 1.3oz, at least the one listed here at Amazon. :)

Cheers!

Quite unique looking and pretty cool.  I'd suggest just a light spray as it is initially a pretty strong aroma, at least compared to others I've tried.  However, it tones down quickly to a nice manly smell.  The ladies in my life seem to like it and so do I.  I'd certainly consider this again among my favorite colognes.

I say this because I really love the scent itself and would be quite enamored with it in a stronger version.  As expected the longevity of the scent was commensurate with it's lightness as it did not last me an entire day and was, in fact, hard to determine.  If this scent could keep  it's fragrance profile, only ramped up in strength,  it would be a knock-out fragrance.  Even in it's present state of lightness it's far more complex than the old 4711 German aftershave which may have it's place even if it's somewhat less refined.  Acqua, as far as scent is concerned, is much better.

review_title: Something you save for special nights
review_text:
How do you review a scent? This is such a subjective thing, but my wife likes it and that's what's important. On first spray I thought it was too strong but it faded into a very pretty perfume. It doesn't smell new and chic, it smells elegant and refined. To me the smell is at contrast with the packaging. The zebra print and bright red makes me think it will have sharp, maybe citrus smells, but instead the smells are floral, fruity, with a soft edge. And I feel that's so subjective that I don't want to knock it for that opinion. I think it's fancy, sensual, feminine--more exotic than exciting.

I do think the packaging is really nice and perfect for gifting. The black and white "zebra stripes" on the outside of the box are embosses. Then when you open it there is a cherry red cardboard that envelopes the perfume bottle. The bottle and the lid are both glass. The zebra print is right on the glass as well as the Josie Natori logo. The button pump is a little darker--maybe a metallic ruby red? Even thought the pump button has a metallic look, it feels like plastic. The bottom of the bottle says "MADE IN U.S.A." which is a always nice to see. The perfume bottle has a nice heft to it.

Overall the wife likes it, and I think it smells good on her. I don't think she'll be wearing it daily but rather save it for a special time where she dresses up.

product_title: Josie By Josie Natori Eau de Parfum
review_title: Fragrance is a very personal thing
review_text:
Since fragrance preference is subjective and highly personal, it's a difficult product to review. Based on the description that mentions citrus and floral notes, I was excited about trying Josie by Josie Natori. I tend toward light fragrances - mostly one-note florals. While I enjoy musk tones on others, I don't care for them in my own fragrance choices.

I find Josie to be too heavy, musky and cloying. It smells "old lady" sweet to me and even though I may be an old lady, I don't want to smell like one. ;-) It does become less cloying after an hour or so and it isn't what I would call unpleasant. It's just too much for my taste.

However, to illustrate how highly personal fragrance preferences are, my daughter and one son adore this scent! Both of them have raved about how fabulous I smell when wearing this. Go figure.

I would say that if you enjoy long-lasting scents that are complex, musky and have sweet floral and citrus notes, you may love Josie. If you prefer lighter, one-note scents that aren't musky, this probably isn't the scent for you. But you never know - try some at a fragrance counter!

As a side note, the bottle is interesting and unique with a vaguely Asian feel in black, white and red. It's beautifully boxed and makes a statement on your dressing table.

review_title: Reveal. Not your typical Calvin Klein.
review_text:
The top notes of this fragrance come on strong with Tonka Bean, Anise, Melon and Agave (which given the boozy undertone comes off like aged tequila) at the start. There are also hints of woodsy (from vettiver), herbal (from clary sage) and aquatic, slightly salty base notes that shine through more on the dry-down. The overwhelming presence is a little syrupy sweet but the woodsy, herbal and aquatic elements help to balance this somewhat.  Uncharacteristic of most of the Calvin Klein scents I've tried, it projects well on my skin for up to 6-8 hours and I can still pick it up distinctly on clothing sprayed the previous day, even in warmer weather.  Apart from the sweetness, I can't find much I don't like about Reveal.  It's a safe choice for most situations or times of the year and I feel like it definitely has some mass appeal, especially with women.  Definitely safe for a blind buy if you're wondering.

If you like this cologne, here are some others that you might also like.

product_title: Juicy Couture I Am Juicy Couture, 1.7 fl. Oz., perfume for women
review_title: I am Juicy Couture is a Sweet, Feminine Eau de Parfum Spray Inside an Elegant Bottle; it is Suitable for a Queens Boudoir!
review_text:
Recently, my parents came to visit me.  It was Moms birthday and I gave her a 0.60 pound bottle of I am Juicy Couture Eau de Parfum Spray from Juicy Couture.  She prefers eau de toilette over perfume and eau de parfum.  There is a difference.  Perfume has the highest concentration of perfume essences, eau de parfum has the second, and eau de toilette has the third.  Perfume is longer lasting.  However, women choose according to the fragrances interaction to their skin and the climate in which they live.  Normally, Mom purchases Chloe Eau de Toilette Spray for herself.  She has delicate skin that is sensitive to high concentrations of perfume essences.

  The I am Juicy Couture came well packaged in an attractive cardboard box that was easy to open.  We saved the box in order to protect the bottle when Mom traveled back home.  It was easy to put the bottle back inside the box and reseal it.  The bottle is extremely gorgeous and elegant.  It would look great sitting on any womans vanity.  Most importantly, its scent is very flowery and feminine.  It lasted surprisingly long for an eau de parfum.  Mom sprayed some on her neck when we went shopping at Greenbrier Mall on a Sunday afternoon.  About four hours later, when we returned to my condo, I could still detect it.  For fun, when we were meandering through Sears, I sprayed some designer fragrances on my wrists.  They had vanished by the time I returned home.

  Mom was very pleased with her gift of I am Juicy Couture Eau de Parfum Spray from Juicy Couture.  It does smell sweet and flowery and juicylike a piece of juicy fruit, such as an overripe peach basking beneath the Georgia sun.  Before leaving to go home to Tennessee, Mom laughed and said to me, You write in your review that I went to the mall and the old men threw down their canes and threw aside their walkers and went after me when they smelled that Juicy Couture.  Well that didn't happen.  However, Mom has been wearing this eau de parfum for nearly two weeks now and her delicate skin hasn't experienced any adverse side effectsno hives, no rashes and no itching.  I highly recommend the I am Juicy Couture Eau de Parfum Spray from Juicy Couture.  It would make a wonderful present on any occasion.

review_title: Impressive alteration of traditional rose.  More fun that only flowers.  Greets softly (like a rose should) without lingering
review_text:
This Lacoste perfume has a fun light floral scent that carries well but does not linger.  The description is "Wild rose and raspberry enveloped in a detectable coconut".  The rose is the strongest aspect of this fragrance, amounting to maybe 70-80% of the aroma.  The raspberry does not stand alone or overshadow the rose, instead it mildly alters a solitary rose fragrance.  Don't expect to smell flowers and fruit, instead experience a more playful rose.  The cocount is very, very light - not anywhere near your sun tan lotion strength.  I apply organic coconut oil to my skin as a moisturizer and the smell of the oil (which is already very light and not at all at perfume levels) is greater than the coconut in this perfume.  Rest assured you won't smell like Coppertone or Hawaiian Tropic sunblock.

I dislike strong perfumes and colognes that are so bold that they linger long after someone has left the area.  To me a scent should stay on the person and offer a gentle greeting to those in conversation or standing side by side.  The power of this perfume is just that.

product_title: Lacoste L.12.12 Pour Elle Natural Eau de Toilette Spray
review_text:
I glanced at a few reviews before starting my own because I was curious what others thought. Perception of scent is really up to the individual and of course how that scent interacts with your own body chemistry. I was expecting a more fruity fragrance, but it didn't seem that way on my skin. For me, this was a heavy almost cloying smell and unlike a few other reviewers, I did not have any issues with the scent fading.

I am rating it 4 stars because I get compliments wearing it and my husband likes how it smells :)

product_title: Lacoste L.12.12 Pour Elle Natural Eau de Toilette Spray
review_text: This Lacoste perfume has a fun, floral youthful scent. I liked how sweet and fresh it smells when you first apply it. However, in order to make the scent last longer, you have to be strategic in your application. I sprayed onto my pressure points and did not rub the pressure points like my wrists together. I also used unscented lotion and sprayed onto myself after putting on the lotion. In all, I felt like this scent was inoffensive. I also brought it into work and because I work with mainly women, my coworkers asked to have a few spritzes of the perfume. So, for me this was a great smell to wear, but results may vary especially as scents are very individual and depend upon your body chemistry.

product_title: Lacoste L.12.12 Pour Elle Natural Eau de Toilette Spray
review_text: I really like this perfume. It is feminine without being overly floral. My husband said it smelled almost unisex to him. If you ever smelled Escada's Magnatisim before it was discontinued,  it is a lighter version of that. While it lasts, it has a hint of fruit and vanillaish(made up word) musk scent. It is so light that it evaporates to nothing within an hour or two. I still love the smell, but I wish it would last longer.

product_title: Lacoste L.12.12 Pour Elle Natural Eau de Toilette Spray
review_title: Nice light scent for daily wear
review_text:
I love to discover new scents, hence why I hound Ross's and TJ Maxx for their discounted perfumes. I had never tried Lacoste before, so I took the plunge, even though it said it had "coconut" and if there is one scent I've grown to hate, it's coconut.

But seriously, this perfume is a fantastic "day to day" perfume! It's light and subtle, a perfect balance between sweet and floral. I don't smell coconut at all, which is absolutely perfect!

This is definitely not a super strong perfume, but really, that's good because those strong perfumes tend to get rather noxious (and make me nauseous) over time.

I really like the packaging - very efficient with little waste. Same with the bottle - while I do love my decorative bottles, I appreciate streamlined ones that fit into cabinets better.

Overall, I do like the scent; I find it very light and refreshing, more floral though than coconut. If that sounds like something you want, head to your perfume counter and check it out!

*C.S. Light*

review_title: Could have been better, maybe for a younger audience
review_text: I love perfume.  I'm the type of girl that buys sample sets and wears a different one everyday.  I don't usually get full sized bottles until I absolutely love them, but when this popped up on Vine, I jumped at the chance.  Now I'm a little disappointed.  This is something that I would maybe wear every once in awhile, but it'll take me years to go through the entire bottle.  I honestly have been thinking about giving it to one of my teenager students because I think they would enjoy it more.  I usually love the mix of flower and fruit.  I like sweet scents and have been currently obsessed with Prada's Candy for exactly that reason.  This is much lighter than almost anything I have word lately and has now lasting power.  By mid-morning, I couldn't smell it at all anymore and no one commented upon it.  I usually get a few students that ask me what scent I was wearing that day, but it was like this disappeared.  I couldn't smell the coconut at all and the rose was more of a generic floral scent than a clear rose.  I guess this is to keep it from going too far into the very specific rose water smell that a lot of rose perfumes go towards.  Regardless, it leaves this without a distinction and without any lasting impact.

review_title: Nice Update to on old Favorite
review_text:
Eternity Now for Men is a modern rendition to an old favorite of mine.  The manufacturer describes it as "exhilarating. fresh. masculine. spicy ginger creates an exhilarating first impression, balanced by a pulsating heart of crisp starfruit and a bold signature of moroccan cedarwood."

Being a unsophisticated person that I am, I can't sense any of the subtleties described above.  I think of cologne in terms of how it makes me feel/smell when I wear it, and also how those around me react when I wear it.  To me, this scent doesn't smell very masculine, but instead smells very vanilla-ee and powdery.  I like how I smell and feel when I wear it, and both my wife and daughter like the smell.  It isn't overpowering, which is good because I like a cologne to be for myself and for someone close to me...not the entire room.

I have added this scent to my arsenal, and will continue to alternate it in every few days.  If you liked the old CK Eternity for Men, no guarantee that you'll like this one.  If you just like CK products and you want to give this one a go, there is a good chance you'll like it.  There is nothing offensive about it, and it is a nice modern fresh scent.

product_title: Calvin Klein Eternity Now Eau de Toilette Spray for Men, 1 fl. oz.
review_text:
I ordered this for my husband to try because he likes wearing different men's colognes and aftershave fragrances. He said he likes this scent, which is crisp and fresh, smelling of tropical fruits, maybe some lemon, wood scents and patchouli. But he thinks it's a little overwhelming unless he uses just a tiny amount. It does have a staying power. I could still smell it in the evening after he applied it in the morning. I think he may have just sprayed on too much the first time. I think it smells nice and has a definite masculine fragrance.

The packaging and bottle are simple and attractive. It's the kind of fragrance that would be nice to give as a gift. It's a little pricey but I believe 1 ounce of this will truly go a long way, even if it turns out to be a favorite that is worn often.

product_title: Calvin Klein Eternity Now Eau de Toilette Spray for Men, 1 fl. oz.
review_title: An Excellent Refresh, Update of a Classic Scent for Men
review_text:
I have used Calvin Klein Eternity for some years. I have found the scent to be compelling, with a very fresh, clean aspect.

Eternity Now for Men is an update, refreshing the product line, initially introduced in 1989. Calvin Klein notes that Eternity Now is "an oriental fougre with ginger, coconut water, star anise, starfruit, cedar, patchouli, tonka bean and vanilla."

The result is excellent. It has an even fresher, cleaner aspect than before. I see that some Amazon reviewers are not happy with the update. So there may be some disagreement among those of us who've long liked the Eternity line.

Will you like it? Fragrances are a very personal thing. Eternity Now is high-quality and priced accordingly. I would suggest trying it at a department store and seeing for yourself.

review_title: Sweet floral with honey-amber base, for night time or winter.
review_text:
Illicit embodies the daring spirit of a woman who is hypnotic, attractive and living life to the fullest, according to the advertising for this perfume. So naturally I was drawn to it.  I classify this as a Winter fragrance, and for the night time.

It's called a modern floral, created by the perfumer Anne Flipo. It starts with spicy notes of ginger and bitter orange, leading to the floral heart of rose and jasmine sambac and the warm, honey-amber base. The dry down is definitely more amber and sandalwood. I like the feeling it gives me, I think it's for a woman in control. The bottle I got (3.3 oz) says "Made in France". I was very pleased as it's rare to get a perfume that's made in France anymore. If you have a warm body chemistry like me, this perfume opens up beautifully and smells gorgeous. It could be too overpowering for some, a little goes a long way, applied to the pulse points. On me the sillage is light and it lasts a few hours.

I kind of like it as it's a longer lasting perfume that does not give me a headache. However, it's not very complex as the dry down is more amber and sandalwood and that's the fragrance that stays on me after the first few minutes. People have compared it to YSL's Black Opium or Giorgio Armani Si but I haven't tried those.  Overall I am giving it 3.5 stars rounded up to 4.

review_title: exactly what I'm looking for in a fragrance
review_text:
I got this as part of a gift set and it is my favorite of the included three fragrances -- definitely my kind of perfume!

I would call this an "evening" fragrance -- it is exotic, a bit woody, and Oriental in character -- although I wear it during the day because that is just my preference.  It lasts about half a work day without needing to be reapplied; this is about average for a fragrance, for me.

This is supposed to open with woody notes and I definitely feel like I smell sandalwood and/or something similar here.  It lasts, though it also transforms a bit -- I suppose this is the "hints of incense" coming through as the top notes wear off.  I'm not really getting the pepper that is supposed to be here, but if it is well-integrated into the blend, I suppose it could be responsible for a little bit of the overall spiciness.  I'm also just not getting the grassy herb scents with this -- guess that could be my body chemistry, though.  (Due to differences in body chemistry, this may not smell the same on everyone.)

Overall, the sandalwood (?) and incense are standing out for me, and that is why I like this one so much.

Please note that large fragrances are flammable and cannot be sent by air, so this may take a little while to arrive and is not returnable.

product_title: Rochas Eau de Toilette, Citrus Chypre Woody, 3.3 fl. oz.
review_title: Intensely citrus, complex, summery and delightful!
review_text:
My last bout with perfume was with my fabulous secretarys addiction to Giorgio of Beverly Hills. She loved it. It made me violently ill. Because she was so awesome, I forced myself to live with the scent. It wasn't the smell that bothered me, but some substance in it that gave me massive headaches. That was in the 1980s and I have avoided fragrances ever since. But what a sad deficit in my life! After all, smell is one of the five primary senses. So, while I hesitated to select this item, a thorough search across the internet convinced me I could safely give it a try. How happy I am that I took the risk.

This Eau de Rochas is a thoroughly delightful fragrance. It is feminine verging toward unisex, light, intensely citrus, initially cool transforming to warm, with complex herbal qualities. There are touches of honeysuckle, jasmine, and coriander as the fragrance develops. The process of change from a bright, lemony garden through to a summery, fern-filled forest is seamless, but profound. There are ephemeral qualities to this eau that are rare, fleeting, and haunting. Upon initial application, there is a delicate minerality, a sense of cool water over dark rocks in a bubbling spring. Classic chypre notes including patchouli and woods are present, but never overwhelming.

This is Eau de Rochas, one of the most intriguing, complex, yet unassuming fragrances I have ever experienced. Of course, it is not for everyone, but it is for me and that is unusual indeed. If, however, you dislike citrus, you will want to avoid it. Some reviewers found it to be more like lemon scented cleaning spray than a fragrance they would wear. But it seems to me that criticism entirely misses its complexity. Still, fragrance is very personal and no one can tell any of us what we like or don't. Personally, I love it!

product_title: Rochas Eau de Toilette, Citrus Chypre Woody, 3.3 fl. oz.
review_text:
This EDT opens with a burst of fresh citrus - lemon, lime, bergamot, grapefruit & hint of mandarin orange with underlying herbal notes of verbena, basil & patchouli & a slight bitterness.  Once the citrus settles down there are some spicy carnation & woody notes & a hint of sandalwood & very light floral (jasmine).

This is a classic citrus fragrance that women & men can wear.  It is uplifting, just-out-of the-shower, clean & fresh.  There are no cloying notes & it smells "natural".  It doesn't have the usual men's citrus cologne notes of lavender & cedar.  I like this kind of fragrance on a hot/humid day.

For a citrus EDT, this has very good sillage & lasting power.  With one generous spritz, it goes to arm length & lasts about 5 hours on my skin becoming an up-close, clean herbal with light citrus.  It lasts even longer on clothing than on my skin.  Citrus fragrance is inherently short-lived on skin but this one is better than most.  Don't overspray thinking it will last longer - just plan to reapply later in the day if it fades too much.

A well-made classic citrus.

product_title: Juicy Couture Viva la juicy rose Eau de parfum spray, 3.4 Ounce
review_text:
Top Notes: Italian Mandarin, Jasmine Petal, William Pear
Middle Notes: Rose Centifolia, Jasmine Sambac, White Peony
Bottom Notes: Orris Absolute, Ambozan, Benzoin

Now let me start by saying that I am not a fan of floral perfumes. Not one bit. But I like Viva la Juicy Rose, to a point. There is enough mixture of fruity notes to offset the heavy floral presence.

The downside of this perfume is it has zero staying power. I can no longer smell the perfume two hours after application, which is unfortunate since I could wear the dry down all day and be very happy. Viva la Juicy Rose starts out fruity and sweet, then goes into a heavy, yet beautiful floral presence before moving to the simplicity of a powdery floral as it fades away.

While this perfume doesnt last it owns whoever wears it for its short life. Viva la Juicy Rose walks into the room 10 minutes before you do and takes command.

I would caution those who are sensitive to scents, be careful with this perfume. Those middle notes are strong and present and while I like this perfume it did cause a pretty bad headache on me. Even as a migraine sufferer that is rare since scents aren't one of my triggers. All Im saying is drive this beauty with care.

product_title: Burberry Mr Burberry Eau De Toilette
review_title: Sophisticated scent but not long lasting.
review_text: This is an overall pleasantly scented woody-herbal fougere fragrance.  The top notes are grapefruit, cardamon, and tarragon.  The citrusy grapefruit tang is the sharpest note here on first impact.  The dry down leads to a nice blend of nutmeg and cedar, with base notes of sandalwood and vetiver.  Other influences are birch leaf and guaiac wood, but not really in sufficient amounts override the other notes.  The scent is a sophisticated one, that has its moments.  The primary drawback with this scent is that it is not very long lasting, no more than half a workday perhaps before dissolution.  The projection is also fairly limited but that is to be expected with the overall style and chicness of the scent itself.
